sections.heading: Four weeks, one term and one exam cycle: what to measure in Mumbai
paragraphs: In the first four weeks measure behaviour, not marks. Does the child underline the command word before writing? Can they say out loud what a question wants? Have they stopped copying definitions into a notebook as a form of studying? Is there one piece of written work that was planned before it was written? Those are observable at the dining table and they are the leading indicators. Four weeks of home classes change what a child does with a question, not yet what a school writes on it. Marks at four weeks tell you about the previous system, not the new one, and a tutor who shows you a mark jump in month one is probably teaching to a test they set themselves.

By the end of a term, three things should be visible. School feedback changes register, from comments about content to comments about depth of analysis, which parents often read as deterioration. Deadlines stop being emergencies. And the student begins to use the vocabulary of the new system unprompted, talking about criteria and research questions rather than about chapters. A dip in scores somewhere in that term is normal and expected, because the behaviour that used to earn marks has been switched off before the replacement is fluent.

Over one full cycle of internal assessments and school examinations, predicted grades settle and the subject grid shows whether it was chosen well. The honest limit is worth stating: if a child has moved boards against their own wishes, is in a year group that repeats a year, and dislikes two of their Higher Level subjects, no tuition arrangement will fix that. The right move is a conversation with the IB coordinator while changes are still possible. We do not guarantee grades, and we will tell a family when the problem is upstream of anything a tutor can reach.

When a match is not working, the signs are usually a student who is polite and silent, homework that appears finished without being understood, or sessions that overrun because nothing was prioritised. Raise it in week three or four. Describe the specific problem, we shortlist again, and the replacement tutor receives the diagnostic note and the marked work so the first session is not repeated from scratch.

sections.heading: Booking the first CBSE to IB transition session in Mumbai
paragraphs: Gather four items before you call. The last two marked CBSE answer sheets. The school's admission letter or portal page showing the programme year and subjects. The term calendar if the school has issued one. And a realistic list of two weekday windows plus one weekend window, allowing for your own corridor rather than an optimistic one. Families across Mumbai, Maharashtra waste the first fortnight on a slot that looked workable and failed twice, and rescheduling a tutor twice in a month is how arrangements quietly end.

Check the gate rule where you live before the first visit. Societies in Chembur, Kharghar and off Ghodbunder Road vary: some want the resident to authorise each visit through an app, some register a regular visitor once, and a few close visitor entry at a fixed hour regardless. A tutor who is turned away once will rearrange; turned away twice, they will ask to move you online, and they will be right to.

The first session is a diagnosis and it should feel slightly uncomfortable. Your child writes one answer with no help on a topic they have already studied, the tutor marks it against the criteria the new school will actually use, and they go through the gap line by line. Then they take a second question and plan it together without writing it. Afterwards you receive a short written note splitting content gaps from skill gaps with a rough time estimate for each, which is also the document you use in week four to check whether anything is happening.

If that note says the right next step is an admission conversation or a year-group decision rather than weekly tuition, it will say that instead. An IB private tutor in Mumbai who only ever recommends more hours is not giving you information.
bullets: Bring marked CBSE sheets, the admission letter and the term calendar
Give two weekday windows and one weekend window, honestly

faqs.question: How long does a CBSE to IB transition realistically take?
faqs.answer: Allow one full term for the skill changes and two to three weeks for each specific content gap. The content work is predictable: a topic CBSE sequences later, statistics taught lightly, a conventions difference in a science subject. The skill work is slower because it means unlearning a scoring habit built over several years, and it typically looks worse before it looks better. Students who moved in the spring, used the gap before the IB year started for content, and then worked weekly on written answers through the first term are usually comfortable by the second. Those who start in the festive season are doing the same work with deadlines on top.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to our building in Kharghar for an evening slot on a weekday?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the tutor is matched from Navi Mumbai rather than from across the creek. Kharghar, Belapur, Nerul, Vashi and Panvel are each a short, predictable drive from one another along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, so a seven o'clock home tutoring start holds through the week. The arrangement that breaks is a tutor coming from Chembur or Bandra at that hour, even with the Atal Setu and the Eastern Freeway, because one bad evening on the highway ends the slot. If the only specialist in your subject is on the island, we will suggest weekend sessions at home plus a weekly online check instead.

faqs.question: Does someone need to be at home during the session, and what should the study space look like?
faqs.answer: An adult should be in the flat, though not in the room after the first fortnight. The space matters more than the supervision: a table and two chairs, the door closed, the phone in another room, and no television within earshot. For home tuition on a transition specifically, keep the old CBSE notebooks and the new school's handouts in the same place, because almost every session refers to both. Families who set this up in week one lose far less time than those who move the session between a bedroom, the dining table and a sofa depending on who else is home.

faqs.question: My child is in CBSE Class 11. Will they lose a year by moving to the IB?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and it is better to decide that with open eyes. The Diploma Programme is a two-year course assessed at the end, so a student who has already done a year of Class 11 ordinarily joins DP1 rather than DP2. Some families accept the extra year because the destination suits the child; others complete Class 12 on their existing board instead. Put the question to the IB coordinator at the school you are applying to, and weigh the child's own appetite for two further years of school. No tutor should be making this call for you, and a tuition plan is not a reason to make it.

faqs.question: Is CBSE Maths good enough preparation for Higher Level Mathematics?
faqs.answer: The content preparation is often better than average, and the presentation preparation is usually weaker. CBSE students arrive fluent in algebraic manipulation and trigonometry, which is exactly what Higher Level work consumes. What they have not practised is showing a calculator-supported method, writing a justification for a step, interpreting a statistical result in a sentence, and producing the exploration, a piece of personal mathematical writing on a question they chose. Ask the school which mathematics route they recommend for your child and read the current subject guide rather than relying on a comparison of old syllabus documents.

faqs.question: What happens with Hindi, Sanskrit or Marathi when a CBSE student moves to the IB?
faqs.answer: Language placement is a school decision and it can work in your favour. A CBSE student with genuinely strong Hindi may be placed in a Hindi A course, which is a more comfortable route through the language requirement than starting a new language from the beginning. Sanskrit generally does not continue, and Marathi availability varies by school. What matters is raising it during admission rather than after, because class sizes and teacher availability decide what a school can actually offer in a given year. Ask the admissions office which language courses are running for your child's cohort, not which ones appear in the brochure.

faqs.question: Why does my child score less in the IB despite studying more than before?
faqs.answer: Because the thing being measured changed and the effort went into the old target. CBSE marking rewards complete, accurate coverage of taught content; IB criteria reward a developed argument, selected evidence and evaluation. A student who studies harder in the old style produces longer, tidier answers that still sit in a middle band, and the extra hours make the frustration worse rather than better. This is the clearest signal that the problem is skill rather than content, and the fix is marking practice with the actual descriptors in front of the student, not more revision.

faqs.question: Do we need separate tutors for each IB subject?
faqs.answer: For the Diploma Programme, usually two or three at most, chosen for the subjects where the transition actually hurts. One tutor across six subjects spreads too thin to be useful at Higher Level, and most families find that mathematics plus one science or one essay subject covers the real need. For the Middle Years Programme a single strong tutor can often work across subjects, because the shared problem is criterion-based writing rather than subject depth. Start with a diagnosis of all six and then buy hours in the two that the diagnosis names, rather than booking everything in month one.

faqs.question: How do IB tuition fees in Mumbai work for a transition, and why will you not quote a figure?
faqs.answer: Fees vary with programme year, level, subject scarcity, travel and session length, and a number published on a web page goes stale and then misleads. A both-boards specialist in a subject with few teachers in the city costs more than a widely taught one. Higher Level preparation takes longer than Standard Level. A tutor crossing a bad evening corridor prices that in, and online removes it. Diagnostic blocks and term bookings are priced differently. Tell us the subject, the level, your area and your windows, and you will get a specific answer rather than a range designed to be meaningless.

faqs.question: Our child was admitted mid-year. Is it too late to catch up?
faqs.answer: Not too late, but the order of work changes. A mid-year entrant has deadlines immediately, so the first priority is the next assessable piece rather than a general audit, and the command-word retraining happens through that piece instead of alongside it. Expect the first month to feel like triage and the second to look more like teaching. Ask the school which internal assessments have already been set, get the briefs, and give them to the tutor before the first session. Families who try to start from the beginning of the syllabus in a mid-year entry lose the term.

faqs.question: Can online tuition cover the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: Yes, better than most subject work. The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge are mostly reading, structuring and redrafting, all of which happen well on a shared document where a supervisor can comment in the margin and the student can see every change. What online cannot do is make a student start, so the schedule needs fixed weekly checkpoints with something written for each. For a student who stalls on blank pages, the first two planning sessions are better in person, then the redrafting moves online. Your school supervises these components formally, and a tutor works around that rather than replacing it.

sections.heading: Matching a CBSE to IGCSE transition tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: Three pieces of information shape the whole arrangement, and families usually send none of them. Which year group the school has actually placed the child in, because Class 8 to Year 9 is a clean entry and Class 9 to Year 10 is a different job altogether. Which subjects the child has chosen or been allocated, since Cambridge schools let students drop and add in ways CBSE never did. And whether the school has entered the child at Core or Extended tier in mathematics and the sciences, which decides what the ceiling is.

Then the sequence: 1. You send the year group, the subject allocation and the last CBSE report card. 2. We shortlist tutors who have taught the chosen subjects on the Cambridge syllabus and also know what a CBSE Class 8 or 9 student arrives knowing. 3. You speak to the shortlist and ask each one what they would do about the tier decision. 4. The tutor runs a baseline session at home, using past-paper questions rather than a quiz they wrote themselves.

That baseline session is the part worth paying for twice. A CBSE student taking a Cambridge past paper cold produces a very characteristic script: the mathematics is correct and the method is unmarked, the science content is present and the application question is blank, the English is grammatically clean and the response to the task is partial. Those three patterns tell a tutor where to start far better than a report card showing good marks in everything.

We will tell you when the shortlist is thin. Tutors who can handle all IB and IGCSE subjects at IGCSE Years 9-11 with a tutor in Mumbai covering both the sciences and the humanities are rarer than tutors who know one subject well, and for a transition year the breadth sometimes matters more than the depth. If the right person is in Chandivali and you are in Borivali, you will hear it before you hear the name.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: which tier has the school actually entered your child for?
paragraphs: Several Cambridge IGCSE subjects are offered at two tiers, and a student entered at the lower tier cannot access the higher grades however well they perform. CBSE has no equivalent of this, so parents arrive with no instinct for it and often learn the word 'Core' in Year 11, which is far too late. The decision is made by the school, usually with a view on the child's performance through Year 10, and it is revisable up to a point. Ask the academic coordinator directly: which tier is my child currently entered for in each subject, when is the decision final, and what would change it.

A CBSE background pushes this decision in an unhelpful direction. Indian board mathematics covers a good deal of algebra and trigonometry early, so a CBSE Class 8 leaver frequently looks strong in Year 9 and is placed on the Extended route with confidence. That placement is often right. What makes it risky is that the apparent strength is content coverage rather than examination technique, and the Extended papers reward applying a method to an unfamiliar situation rather than repeating a practised one. The honest position is to place on the Extended route and then teach deliberately towards it, not to assume the content head start carries through to the series.

Beyond tiers, Cambridge IGCSE is a Years 9 to 11 structure where the final two years carry the assessed course. Establish which course your child is actually entered for before buying anything: subject by subject, with the syllabus code the school is using, because two syllabuses with similar names can be assessed quite differently. Do not accept any paper count, duration, component weighting or coursework proportion from a tutor's memory or from a page like this one. Cambridge International Education revises syllabuses on a published cycle, and the current syllabus document for your child's examination year is the only reliable source. The school's examinations officer can confirm which version applies.

Working across all IB and IGCSE subjects at IGCSE Years 9-11 with a tutor in Mumbai, the pattern we see is that tier and subject decisions made in Year 9 explain more of the Year 11 result than anything a tutor does in Year 11. Spend an hour on those decisions. It is the cheapest hour of any CBSE to IGCSE transition in Mumbai.

sections.heading: Choosing subjects for the first time: the thing CBSE never asked
paragraphs: A CBSE student has rarely chosen anything. The timetable arrived, the subjects were on it, and the only decision was how hard to work. A Cambridge school asks a fourteen-year-old and their parents to pick a set: the sciences separately or as a combined course, which second language, whether to take Business Studies, Economics, Computer Science, Information and Communication Technology, Global Perspectives, Art and Design or Drama. Families who treat this as a formality fill the grid with the most familiar-sounding subjects and discover in Year 11 that the child is carrying three they dislike.

The language questions deserve particular care. English is offered on more than one route, and placement on a first-language or second-language course changes both the work and what the certificate shows, so ask the school which route they have entered your child for and why. Hindi is widely available as a second language and a CBSE student is usually comfortable with it, which makes it the pragmatic choice; Hindi at a more demanding level is worth asking about for a child who reads in Hindi willingly. French and Spanish are usually started from scratch, which is a real workload for a transition year, and that is worth knowing before a child picks one because a friend did.

In the sciences the decision between three separate subjects and a combined course is about appetite and destination rather than ability. A child aiming at a science-heavy pathway after Year 11 generally wants the separate sciences; a child with other interests is often better served by the combined route and the time it frees. The practical component also differs by route, with some subjects assessed through laboratory coursework and others through a written paper about practical work, and a CBSE student who has only ever followed a prescribed experiment needs teaching in reading apparatus diagrams, recording to a sensible precision and explaining why a method controls a variable.

All IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai teaches at this level divide into the familiar and the genuinely new, and the genuinely new ones need ordinary teaching rather than transition work. Business Studies, Economics, Global Perspectives and Computer Science have no CBSE predecessor for most students, so a child taking two of them is learning two new subjects while also learning a new examination style.
bullets: A CBSE student has never built a subject grid before
Ask which English route the school has entered the child for
Hindi as a second language is usually the pragmatic choice
Separate sciences or combined is about destination, not ability
New subjects with no CBSE predecessor need teaching, not transition work

sections.heading: IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai, corridor by corridor
paragraphs: The Central Suburbs are where this request clusters, because Powai and Chandivali hold both a large CBSE-schooled population and several Cambridge schools within a few kilometres. Powai is the awkward one logistically: physically central, no station of its own, reached by road along JVLR from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, with the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road making Chembur and Kurla tutors viable. Ghatkopar sits on both the Central Line and Metro Line 1, which makes it the easiest node in the city to reach from either side, and we use that deliberately when a scarce subject tutor needs to serve several families.

Northward along the Western Line and the Western Express Highway we cover Andheri East and West, Jogeshwari, Goregaon East, Malad, Kandivali, Borivali and Dahisar, with Metro Lines 2A and 7 having changed what a Dahisar or Borivali tutor can accept as a weekday slot. Link Road carries the traffic the highway does not. In the Eastern Suburbs we work in Chembur, Govandi, Vikhroli, Bhandup and Mulund along the Central and Harbour lines, the Eastern Express Highway and the Eastern Freeway. South Mumbai families in Cuffe Parade, Fort, Tardeo and Walkeshwar are matched within the island, with the Coastal Road, Metro Line 3 and the Bandra-Worli Sea Link doing the work.

Navi Mumbai divides into Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel, matched node to node along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, with the Trans-Harbour Line and the Atal Setu available and not relied upon for a weekday evening. Thane runs from the station across Pokhran Road and Majiwada towards Ghodbunder Road and Kasarvadavali, where the evening peak, not the map, sets the hour. Families searching for IGCSE tutors near me in Mumbai should know that the answer depends on the subject: mathematics and the sciences are widely covered in every zone, while Business Studies, Computer Science or a second language at this level may mean a tutor from two suburbs away or an online match.

For a transition specifically, we try to keep the first month local even if the subject specialist is not, running the baseline and the technique work with a nearby tutor and adding the specialist later.

sections.heading: How do Mumbai Cambridge schools admit a CBSE student mid-stream?
paragraphs: Through a written assessment and an interview, almost always, and the written paper is where CBSE students are either placed well or placed badly. Bombay Cambridge International School in Andheri East, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, Podar International School in Powai and Santacruz, Thakur International School in Kandivali East, JBCN International School in Borivali and Oshiwara, Witty International School in Malad and Chembur, Billabong High International School in Santacruz, Juhu, Malad and Thane, Singapore International School in Dahisar East, Oberoi International School at JVLR and Smt Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane all run Cambridge pathways, and their entrance papers test reading of unfamiliar material rather than recall of a syllabus.

Year-group placement is the question to settle first and in writing. Most schools map CBSE Class 8 to Year 9, which loses nothing, but placement depends on age cut-offs and on the school's own policy, and a child occasionally repeats a year. A family that discovers this in July, after fees are paid, has no room to negotiate. Ask in the first conversation which year group the child is being considered for, and what the school does if the entrance assessment suggests a different placement.

The calendar then imposes its own order. Cambridge schools in the city run admissions through the cooler months for a monsoon start, while a CBSE child is still mid-session, so the family is often asking for a transfer certificate in the middle of a school year. Coursework deadlines in Year 11 arrive well before the written series, so the final year is front-loaded in a way CBSE's single examination season is not. Get the actual dates from the school's examinations officer for your child's cohort instead of relying on anything published online, including here, because series arrangements and internal deadlines move.

IB Gram is an independent platform and has no affiliation with any school listed here. They are named because their admission formats and calendars decide what preparation is worth doing, and for nothing else.
bullets: Entrance papers test unfamiliar material, not syllabus recall
Settle the year-group placement in writing before fees are paid
Admissions run in the cooler months for a monsoon start
Year 11 coursework deadlines fall well before the written series

sections.heading: Home classes, online lessons and the Mumbai evening peak
paragraphs: Home tutoring leads for the first stretch of a transition because the work is diagnostic and physical. The tutor needs the child's CBSE notebooks, the new school's handouts, a printed past paper and a desk to spread them on, and the student needs to be watched while attempting an application question so the tutor can see exactly where the reading of the question went wrong. Two or three weeks of home classes at the start saves a month of guessing later, and it is why our lead service on this request is home tuition rather than a video call.

Online then handles two situations well. The first is scarcity: a Computer Science or Business Studies specialist with Cambridge experience may be the only sensible match and may live nowhere near you, in which case an IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai is the arrangement rather than a compromise. The second is the evening peak. A Powai family wanting a seven o'clock start with a tutor from Andheri East is asking that tutor to cross JVLR at its worst, and the slot that looks fine in April fails repeatedly in July. Moving one of two weekly sessions online keeps continuity without anyone sitting in traffic.

The trade-offs, stated plainly. Online is weak for anything involving apparatus diagrams, construction with a compass, or a long worked solution where the tutor needs to see the student's hand moving. It needs the paper printed, because a student reading a question on the same screen as the video call reads neither properly. It suits an organised household and punishes a chaotic one. Home sessions carry travel cost and monsoon risk, and they are worth it for the baseline, the tier conversation and any coursework planning.

Hybrid is where most families settle: one home session for written and practical work, one shorter online session for marking and corrections. A family asking for all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Mumbai from a single tutor usually ends up with thin coverage in the two subjects that mattered most, and we will say so rather than take the booking quietly.
bullets: First weeks at home: the tutor must watch the question being read
Online solves scarce subjects and avoids the JVLR evening crossing
Print the paper; a question read on the call screen is read badly
Online is weak for apparatus diagrams and compass constructions
Hybrid: one home session for written work, one online for corrections

sections.heading: What we verify, and what to ask a Cambridge-experienced tutor
paragraphs: The platform verifies identity against a photograph document, verifies the degree claimed, and interviews each applicant about board experience in specifics: which syllabus codes, which years, taught in a school or privately, and whether they have prepared students through a full Year 11 series. References from earlier families are taken up for anyone new. For transition requests we add a marking exercise, because the skill in demand is diagnostic. We hand over a CBSE-style script and ask what a Cambridge examiner would not reward in it.

Your questions on the call should be equally concrete. Ask the tutor to explain what 'suggest' asks for in a Cambridge question and how it differs from 'state'. Ask how method marks work in a mathematics solution and what a student loses by writing only the answer. Ask what they would advise on the tier decision for your child, and whether they would want to see a past paper attempt first; the right answer is yes. Ask which syllabus version they teach from and watch whether they check rather than answer from memory.

Some signals should end the conversation. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, who quotes a fixed number of hours to finish a syllabus they have not read, or who supplies model coursework for a student to adapt. Coursework submitted as a student's own work has to be the student's own work, and a shortcut there is a far worse outcome than a mediocre draft. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and the thing we will commit to is a written diagnosis and an honest view on the tier.

Parents hunting for the best IGCSE tutor in Mumbai are usually hunting for the one who will tell them the truth about Year 11 in Year 9. That tutor exists, is not always the most expensive, and can be identified by the fact that they asked to see a script before quoting anything.
bullets: Identity, degree and syllabus-level board experience verified first
Applicants say what a Cambridge examiner would not reward in a script
Ask the tutor to distinguish 'suggest' from 'state' on the call
Ask how method marks are earned in a mathematics solution
Be wary of promised grades or supplied model coursework

sections.heading: Why a CBSE child finds IGCSE easy in Year 9 and hard in Year 11
paragraphs: The first two terms genuinely are easier, and that is not an illusion. Indian board mathematics introduces algebraic manipulation, factorisation and trigonometry earlier than the Cambridge sequence does, so a Class 8 leaver meets Year 9 content they have largely seen. Science content overlaps substantially. Homework volume usually drops. The child reports that school is relaxed, the family concludes the transition went well, and nobody does the technique work. Then Year 11 arrives with Extended papers that ask the student to apply a known method to an unfamiliar context, and the gap that was always there becomes a grade.

The gap has three parts and they are all mark-scheme literacy rather than knowledge. First, method marks: CBSE marking rewards a correct final answer generously, while a Cambridge solution earns credit for steps, so a student who computes mentally and writes one line loses marks they had earned in their head. Second, the command words: 'state' wants a fact, 'describe' wants what happens, 'explain' wants why, 'suggest' wants the student to apply knowledge to a situation the syllabus never mentioned, and 'calculate' expects working. A CBSE-trained student answers nearly everything as though it said 'state' or 'describe'. Third, precision and units in the sciences, where a correct number recorded to an implausible precision or without units is simply wrong.

Separate the two kinds of gap before buying hours, because they cost differently. Content gaps for a CBSE child entering Cambridge are small and specific, and often run the other way: a few topics the Indian sequence covers later, probability and some statistics treated differently, set notation and vector conventions, and subject-specific vocabulary. Two or three weeks closes them. Skill gaps are the real bill: reading a question for its command word, writing working that earns method marks, applying a method to an unfamiliar context, handling a source or data-response question, reading apparatus diagrams, and meeting coursework deadlines nobody enforces daily. Those take a term and they improve through marked past-paper work rather than through more notes. A CBSE to IGCSE transition in Mumbai that is sold as syllabus coverage has misread the problem, which is why some families buy two years of tuition and still see the drop in Year 11.

What IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on follows from that: the subject and how many Cambridge-experienced teachers of it live in the city, the tier, whether coursework supervision is involved, the travel corridor and the evening peak the tutor crosses, session length, and whether the booking is a short diagnostic block or a full year. Online removes the travel element. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai looks cheaper per hour and tends to cost more per grade.
bullets: Year 9 overlaps with CBSE content, which hides the technique gap
Method marks: computing mentally and writing one line loses credit
'Suggest' asks for application to a context the syllabus never mentions
Precision and units are marked, not assumed, in the sciences
Content gaps clear in weeks; mark-scheme literacy takes a term

sections.heading: What changes at four weeks, one term and one exam series?
paragraphs: At four weeks the only honest measure is the behaviour of the pen. Does the child write working before the answer? Do they underline or circle the command word? Do they read the data in a table before attempting the question about it? Do they write units? Those four habits are visible on any marked past paper and are the leading indicators for everything that follows. School marks four weeks into a CBSE to IGCSE transition in Mumbai tell you very little, because most Cambridge schools are still teaching content the child has met before.

By the end of a term, past-paper performance should separate from classwork performance in a useful direction. The student should be scoring better on application questions than they did in week one even if the topic is unfamiliar, and the tutor should be able to show you two marked scripts that demonstrate it. Coursework behaviour is the other term-level signal: a draft produced before the school's internal deadline rather than in the week it falls due. If neither has changed in twelve weeks, something is wrong with the arrangement rather than with the child.

Over a full examination series the picture completes, and here are the honest limits. Tuition does not change a tier entry that was fixed too low, it does not create two years of coursework in a final term, and it cannot make a child care about a subject they were pushed into. If your child is in Year 11, entered at Core in a subject where they need a higher grade, the useful conversation is with the school about whether the entry can still be changed, not with a tutor about extra hours. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and will say plainly when the limiting factor is a decision made two years earlier.

If the tutor is not right, the signs are a student who has stopped asking questions, past papers that are 'completed' but not marked, and sessions that drift into going over classwork. Say so in week three or four. Describe what specifically is wrong, we shortlist again, and the replacement tutor gets the baseline scripts and the written diagnosis so the first session is not spent re-establishing what is already known.
bullets: Week four: working shown, command words marked, units written
One term: application questions improve even on unfamiliar topics
Coursework drafted before the internal deadline, not during it
A tier entered too low cannot be fixed with extra hours
Report a weak match in week three; baseline scripts pass to the next tutor

sections.heading: Starting CBSE to IGCSE transition work in Mumbai
paragraphs: Have four things ready. The year group and subject allocation from the school, in writing. The tier for mathematics and each science, if it has been set. The last CBSE report card, which is useful as context rather than as evidence. And two weekday windows plus a weekend window that hold on your corridor during the monsoon, not only in the dry months. Families across Mumbai, Maharashtra routinely agree a slot in April that fails three times in July, and a tutor who has been stood up twice will ask to move online.

Settle the building access question in the same conversation. Societies in Powai, Chandivali, Kandivali East and off Ghodbunder Road handle repeat visitors differently: an app-based resident approval each time, a one-off registration of a regular visitor, a photo identity record at the gate, or a cut-off hour after which visitors are not admitted at all. One question to your society manager prevents a tutor waiting at a gate while the session time runs out.

The first session is a Cambridge past paper taken cold, with no revision and no help, on topics the child has already studied. The tutor marks it against the published mark scheme, not generously, and then goes through it with the student showing where marks existed and were not collected. That usually produces the moment the whole arrangement depends on, when a child who has been told they are good at mathematics sees eight marks lost for not writing a method. You then receive a written note splitting content gaps from technique gaps, with a view on the tier.

From there the pattern is weekly or twice weekly, reviewed against that note at four weeks. An IGCSE private tutor in Mumbai working this way is accountable to something written down rather than to how the sessions feel, and if the note says your child needs a fortnight of technique work and nothing else, it will say that.
bullets: Bring the year group, subject allocation and tier in writing
Give windows that survive the monsoon on your own corridor
Ask your society once about repeat-visitor entry rules
First session: a past paper taken cold and marked strictly
A written content-versus-technique note, with a view on the tier

faqs.question: Which year group will my child be placed in moving from CBSE?
faqs.answer: Most Mumbai Cambridge schools map CBSE Class 8 to Year 9, so a child usually loses nothing, but placement depends on the school's age policy and on the entrance assessment. Some schools will place a child a year lower if the assessment suggests the English or mathematics base is not ready for an Extended route, and a few will not take an entrant directly into Year 11 at all. Ask the admissions office in the first conversation which year group is being considered and what happens if the assessment points elsewhere. Get the answer in writing before fees are paid, because it is very hard to renegotiate afterwards.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to our building in Powai for a seven o'clock evening slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the tutor is matched from the right side. Powai has no station of its own, so tutors reach it by road along JVLR from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg, Ghatkopar or Chandivali, and from Chembur and Kurla using the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road. A home tutor already on the Powai side manages a seven o'clock start comfortably. One crossing JVLR westbound at that hour will be late in the monsoon more often than not. Tell us your preferred window first and we filter the shortlist by who can actually keep it, rather than asking a tutor to promise a commute they will come to resent.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home, and what does the study space need?
faqs.answer: An adult in the flat, yes; in the room, only for the first session or two. For this transition the space needs a flat surface big enough for an A4 past paper, a calculator, a geometry set and the child's notebook open at the same time, because sessions constantly compare what the school taught with what the paper asks. Good light, the door closed, the phone in another room. Families who run sessions at a cleared dining table consistently get more out of them than those who use a bed or a sofa, and the difference shows up in the quality of written working.

faqs.question: My child found Year 9 easy. Should we even bother with a tutor?
faqs.answer: Probably yes, and for technique rather than content. The Year 9 overlap with CBSE material is real, so an easy first year is expected and tells you nothing about Year 11, where Extended papers ask for application to unfamiliar contexts. The cheap version of this is a short diagnostic block of home classes: a few sessions in which the child attempts past-paper questions, gets them marked strictly, and learns how method marks, command words and units work. If the script comes back clean, stop. Most do not come back clean, and finding that out in Year 9 costs a fraction of finding it out in Year 11.

faqs.question: How do we decide between Core and Extended?
faqs.answer: Decide with the school, with a past-paper attempt in front of you rather than a report card. Ask the academic coordinator which tier your child is currently entered for in each subject, when the entry is finalised and what evidence would change it. A child who handles unfamiliar application questions, shows method and works accurately under time pressure belongs on the Extended route. A child who is accurate on practised material but stalls on anything unfamiliar can get there with a term of technique work, which is the argument for doing that work in Year 10 rather than accepting a lower tier in Year 11.

faqs.question: Which second language should a CBSE student take?
faqs.answer: Usually the one they already have, which for most CBSE students means Hindi. A new language started from scratch in a transition year adds workload at precisely the moment a child is also learning a new examination style, and French or Spanish begun in Year 9 generally only works for a student who enjoys languages. Ask the school which language courses are actually running for your child's cohort rather than which appear in the prospectus, because availability depends on teacher allocation each year. Also ask which English route the school has entered the child for, since that interacts with the language choice.

faqs.question: What is the Alternative to Practical paper and does it matter for us?
faqs.answer: Some Cambridge science subjects assess practical skills through a written paper about experiments rather than through assessed laboratory work, and which route applies depends on the syllabus and the school's entry. It matters because the skills are specific and teachable: reading a measuring instrument from a diagram, identifying the variable being controlled, spotting why a method would give an unreliable result, and recording values to a sensible precision. CBSE students who followed prescribed experiments have rarely practised any of it. Ask the examinations officer which component your child is entered for, then ask the tutor to work through past questions from that exact component.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge mathematics harder or easier than CBSE mathematics?
faqs.answer: Different rather than harder, and the difference is where marks live. CBSE questions tend to reward a correct final answer and recognisable methods; Cambridge papers award credit through the working, expect a method to be applied to situations the syllabus never showed, and use command words precisely. A CBSE student is often ahead on content and behind on presentation, losing marks in their own head by computing without writing. The fix is mechanical and fast once a student sees a marked script: show the method, write the units, read the command word. Most of the improvement appears within a few weeks of marked practice.

faqs.question: We are moving mid-year. How much catching up is involved?
faqs.answer: A mid-year CBSE to IGCSE transition in Mumbai involves less content than you fear and more organisation than you expect. A mid-year entrant has to pick up the units already taught, which is usually a few weeks of direct teaching, and simultaneously learn a mark scheme culture their classmates have had since Year 9. Get the school's scheme of work and any coursework briefs already issued, and give them to the tutor before the first session. The first month is triage and the second looks like teaching. Trying to start from the beginning of the syllabus in a mid-year entry wastes the term and leaves the immediate deadlines unaddressed.

faqs.question: What do IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on, and why no price here?
faqs.answer: They depend on subject scarcity, tier, whether coursework supervision is involved, travel corridor and evening peak, session length, and whether you book a diagnostic block or a year. A Cambridge-experienced Computer Science or Business Studies tutor is scarcer than a mathematics tutor and prices accordingly. Online removes travel from the calculation entirely. Any figure printed on a web page goes out of date and then misleads a parent who read it a year later, so we would rather give you a specific answer for your subject, area and windows than publish a range designed to look reassuring.

faqs.question: My child's school says everything is fine but the mock results dropped. Who is right?
faqs.answer: Both, usually. School feedback often reflects classwork and effort, both of which can be good while examination technique is weak, and mocks are the first place where unfamiliar application questions appear in volume. Ask the school for the marked mock script rather than the grade, and look at where the marks were lost: unanswered application parts, missing working, no units, or a misread command word. That pattern tells you whether the problem is content or technique. Take the script to the first tutoring session, because it is better evidence than any report comment.

cbse-to-igcse-transition.closingCta: Send the year group, the subject allocation, the tier if it is set, and the windows that hold on your corridor in the monsoon. We shortlist tutors with real Cambridge classroom experience, you ask each of them about the tier decision, and the one you choose runs a past paper cold at home and marks it strictly. You get a written note splitting content gaps from technique gaps. Review it at four weeks before committing further.

sections.heading: How we match an IB and IGCSE home tutor in the Central Suburbs of Mumbai
paragraphs: A request for an IB and IGCSE home tutor in the Central Suburbs is answered in three moves. We take the board, the year and the exact subject, we filter to tutors who already travel your corridor on a weekday, and we send you a short list of profiles carrying their board experience and the evenings each one can genuinely hold. Corridor filtering is the part that decides whether a weekly slot is still running in February. A Chemistry specialist who lives in Mulund West can hold a seven o'clock Tuesday in Bhandup or Kanjurmarg for a full term without drama. The same tutor promising a seven o'clock Tuesday in Chandivali has to cross the Eastern Express Highway and then grind up Saki Vihar Road at its worst hour, and by the third week the session starts at twenty to eight and finishes early. Parents in Hiranandani Gardens often add the tower number, which is more useful than it sounds: two families in two towers behind the same gate can share one tutor's travel evening and both get a better slot for it.

sections.heading: PYP, MYP, DP or IGCSE: which programme is your child actually in?
paragraphs: Schools in this part of Mumbai run four different things, sometimes under one roof. The International Baccalaureate (IB) covers the Primary Years Programme (PYP) up to Year 5, the Middle Years Programme (MYP) across Years 6 to 10, and the Diploma Programme (DP) in Years 11 and 12. IGCSE, examined by Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel, occupies the same two years as MYP 4 and 5 but assesses in a completely different language. Knowing which one your child sits in is the first thing a tutor needs, and a surprising number of parents are told one acronym by the school and another by a relative.

The difference matters most in Years 9 and 10. MYP grades a Science student against criteria with descriptor bands, so a report line reads as a criterion letter and a number rather than a percentage. IGCSE grades a timed paper against a mark scheme, and the skill of reading a four-mark question and writing exactly four scoring points is learnable in a term. Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai takes students through IGCSE and then into the IB DP, which means the same child changes assessment language twice in four years. A tutor who has only ever taught one of the two boards will hand your child the wrong instincts at exactly the wrong moment.

Above Year 10 the structure tightens again. The DP requires three subjects at Higher Level (HL) and three at Standard Level (SL), plus the Core: Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and Creativity, Activity, Service. IGCSE instead splits several subjects into tiers, so a Maths candidate sits either the Core or the Extended paper and an Extended entry caps nothing while a Core entry caps the top grade. Those choices are made in one week of February or March and lived with for two years, which is why we treat subject selection as tutoring work rather than paperwork.

sections.heading: Subject choice across both boards, and the internal assessment each one carries
paragraphs: Every IB subject carries an internal assessment that is marked at school and moderated by the IB, and together those pieces decide a chunk of the final grade before any exam hall opens. DP Physics and Chemistry each need an individual scientific investigation with a research question narrow enough to produce a gradient worth discussing. Maths Analysis and Approaches and Maths Applications and Interpretation both need an exploration, and the commonest failure is not weak mathematics but a topic chosen in week one that cannot carry a personal engagement mark. Economics needs three commentaries on current articles, each tied to a different section of the syllabus, and an article picked lazily in October costs marks in March.

Languages and humanities work differently again. English Language and Literature asks for an individual oral built on a global issue, and the extract pair has to be chosen early enough to rehearse. History needs an investigation with genuine source evaluation. Business Management asks for a research project grounded in a real organisation, and families in Vikhroli or Kurla often have a parent working somewhere that makes a perfectly good case study if the question is framed properly. On the IGCSE side the equivalent pressure sits in the practical papers and coursework: an alternative-to-practical paper rewards students who have actually handled apparatus, and that is hard to fake from a textbook.

A worked example is clearer than a list. A DP year one student at NES International School in Mulund West taking Maths Analysis and Approaches HL, Physics HL and Economics SL has an exploration topic due around the same fortnight as her first Economics commentary and her EE research question. A home tutor who treats those as three separate jobs will run out of evenings. One who notices that her Physics investigation and her Maths exploration can share a data set, collected once, buys her back two weekends. That is the sort of planning you want from a specialist in all IB and IGCSE subjects and a tutor in the Central Suburbs who has supervised these pieces before and does it without being asked.

Maths AA and AI explorations are lost on topic choice, rarely on the mathematics

sections.heading: Which Central Suburbs localities do Mumbai tutors cover?
paragraphs: Parents here mostly search for IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Central Suburbs localities, and the answer is narrower than the phrase suggests. We place an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Central Suburbs addresses across the whole of this zone: Powai, Hiranandani Gardens, Chandivali, Kurla, Ghatkopar West, Ghatkopar East, Vikhroli, Kanjurmarg, Bhandup, Mulund West, Mulund East and Tilak Nagar. Those are not interchangeable addresses. Mulund West and Mulund East are separated by a railway line and a level of traffic that makes a seven o'clock crossing a gamble. Ghatkopar West and Ghatkopar East behave like two different suburbs for anyone arriving by Metro. Tilak Nagar and Kurla are close enough on a map to look like one pool and far enough apart at the Kurla junction to need two different tutors.

The spine here is the Central Line from Kurla up through Vidyavihar, Ghatkopar, Vikhroli, Kanjurmarg and Bhandup to Mulund, and tutors who commute by train will hold a slot anywhere along it. Metro Line 1 terminates at Ghatkopar, which makes Ghatkopar East and West reachable from Andheri and Powai-adjacent Chandivali in a way the suburban map hides. The Eastern Express Highway runs parallel for cars and autos, the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road (SCLR) brings tutors over from the western side into Kurla, and JVLR carries everyone into Powai and Chandivali. Saki Vihar Road, the Chandivali approach, is the one stretch that reliably seizes after half past six in the evening.

IB Gram works across Mumbai, Maharashtra, and the rest of the city is covered by its own pages: South Mumbai for Colaba and Peddar Road, the Western Suburbs for Bandra and Andheri along the Western Line and Metro Lines 2A and 7, the Eastern Suburbs for Chembur and Govandi on the Harbour Line and the Eastern Freeway, Navi Mumbai for Vashi and Nerul off Palm Beach Road and the Atal Setu, and Thane for Pokhran Road and Ghodbunder Road. Metro Line 3, the Bandra-Worli Sea Link and the Coastal Road matter if you are moving a child between zones, but for a weekly home session in Mulund or Powai they are somebody else's problem.

sections.heading: The school calendar across the Central Suburbs of Mumbai, and the months that hurt
paragraphs: The academic year here opens in June, in the middle of the monsoon, and the first pressure point arrives before most parents expect it. By late August a DP year two student has an EE draft deadline and an internal assessment proposal sitting in the same fortnight. October and November bring mock examinations and the Diwali break, which looks like a holiday and is actually the fortnight in which the IGCSE and DP cohorts either catch up or fall a month behind. January and February are the worst stretch of the year: TOK essays, final internal assessment submissions and school mocks land together, with the May examination session close enough to be real. By March the tutoring job has changed from teaching content to rationing revision time.

The schools families here attend set those dates. Hiranandani Foundation School sits inside Hiranandani Gardens in Powai and runs IGCSE and the IB DP. NES International School in Mulund West serves the northern end of the zone. Podar International School has a Powai campus, Witty International School draws from across the eastern corridor, and Oberoi International School is reached by many Powai and Chandivali families along JVLR rather than through the Western Suburbs. Each sets its own mock dates and its own internal assessment deadlines, so two children on the same staircase in one tower can be under completely different pressure in the same week.

We name these schools because the calendar is local knowledge a tutor needs, and nothing more than that. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school, board or examination body named on this page. We do not place tutors on behalf of a school, we do not see internal marks, and we do not speak for any institution's assessment policy. What a good home tutor does is work backwards from the dates your own school has published, and ask to see them in the first session rather than guessing from a generic Mumbai timetable.

Late August: EE drafts and internal assessment proposals arrive together

sections.heading: Home tuition, online classes or hybrid in the Central Suburbs?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default here and it is what most parents in this zone are searching for. We run all IB and IGCSE subjects as home classes in Central Suburbs flats, from PYP reading support up to Diploma Programme Higher Level. A tutor at your dining table sees the things a video call hides: the phone face-up next to the notebook, the handwriting that collapses in the last ten minutes, the diagram copied without understanding. Younger students, anyone in PYP or the lower MYP years, and any child who negotiates their way out of work need a person in the room. IB and IGCSE home tuition in Central Suburbs flats also solves a practical problem, because a child who has already travelled back from Mulund or Andheri by six o'clock has no appetite for a second commute.

Online tuition earns its place in three specific situations. Scarce subjects are the first: a DP Film, Psychology or Computer Science specialist may not live within reach of Bhandup, and an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Central Suburbs homes is better than a generalist who is physically close. The monsoon is the second, because a Powai or Chandivali session that would be cancelled outright can still run from a laptop. The third is the week before mocks, when a thirty-minute question-and-answer at nine at night is worth more than a two-hour slot three days later. The honest cost is supervision: online works properly only with a document camera or a phone propped to show written working.

Hybrid is what most families here settle into by the second term. One home session at the weekend carries the teaching and the marking of written work, and one shorter online session midweek keeps the homework honest. For a Chandivali family whose tutor comes from Andheri East, that pattern removes the one journey that was always going to break, the weekday crawl along Saki Vihar Road. For a Mulund East family it simply buys an extra contact point without an extra trip. We will say outright when a request is better served online than in person; promising a weekday home slot that the road will not allow wastes your term.

sections.heading: How are tutors checked before they reach your door in Mumbai?
paragraphs: An IB and IGCSE private tutor in the Central Suburbs walks into your flat every week, so the checking has to happen before you ever meet them. Every IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai listed on this platform clears the same checks: a government photo identity document, degree certificates for the subject they claim to teach, and a specific account of their board experience, meaning which boards, which years, which papers and whether they have supervised internal assessments. We interview on subject rather than on manner, because a confident talker who cannot mark a DP Maths exploration against the criteria is no use to a year two student in February. Tutors who have taught only a state or CBSE syllabus are not presented as IB or IGCSE specialists, however strong their subject knowledge.

You should still run your own checks, and they take ten minutes. Ask the tutor which examination session they have taught to, May or November, and what changed in the subject guide most recently. Ask them to mark one question from your child's last graded paper in front of you and explain where the marks went. Ask what a criterion descriptor band actually requires at the level your child is aiming for. A specialist answers all three without hedging. Sit in on the first twenty minutes of the first session; you will learn more from watching one explanation than from any profile.

Then there is the building, which in this zone is half the job. Societies in Hiranandani Gardens, Godrej Platinum in Vikhroli, Runwal Greens and Kalpataru Aura all run visitor systems with gate passes or an app-based approval, and a tutor who has to be cleared from scratch every week loses ten minutes at the gate and arrives unsettled. Register the tutor once with your society office as a recurring visitor, leave an identity copy at the gate, and tell the guard the slot. Where a tutor already teaches another family behind the same gate, that clearance usually exists already, which is one of the quiet advantages of a large township.
bullets: Photo identity, degree certificates and a named board-experience history before any match
Interviewed on subject: marking against criteria, not interview charm

sections.heading: Powai has no railway station of its own: what that does to your weekly slot
paragraphs: Powai is the one locality in this zone with no suburban railway station. It sits physically in the middle of the Central Suburbs and is served by none of the lines that pass on either side, so every IB and IGCSE home tutor in Central Suburbs addresses like Hiranandani Gardens, Chandivali or the Powai lake stretch arrives by road. The three realistic approaches are Kanjurmarg and Ghatkopar on the Central Line to the east, and Andheri East on the western side by way of JVLR. Choosing which of those three your tutor comes from is, in practice, choosing whether your slot holds.

The arithmetic is worth doing once. A tutor who gets off at Kanjurmarg has the shortest road leg into Hiranandani Gardens and can realistically hold a seven o'clock weekday slot, as long as the session is not immediately after another one. From Ghatkopar the trip runs up past Vikhroli and across, longer but predictable, and Ghatkopar has the added advantage of being the terminus of Metro Line 1, so a tutor living near Andheri or Marol can arrive by Metro instead of fighting the highway. The Andheri East approach is the fragile one: either JVLR, which is tolerable, or Saki Vihar Road through Chandivali, which does not move between half past six and half past seven. A tutor who tells you cheerfully that they will come from Andheri East at seven on a Wednesday has not done this before.

So the scheduling guidance for a Powai or Chandivali family is specific. If you want a seven o'clock weekday session, ask for a tutor who approaches from Kanjurmarg, Ghatkopar or Vikhroli. If the best academic match for your child happens to live in Andheri East or Marol, give that tutor the last slot of the evening, after eight, or move the session to a weekend morning when Saki Vihar Road is empty. Do not put a Powai session immediately after a Mulund one. And if your tutor already teaches another child in your complex, ask to be scheduled back to back with that family: one journey, two sessions, and a tutor who will still be turning up in March.

Townships make this workable in a way that standalone buildings do not. Hiranandani Gardens is large enough that a tutor can serve several families inside one gate across an evening, and the same holds at Godrej Platinum in Vikhroli, at Runwal Greens and at Kalpataru Aura. Parents who find each other inside a complex and ask for consecutive slots get better tutors, because a tutor will travel for three hours of teaching what they will not travel for one. It is the single most effective thing a Powai parent can do about an address with no station.
bullets: No station in Powai: tutors come by road from Kanjurmarg, Ghatkopar or Andheri East
Seven o'clock weekday slots work best with a tutor approaching from the Central Line side

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle
paragraphs: At four weeks you are not looking for a grade, you are looking for evidence that the diagnosis was right. A good home tutor has identified the actual gap by the second session, and by the fourth you should see homework coming back on time, fewer careless losses on questions the student understood, and your child able to say what they are weak at in specific language rather than saying a subject is hard. If after a month nothing has changed in how work is produced, something is wrong with the match and not with your child. Tell us then, not in February.

At one term the measurable things appear. An internal assessment draft moves up a descriptor band because the research question was tightened. A Physics student stops losing marks on uncertainties. An IGCSE Maths candidate starts finishing the Extended paper with time left, which is usually a working-method change rather than new content. A term is also long enough to see whether the student works between sessions, and that is the honest predictor of everything that follows. One exam cycle, mock to final, is the first point at which a grade is a fair test of anything.

The limits are worth stating plainly. No tutor, however good, can guarantee a grade, and IB Gram does not guarantee grades either; the IB and the examination boards mark the work, and the work is your child's. A tutor can close a content gap, teach exam technique, fix a weak internal assessment question and build a revision plan that fits the January crush. A tutor cannot make up two years of missed foundations in six weeks, cannot sit the paper, and should never be asked to write any part of coursework. If a tutor hints otherwise, that is the signal to change tutors.

When a match is not working, the fix is quick and it is normal. Say what is wrong, specifically: the pace, the explanation style, the punctuality, the fact that your child goes silent. We stop that engagement and re-match from the same corridor, usually within the same week, and the new tutor is briefed on what did not work so your child is not re-diagnosed from zero. Nobody should spend a term paying for a tutor their child has stopped talking to.
bullets: Four weeks: right diagnosis, homework returning, specific language about weaknesses
One term: a draft moves a band, a paper gets finished, a method changes

sections.heading: Starting IB and IGCSE home tuition in the Central Suburbs of Mumbai
paragraphs: Getting a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai started is mostly a matter of paperwork you already own. Have five things ready before the first session and you will save a fortnight. The most recent report card, with criterion bands or percentages as the school writes them. The subject guide or syllabus document for each subject in question, which most schools share and most parents have never opened. The last graded paper, marked, mistakes and all, because that single document tells a specialist more than an hour of conversation. Any internal assessment brief with its deadline. And the school timetable, so the tutor knows which day already ends at half past four and which one ends at six.

The first session is diagnostic and it should feel like it. Expect the tutor to work through your child's last paper question by question, ask where each mark went, set two or three problems at the level above to find the ceiling, and then say out loud what the plan is for the next month. You should finish that session knowing what will be covered, in what order, and what your child is expected to do between visits. A tutor who spends the first hour teaching new content has skipped the part that makes the rest efficient.

The practical side matters more than parents expect. Pick a table, not a bed, with a plug point and no television in line of sight. Have one parent in the flat, not in the room, for the first few sessions. Keep the phone in another room by agreement rather than by argument. Tell the tutor at the start of the term about the weeks your child will be away, and agree then how a missed session is made up. Families who settle these five things in the first week almost never raise them again, and the tutoring gets the full hour.
bullets: Bring the report card, the subject guide, the last graded paper and the timetable
First session is diagnostic: question-by-question review, then a stated month plan
A table with a plug point, no television in view, phone in another room

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Central Suburbs depend on?
faqs.answer: They depend on five things, and no honest page can quote you a single figure. The board and level come first, because a Diploma Programme Higher Level subject with an internal assessment to supervise is more demanding work than lower Middle Years Programme support. Then subject scarcity: a DP Physics, Computer Science or Psychology specialist is harder to find near Bhandup than a Maths tutor. Then travel, which is why a Powai slot reached from Andheri East costs more of a tutor's evening than a Kanjurmarg one. Then session length and frequency. Then timing, because a tutor taking a new student in January is reorganising an existing week.

faqs.question: Will a tutor really travel to Powai when there is no station there?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most of our Powai placements work, but the slot has to respect the road. Powai has no railway station of its own, so the tutor arrives by auto, bike or cab from Kanjurmarg, Ghatkopar or Andheri East. That means a seven o'clock weekday session should go to a tutor approaching from the Central Line side, while a tutor coming from Andheri East or Marol is better given the last slot of the evening or a weekend morning. Tell us your society name in Powai or Hiranandani Gardens and we will match from the direction that holds, rather than the direction that looks closest on a map.

faqs.question: How do you handle the Saki Vihar Road jam for a Chandivali evening slot?
faqs.answer: By not scheduling against it. Saki Vihar Road, the main approach into Chandivali from Andheri East, is reliably blocked from about half past six to half past seven on weekday evenings, so we either place a tutor who lives on the Chandivali or Powai side and needs no highway at all, or we move the session to eight o'clock, or we convert the midweek slot to online and put the home session on Saturday morning. What we will not do is promise you a half past six weekday start from across JVLR. That slot works twice and then quietly becomes a quarter past seven start every week.

faqs.question: Who is the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Central Suburbs?
faqs.answer: There is no single answer to that, and anyone who gives you one is selling. The right tutor is specific to your child: the board, the subject, the year, the particular gap, and the personality your child will actually talk to. A brilliant DP Chemistry specialist is the wrong choice for a Middle Years Programme Year 7 student who needs study habits built. What you should look for is board-specific experience in that exact subject, a tutor who lives or already teaches in your corridor, and a first session that diagnoses before it teaches. Judge the match after four weeks against how work is being produced.

faqs.question: Does online tuition actually work for DP Maths and Sciences?
faqs.answer: It works for Maths and Sciences better than for most subjects, provided the setup is right. These subjects live in written working, so the tutor must be able to see the page: a second camera, or a phone propped above the notebook, or a tablet the student writes on. With that, a DP Maths Analysis and Approaches session online is close to equivalent, and marking an exploration draft is arguably easier on screen. Where online loses is attention management with younger students and practical work for the Sciences. Most families in Mulund, Bhandup and Vikhroli end up running one home session and one online session each week.

faqs.question: There has been no progress after a month. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Raise it immediately, and be specific about what you are seeing. After four weeks you should expect the gap to have been correctly identified, homework to be coming back, and your child to describe their weakness in precise terms. If none of that has happened, the match is wrong, and that is a fixable problem rather than a verdict on your child. Tell us what is failing: pace, explanation style, punctuality, or your child going quiet. We end that engagement and re-match from the same corridor, usually inside the week, and brief the new tutor on what did not work.

faqs.question: How does a tutor get through my society gate every single week?
faqs.answer: Register them once as a recurring visitor and the problem disappears. Societies in Hiranandani Gardens, Godrej Platinum, Runwal Greens and Kalpataru Aura mostly run gate passes or an app-based approval, and a tutor cleared from scratch each week loses ten minutes at the gate and arrives flustered. Give the society office the tutor's name and identity number, leave a copy at the gate, and tell the guard the day and the time. If the tutor already teaches another family in your complex, that clearance usually exists. Parking is the other thing to settle in week one, especially in older buildings in Ghatkopar West and Mulund East.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two children, one in MYP and one in IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, but check the subject rather than assuming. A Maths or Science specialist with real experience of both the Middle Years Programme criteria and the IGCSE mark scheme can run consecutive sessions for two children in the same flat, which saves a journey and often buys you a better tutor. What does not work is one session with both children in it at different levels; somebody is always idle. For Diploma Programme Higher Level subjects, assume a separate specialist, because the internal assessment supervision in year two is a different job from Year 8 support.

faqs.question: Do I need to be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: For the first few sessions, yes, in the flat but not in the room. You are checking the things a profile cannot show you: whether the tutor explains or dictates, whether your child asks questions, whether the hour is actually used. After that, your presence matters less than a quiet table and a phone in another room. For younger PYP and Middle Years Programme students, an adult or a responsible family member at home is sensible throughout. If nobody can be home for an evening slot in Kurla or Tilak Nagar, say so, and we will suggest a weekend slot instead.

faqs.question: What happens if a session is missed because of rain or a tutor's travel?
faqs.answer: It gets made up, and the rule should be agreed in your first week rather than argued about in January. The Mumbai monsoon will cost you sessions in June, July and August, and the Eastern Express Highway will cost you one or two more over a year. The usual arrangement is that a session cancelled by the tutor is rescheduled or run online that same week, and a session cancelled by the family with reasonable notice is moved rather than lost. Short-notice cancellations are where families and tutors fall out, so settle the notice period explicitly at the start.

faqs.question: Can a Mulund or Ghatkopar tutor travel to Kurla or Tilak Nagar?
faqs.answer: Yes, because that whole stretch is one Central Line corridor, and it is one of the easier journeys in Mumbai. A tutor living in Mulund West or Ghatkopar East reaches Vikhroli, Kanjurmarg, Bhandup, Kurla or Tilak Nagar along the line without touching a highway, which is why slots in those localities are the most stable ones we place. The Kurla junction itself is the only reliable delay, so allow fifteen minutes around it. What we avoid is pulling a Mulund tutor across to Chandivali or Powai in the evening peak, which is a different kind of journey altogether.

faqs.question: How fast can a replacement tutor start if this one is not working?
faqs.answer: Usually within the same week, because the shortlist that produced the first match still exists. When you tell us a tutor is not working out, we stop that engagement, go back to the tutors who were already filtered for your corridor, your board and your subject, and brief the new one on the diagnosis and on what specifically failed. Your child is not re-assessed from zero, which is the part parents dread. If the problem is scarcity rather than fit, for instance a DP subject with few specialists near Bhandup, we will say so and offer an online option honestly.

sections.heading: How does IB Gram handle a search for a certified IB tutor in Mumbai?
paragraphs: We translate the word certified into the four things it is standing in for, because the word itself cannot be matched on. When a request for a certified IB tutor in Mumbai reaches a coordinator here, it gets broken into four questions a parent is really asking: does this person know the subject at the level being taught, have they taught it to this age group before, will somebody outside their own CV vouch for them, and can they be at your flat at the same hour every week for a full term. Not one of those four is a certificate. All four can be checked in an afternoon.

So the intake call never asks about certificates. It asks which board and which year: Diploma Programme (DP) Year 1 or Year 2, Middle Years Programme (MYP) Year 4, IGCSE Year 10 or Year 11. It asks for the subject and the level, meaning Higher Level (HL) or Standard Level (SL) on the IB side and Core or Extended on the IGCSE side. It asks what came back on the last marked piece of work and what the teacher wrote underneath it. Then it asks where you live, which floor, and which two evenings genuinely work. A tutor who is right for Chemistry HL in Khar West is the wrong match for the same subject in Kharghar, because the travel quietly kills the slot by week three and nobody says so until the term is half gone.

The shortlist that comes back writes qualifications out in full rather than summarising them into a badge. It names the degree and the university that awarded it, the teaching qualification where there is one, the schools taught at with the years, and the boards and levels actually taught. Where a tutor has done examining work for a board under contract, the profile says examining work for a named board, which is a job rather than a certification. Where a tutor has attended an IB professional development workshop, the profile says workshop attendance, because that is exactly what attending a workshop is. Reading three profiles written that way takes about four minutes and tells you more than any certificate scan sent on WhatsApp.

The last step is the one most parents skip, and it is the only one that tests ability rather than paperwork. Before you commit to a weekly slot, hand the tutor one piece of your child's recent marked work with the teacher's grade covered up, and ask them to mark it against the published criteria for that subject and say which criterion is costing the marks. A tutor who can do that in fifteen minutes has shown you something no framed document can. A tutor who talks around it has also told you something.

5. Ask the tutor to mark a past script against the published subject criteria
