sections.heading: What the IB runs for teachers, and what nobody runs for tutors
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) does run professional development, and it is worth understanding precisely what it is. The IB runs workshops for teachers, organised into recognised categories that move from an introduction to a subject's requirements through to more advanced practice, delivered in person at regional events and online. A school registers its staff, the staff attend, and the school keeps the record as part of showing it supports the people in its classrooms. That is the entire mechanism. It is professional development for classroom teachers working inside authorised IB schools, and it is aimed at the school's programme, not at anybody's private practice.

What follows from that is narrow, and the narrowness is the point. A teacher who has attended an IB subject workshop has attended an IB subject workshop. It is a genuine and useful thing to have done, and someone who has sat through one usually reads the assessment model more accurately than someone who has not. But it is not a tutoring licence. It does not transfer to a private arrangement at your dining table in Chembur, nobody inspects or renews it when that teacher starts taking students privately, and it does not make the person an IB certified tutor, because the IB does not certify tutors. There is no IB register of approved private tutors, no IB tutor examination, and no IB endorsement that any platform, including this one, can apply for or buy.

Cambridge International Education works on the same logic. It supports and trains teachers at registered schools and examination centres, and what it recognises is the centre, not the individual coaching a student at home in Vashi. Pearson Edexcel is the same again. Separately, some universities offer teaching certificates and master's routes recognised by the IB for classroom educators, and where a tutor holds one of those, the award comes from the named university and is a teaching qualification rather than a permit to tutor. The pattern across every board is identical: the bodies register schools and centres, and nobody anywhere registers tutors. An IB private tutor Mumbai families hire is not holding a regulated title.

This matters most at the boundaries between programmes, where a mismatched specialist does real damage. Primary Years Programme (PYP) teaching runs on inquiry and transdisciplinary units, and a DP Physics specialist is usually a poor fit for a Year 3 child. MYP Years 4 and 5 run on published subject criteria and a personal project. IGCSE Years 10 and 11 run on syllabus content and a fixed set of papers. The Diploma Programme adds Internal Assessment (IA) in every subject, the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) on top of six subjects and a timetable that does not move. No certificate tells you which of those four a person can teach. The schools they taught in, and the years they were there, tell you almost immediately.
bullets: The IB runs teacher workshops through authorised schools, not tutor licensing
Attending a workshop is attendance, not a qualification to tutor privately
Cambridge International registers schools and examination centres, never individual tutors
University-awarded IB teaching certificates exist and name the awarding university
No board issues, renews or inspects any private tutoring credential anywhere

sections.heading: Testing real depth across all IB and IGCSE subjects
paragraphs: Subject choice is where a credential claim either holds up or falls apart, because every subject carries its own assessment machinery. On the IB side a DP student picks six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, and the HL decision changes the paper structure, the content volume and the IA expectation. On the IGCSE side the equivalent decision is Core or Extended, which changes which papers the student sits and the grade range available to them, and it is routinely made in Year 9 by families who have not been told it caps an outcome. Ask any tutor to explain the Core and Extended split in Mathematics before you discuss anything else. The answer takes thirty seconds and separates the people who have taught it from the people who have read about it.

Then there are the internal assessments, which is where parents lose marks they never see coming. MYP Sciences is marked against published criteria covering knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science, and a child who writes a beautiful method but never evaluates the limitations of their data loses a band on one criterion alone. A DP Sciences IA lives or dies on research design and the evaluation paragraph, not on the quality of the graph. A DP Mathematics exploration is marked on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the mathematics itself, which means a technically perfect piece with no reflection sits mid-band. The published criteria for all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai teaches are public documents, and a tutor who cannot name the criteria for your child's subject has not been working in it.

The language and humanities subjects behave differently again, and the mismatch here is the most common one we see. DP English Language and Literature splits a guided textual analysis from a comparative essay and an oral component, and a tutor whose instinct is to teach content summaries will coach the wrong skill for a year. Economics at Higher Level carries an extra paper with a quantitative and policy emphasis that Standard Level students never sit. History carries an internal investigation with its own structure and its own reference expectations. A tutor who taught IGCSE History well does not automatically transfer to a DP History investigation, and the honest ones say so on the first call.

So the subject conversation we run is deliberately specific. Not can you teach Biology, but can you teach DP Biology HL with the IA due in February, or MYP Year 5 Integrated Sciences with a criterion-marked lab report next fortnight, or IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences Extended with a child who is strong in Chemistry and lost in Physics. Those three requests need three different people. Matching them to one person because that person had a certificate is how a term gets wasted politely.
bullets: HL or SL on the IB side changes paper structure and IA expectation
Core or Extended in IGCSE Mathematics changes papers and available grade range
MYP subjects are marked against published criteria, not against a content list
DP IAs turn on research design and evaluation more than presentation
A tutor should name your child's subject criteria without being prompted
IGCSE strength does not automatically transfer to a DP investigation

sections.heading: Home tuition across all six zones of Mumbai
paragraphs: The same request arrives from every corner of Mumbai, Maharashtra, and geography changes the answer more than credentials do. In South Mumbai the distances look trivial and behave badly: a tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers eight kilometres and can still lose forty minutes to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals at seven in the evening, which is why we match inside the island for Cuffe Parade, Walkeshwar, Fort and Tardeo rather than pulling somebody down the Coastal Road from the suburbs. The Western Line through Churchgate, Grant Road and Mumbai Central and Metro Line 3 towards Bandra Kurla Complex make midday and weekend slots workable here in a way weekday evenings are not. In the Western Suburbs the city runs north to south along the Western Express Highway, Link Road and the Western Line, so Bandra to Andheri is quick at eleven in the morning and brutal at six, and matching along the line, Khar West to Santacruz West, Malad to Kandivali, Borivali to Dahisar, holds together where matching across it does not. Metro Lines 2A and 7 have changed Goregaon, Malad and Dahisar genuinely, and Metro Line 1 makes Andheri to Ghatkopar a reliable thirty minutes.

The Central Suburbs sit on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off the Jogeshwari Vikhroli Link Road in between. Powai is the exception that catches new tutors out: it is physically central and has no station of its own, so a tutor reaches a Hiranandani Gardens flat by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, and a monsoon evening turns a twenty-minute run into fifty. Kurla and Mulund are straightforward by train. The Santacruz Chembur Link Road is the piece that makes a Chembur tutor viable in Powai at all. In the Eastern Suburbs, from Chembur and Govandi through Vikhroli and Bhandup up to Mulund, the Central and Harbour lines plus the Eastern Freeway mean South Mumbai is closer from Chembur or Wadala than the map suggests, and a tutor living in Chembur can realistically cover both a Govandi student at five and a Wadala student at seven.

Navi Mumbai is planned in nodes, and node-to-node is the only pattern that survives a full term. Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are each a short drive from the next along Palm Beach Road and the Sion Panvel Highway, served by the Harbour Line, the Trans-Harbour Line from Thane and Navi Mumbai Metro Line 1 between Belapur and Pendhar. The Atal Setu has shortened the island crossing on paper, but pulling a tutor across the creek for a Tuesday evening lesson in Kharghar still breaks by about week five. Thane spreads west to east from the station across Pokhran Road, Majiwada and Ghodbunder Road, and the Ghodbunder stretch sets the whole schedule: a tutor near Thane station reaches Kasarvadavali in twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour in the evening peak. Thane tutors cover Thane, and a Mulund tutor crosses over only for a weekend slot.

None of this is logistics trivia dressed up as content. It is the single most common reason a credential-led search ends badly. A parent in Dahisar finds a tutor in Chembur whose paperwork looks impressive, books the slot on that basis, and by the fourth week the sessions are starting at eight and ending early. The tutor was not the problem; the commute was. One home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families actually study is rare in any case, so for a DP student taking Physics HL and Spanish SL you are usually arranging two people, which doubles the travel question. All IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Mumbai parents book get judged on whether the slot survives March, and that is a map problem before it is a qualifications problem. When a parent searches IB tutors near me in Mumbai, the instinct behind the search is correct.
bullets: South Mumbai: Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Worli, Walkeshwar, Fort, matched within the island
Western Suburbs: Bandra, Khar West, Santacruz West, Juhu, Andheri, Malad, Borivali, Dahisar
Central Suburbs: Powai, Chandivali, Ghatkopar, Kurla, Kanjurmarg, Mulund, reached via JVLR
Eastern Suburbs: Chembur, Govandi, Vikhroli, Bhandup, Wadala, helped by the Eastern Freeway
Navi Mumbai: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar, Panvel, matched node to node
Thane: Pokhran Road, Majiwada, Ghodbunder Road, Kasarvadavali, scheduled around the evening peak

sections.heading: Which Mumbai school calendar sets your real deadlines?
paragraphs: Your child's school calendar, not the examination session, is what decides when a tutor is urgently needed. The Mumbai academic year opens in June or early July, the first reporting round lands in August and September, mock examinations cluster through October and November, and the serious internal assessment submissions fall between December and the end of February. Final uploads for a May session sit in the first weeks of March. Which means the honest advice is that a tutor hired in January for a May examination is arriving after most of the coursework marks have already been fixed, and the useful hiring months are July, August and early September.

The pressure points stack rather than arrive one at a time, and this is what parents underestimate. Families at Dhirubhai Ambani International School in Bandra Kurla Complex, the American School of Bombay, Ascend International School, Ecole Mondiale World School and Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, Oberoi International School off the Jogeshwari Vikhroli Link Road, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, NES International School in Mulund West and the JBCN International School campuses in Parel, Borivali, Oshiwara and Chembur all work to the same broad DP rhythm. In South Mumbai, B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade, Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, Bombay International School at Babulnath, Activity High School on Peddar Road, Gopi Birla Memorial School in Walkeshwar and Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo set the IGCSE and DP pattern. Across the creek and up the Central Line, D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul and Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane add their own dates, as do Thakur International School in Kandivali East, Singapore International School in Dahisar East, Bombay Cambridge International School in Andheri East and the Billabong High, Podar, Witty and Ryan Global campuses spread between Santacruz, Malad, Chembur, Worli and Thane.

IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and is not affiliated with the International Baccalaureate organisation, with Cambridge International Education, or with any school named on this page. Naming those schools here is local context and nothing more: it tells you which calendar your neighbour's child is working to, which is genuinely useful when you are deciding whether a Thursday slot will collide with a submission week. We do not represent any of them, and none of them has approved, endorsed or reviewed this page or any tutor on the platform.

There is one calendar point worth separating out, because it is where a school posting becomes a checkable credential rather than a boast. A tutor who says they taught DP Chemistry at a named Mumbai school in a named academic year is making a claim you can test with two polite questions: which school, and which years. Schools keep staff records, former colleagues answer the telephone, and an honest tutor expects the question. A tutor who says they are IB certified is making a claim with nothing behind it to test, because there is no body to ring and no register to search. The difference between those two sentences is the entire subject of this page.
bullets: Mumbai school year opens in June or July, with mocks in October and November
Internal assessment submissions cluster from December to late February
Hiring in July or August beats hiring in January for a May session
A named school and named years can be verified; a certificate claim often cannot
Ask whether a proposed weekly slot collides with a submission fortnight

sections.heading: Does an IB home tutor in Mumbai need a certificate to teach my child?
paragraphs: No. No board, the IB included, requires or issues any certificate for private tutoring in Mumbai or anywhere else, so a certificate is never the right thing to screen on. What decides whether an IB home tutor in Mumbai is worth the money is subject depth at the right level, a teaching history somebody can confirm, and a weekly slot that survives the traffic until March.

Home tutoring is what most families here want and what we lead with, and the reasons are practical rather than sentimental. A tutor at your table sees the things a screen hides: the child who has not opened the textbook, the folder with three unmarked worksheets in it, the brother practising tabla in the next room during the only quiet hour of the evening. Hand-marked diagrams in Biology, working shown line by line in Mathematics and the physical act of annotating a past paper all go faster in person. The cost is travel, and travel is the real constraint: an evening home slot in Mumbai locks a tutor out of roughly two hours around it, which narrows who can genuinely commit to a Kandivali or Kasarvadavali address on a weekday. Parents who searched for a certified IB tutor in Mumbai and then booked home sessions usually find the shortlist was shaped by geography as much as by subject.

Online is the honest answer for scarce subjects and awkward addresses, and it is better than its reputation for some work and worse for others. An IB online tutor in Mumbai can be a specialist in DP Economics Higher Level or Spanish B or Global Politics who simply does not exist within forty minutes of your flat, and for essay feedback, mark-scheme walkthroughs, IA structuring and TOK discussion a shared screen is genuinely equal to a shared table. It is weaker for a child who needs somebody sitting beside them to stay on task, and weaker again for early MYP, where attention management is half the job. The trade-off is explicit: you gain the right specialist and lose some of the supervision.

Hybrid is what most of our longer arrangements settle into after a few months, usually without anybody planning it. One home session a week for the hard, supervised work and one online session for review, feedback and question practice keeps the specialist and cuts the travel, which also keeps the slot alive through the monsoon. For a Thane family on Ghodbunder Road or a Panvel family at the far end of the Harbour Line, hybrid is frequently the only arrangement that lasts a full academic year. IB home tuition in Mumbai does not have to be all or nothing, and the mode should be chosen on your child's attention span and your address, not on whose profile carried more paperwork.
bullets: Home sessions expose unopened folders and unmarked worksheets that a screen hides
An evening home slot blocks about two hours of a tutor's travel time
Online opens up scarce subjects: Economics HL, Spanish B, Global Politics
Online is weaker for early MYP and for children who drift off task
Hybrid keeps the specialist, cuts the travel and survives the monsoon
Choose the mode on your address and your child, not on paperwork

sections.heading: What can you check yourself before the first home tuition session?
paragraphs: Four things, and all four take one conversation. Ask to see the degree certificate and note the awarding university. Ask for the teaching qualification, if there is one, and who awarded it. Ask which school, which subject and which years for every teaching post claimed. Ask for one reference you can telephone. Everything a search for a certified IB tutor in Mumbai is trying to establish is contained in those four answers.

Take them one at a time, because each has a failure mode. A degree in the subject is the easiest to confirm and the most frequently glossed over: a tutor teaching DP Physics HL should hold a degree with real physics in it, and a general science or engineering degree is fine while a management degree with a school-level physics background is a different proposition you should at least know about. A teaching qualification, a Bachelor of Education, a Postgraduate Certificate in Education or a university-awarded certificate in international education, is a genuine credential, and the awarding body is printed on it. A verifiable posting at a named school is the strongest single signal we see, because it has a date, a place and colleagues attached. Examining or moderating work done for a board under contract is real work, and a tutor who has done it will describe the contract rather than wave a title.

How you ask matters more than most parents expect, because the polite version gets better answers than the suspicious version. Try: may I see the degree certificate, just so I have the subject right. Try: which school was that, and which years were you there. Try: is there a parent or a head of department I could speak to for five minutes. A good tutor answers all three without tensing up, and several will offer the reference before you ask. A tutor who deflects to a certificate, who cannot name the years, or who explains that the school prefers staff not to be contacted, has given you your answer, and you have lost nothing but a cup of tea.

On our side we check identity, the degrees and teaching qualifications claimed, and the school postings we can confirm, and we write the result on the profile in plain words rather than converting it into a badge. What we cannot do is certify anybody, because no such certification exists to pass on, and we will not describe a tutor as IB certified, IB approved or IB endorsed, as none of our tutors is any of those things and neither is any tutor on any platform. We also cannot verify something a tutor has not evidenced, so where a claim is unconfirmed the profile says unconfirmed. If you ever see a tutor profile anywhere that claims board certification for an individual, treat the whole profile as unverified until somebody shows you who issued it.
bullets: Ask to see the degree certificate and read the awarding university's name
Ask who awarded any teaching qualification, then confirm that body exists
Ask which school, which subject and which years for each post claimed
Ask for one reference you can telephone, not an emailed testimonial
Treat unconfirmed claims as unconfirmed, including on our own profiles
No platform can supply board certification for an individual tutor

sections.heading: How to read a tutor's certificate, and what an honest claim sounds like
paragraphs: Start with the issuer, because that is where almost every misleading certificate gives itself away. A legitimate document names the body that awarded it, and that body can be found, telephoned or looked up in thirty seconds. A university prints its own name and a degree title. A teacher-training authority prints its own name. An IB workshop record names the IB, names the subject, names the category of workshop and names the date, and describes attendance at professional development, which is a precise and limited thing. The documents that mean nothing are the ones with a crest, a ribbon, a flourish of serif type and either no issuing body at all or a body whose name sounds official and returns nothing when you search it. An unnamed issuer is not a formality. It is the whole content of the document.

Then listen to the sentence. An honest claim sounds like this: I taught this subject at an IB school for four years, I attended the subject workshop the school sent me to, and I have marked coursework against these criteria. Every clause in that sentence is checkable and none of it overstates anything. A dishonest claim sounds like this: I am an IB certified tutor. That sentence asserts a credential that does not exist, implies the IB has assessed and approved the speaker, and cannot be tested because there is no issuer to test it against. The grey zone sits between them, in phrases like IB trained or IB qualified, which are sometimes a loose and forgivable shorthand for having attended a workshop and sometimes a deliberate upgrade of attendance into approval. The way to resolve the grey zone is one question, asked pleasantly: trained by whom, and in what year.

Three more patterns are worth recognising. Workshop attendance presented as a tutoring credential is the common one, and the giveaway is that the document describes a two or three day event while the claim describes a standing qualification. School employment presented as board approval is the second: working at an authorised IB school means the school was authorised, and the authorisation belongs to the school and stays with the school when the teacher leaves. The third is a certificate for a subject or programme other than the one being taught, which is easy to miss when you are reading a photograph on a phone: a PYP workshop record does not support a claim to teach DP Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, and an IGCSE workshop record is not a DP credential. Read which programme and which subject is printed on it, not just the logo at the top.

The conclusion is the constructive part, and it is the only test we would urge on every parent reading this. A tutor's demonstrated ability to mark your child's actual work against the published criteria tells you more than every certificate they own put together, so ask them to do it. Give them one recent piece with the school's grade covered, ask which criterion is losing the marks, ask what the next band up would require, and ask what they would have the child change in the next draft. The tutor who has really taught the subject will reach for the criteria by name, point at a specific paragraph and tell you something you did not know about your own child's work. That is a credential, and it is the only one in this field that cannot be printed.
bullets: A real certificate names its issuer; an unnamed issuer means nothing at all
An IB workshop record states attendance, a subject, a category and a date
Honest: I taught this subject at an IB school and attended the workshop
Dishonest: I am an IB certified tutor, because no such certification exists
IB trained is shorthand or inflation; ask trained by whom and when
A school's authorisation belongs to the school, not to its former teachers

sections.heading: Progress, fees and the honest limits of IB tutoring in Mumbai
paragraphs: Progress is visible well before marks move, and knowing what to look for stops a good arrangement being cancelled too early. At four weeks you should not expect a grade change; you should expect your child to describe what the next band on a criterion requires, to stop guessing at command terms like evaluate and discuss, and to arrive at a session with a specific question rather than a general gloom. At one term you should see it in marked work: fewer marks lost to structure and presentation, an IA draft that exists rather than being promised, and a teacher comment that has changed its tone. At one full examination cycle you can fairly judge the arrangement on results, and not reasonably before that. We do not guarantee grades, and anybody who does is selling you something other than tutoring.

What IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on is nothing to do with a certificate on a wall. Rates move on the board and the level, because DP Higher Level work with an IA attached is a different job from MYP Year 3 support. They move on subject scarcity, which is why a DP Spanish B or Higher Level Economics specialist costs more than a Mathematics tutor in a city with many of them. They move on travel, because a tutor giving up two hours around a Kasarvadavali or Panvel slot prices that time in. They move on session length and frequency, and a ninety-minute session is not simply one and a half times a sixty-minute one in value, since the longer session is where real IA work happens. Nobody should quote you a figure before knowing those five things, and a quote that arrives before the questions is a quote for something generic.

The honest limits deserve stating plainly, because the alternative is a disappointed family in March. A tutor cannot repair a Year 11 foundation in six weeks before an IGCSE paper, and pretending otherwise wastes money that could have gone on a longer arrangement started earlier. A tutor cannot submit coursework or sit a paper, and the internal assessment marks that were set in December are set. A tutor cannot make a child work who has decided not to, although a good one often finds the reason the child stopped, which is sometimes the most valuable thing we are paid for. And a tutor cannot change the school's deadline structure, only help your child get ahead of it.

When a tutor is not working out, say so early and say so to us rather than to the tutor alone. Three sessions is enough to know whether the room works. Tell us what is wrong in concrete terms, meaning the tutor talks for fifty minutes of the hour, or they will not touch the IA, or your daughter has stopped coming out of her room on Thursdays, and we will propose a different person rather than defend the first. Changing a tutor in week four is ordinary and costs nothing in lost time. Changing one in February costs a term. The parents who get the most out of this platform are the ones who tell us early and specifically, and the awkwardness of that conversation lasts about ninety seconds.
bullets: Four weeks: better questions and command-term fluency, not a grade change
One term: fewer structural marks lost, an IA draft that actually exists
One examination cycle: the first fair point to judge on results
Fees track board, level, subject scarcity, travel distance and session length
Nobody can guarantee grades, and no tutor can submit or sit the assessment
Raise a mismatch at three sessions, in concrete terms, and ask for a change

sections.heading: Booking home classes with a verified IB tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: Getting started takes one message and about ten minutes of preparation at your end. Put together three things before you write: your child's board, year, subject and level, meaning something like DP Year 1 Chemistry Higher Level or IGCSE Year 10 Mathematics Extended; one recent piece of marked work, photographed, with the school's comment visible; and the two evenings or weekend mornings that genuinely work at your address, not the ones that would work if the traffic behaved. Those three things let us shortlist properly instead of asking you five rounds of questions.

What comes back is two or three tutor profiles with the qualifications written out in full: degree and awarding university, teaching qualification where there is one, schools taught at with the years, boards and levels taught, and anything we could not confirm marked as unconfirmed. Read the history rather than the headline. Then pick one and book a paid first session, which we would rather you treated as an assessment of the tutor than as a free sample of your child.

The first session has a shape, and you should hold the tutor to it. The first half is diagnostic: the tutor works through the marked piece you supplied, identifies which criterion or paper skill is costing the marks and says so in words you can repeat to the school. The second half is a plan tied to your child's actual calendar, naming which fortnight the IA draft has to exist in and what happens weekly between now and then. Before the tutor leaves, ask the question this page has been building towards: mark this script against the published criteria and tell me which band it sits in and why. Then decide. If the fit is wrong, tell us within the first three sessions and we will propose somebody else without an argument.
bullets: Send board, year, subject and level in your first message
Attach one photographed piece of recent marked work with the teacher's comment
Name two evenings or weekend mornings that work at your real address
Read the written history on each profile, not the headline summary
Book a paid first session and treat it as your assessment of the tutor
Ask the tutor to band one script against the criteria before you commit

faqs.question: Is there such a thing as an IB certified tutor?
faqs.answer: No. There is no such thing as a certified IB tutor in Mumbai or anywhere else, because the International Baccalaureate does not certify, license, approve or register private tutors. The IB authorises schools to run its programmes and it runs professional development workshops for teachers at those schools, and that is the extent of it. Nobody sits an IB tutoring examination, no register of approved tutors exists to be searched, and no platform can obtain IB certification for the people on its list. If a tutor, an agency or a website uses that phrase, treat it as marketing language rather than a credential and ask who the issuing body is.

faqs.question: Are IB Gram's tutors IB certified or IB approved?
faqs.answer: No, and we will not describe them that way. IB Gram tutors are verified by IB Gram, which means we check identity, the degrees and teaching qualifications they claim, and the school postings we can confirm, and we write the outcome on the profile in plain words. They are not IB certified, IB approved or IB endorsed, because no tutor anywhere is: the certification does not exist to be held. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with the IB organisation, Cambridge International Education or any school. We also do not guarantee grades. What we can do is show you a checkable history and let you test the teaching yourself.

faqs.question: A tutor sent me a photo of an IB certificate. How do I read it?
faqs.answer: Read the issuing body first, then the programme and subject, then the date. A genuine IB workshop record names the IB, names the subject, names the workshop category and gives a date, and what it records is attendance at professional development for teachers, which is useful but is not a tutoring qualification. If the document carries a crest and a signature but no identifiable issuer, or an official-sounding body that returns nothing when you search for it, it means nothing at all. Also check the programme matches: a Primary Years Programme workshop record does not support a claim to teach Diploma Programme Mathematics, and an IGCSE record is not a DP credential.

faqs.question: My tutor says they are IB trained. Is that the same as certified?
faqs.answer: No, and the gap between those two words is worth one polite question. IB trained is usually loose shorthand for having attended an IB professional development workshop while employed at an authorised school, which is a real and useful thing to have done. It is not a certification, it is not inspected or renewed when the teacher starts tutoring privately, and it carries no authority over a private arrangement. Ask who provided the training and in which year. A tutor who answers with a school, a subject and a date is being straight with you. A tutor who cannot name any of the three is describing something that did not happen the way they implied.

faqs.question: Does teaching at an IB school make a tutor IB certified?
faqs.answer: No. The authorisation belongs to the school, not to the individual, and it stays with the school when the teacher leaves. What a posting at an authorised IB school does give you is the single most useful checkable credential in this field: a named institution, a named subject and a set of years, all of which you can confirm with two questions and one telephone call. That is far more informative than any certificate, which is why our profiles list schools and dates rather than badges. Ask which school, which subject and which years, and ask for a colleague or former parent you can speak to briefly.

faqs.question: What qualifications should I actually ask for?
faqs.answer: Four: a degree in or close to the subject with the awarding university named, a teaching qualification such as a Bachelor of Education or a Postgraduate Certificate in Education where the tutor has one, a verifiable teaching post at a named school with the years attached, and examining or moderating work done for a board under contract if they have done any. Those four exist, are issued by identifiable bodies and can be checked. A tutoring certificate from an unnamed organisation is not on the list. Ask for the four, in that order, and accept unconfirmed as an honest answer where a tutor cannot evidence something.

faqs.question: Can a tutor with no IB school experience still teach DP well?
faqs.answer: Yes, with one condition: they must know the assessment model as well as the subject. A university-level mathematician who has never worked inside the Diploma Programme can be excellent once they have learned how the exploration is marked and how the command terms behave in a paper, and some of the strongest tutors we place came in that way. The test is not where they worked but whether they can band a script against the published criteria and explain what the next band requires. Ask them to do exactly that with a piece of your child's marked work before you commit to a weekly slot.

faqs.question: Should I really ask a tutor to mark my child's script before booking?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the most useful fifteen minutes you will spend on this decision. Cover the school's grade, hand over one recent piece, and ask which criterion is costing marks, what the next band would require and what should change in the next draft. A tutor who has genuinely taught the subject reaches for the criteria by name, points at a specific paragraph and tells you something new about work you have already read. A tutor who talks in generalities about hard work and confidence has answered you too. No certificate produces that information, and every tutor we list expects the request.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Five things, and a tutor's paperwork is not among them. Rates move on the board and the level, since Diploma Programme Higher Level work with an internal assessment attached is a heavier job than Middle Years Programme support. They move on subject scarcity, so a Spanish B or Higher Level Economics specialist sits above a Mathematics tutor. They move on travel, because an evening slot in Kharghar or Kasarvadavali costs a tutor about two hours. They move on session length and on frequency. We will not quote a figure before knowing those five, and you should be wary of anyone who does.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor reach Kasarvadavali on Ghodbunder Road for a 7pm weekday session?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and you should insist on knowing where the tutor lives before agreeing. A tutor near Thane station reaches Kasarvadavali in about twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour in the evening peak, so a 7pm start is realistic for a Thane-based tutor and fragile for anybody travelling from Mulund or the Western Suburbs. In practice we match Thane addresses to Thane tutors and keep cross-city travel for weekend mornings. If a slot that far out is the only one available, a hybrid pattern of one home session and one online session usually holds together where two home sessions will not.

faqs.question: Our building in Vashi requires a visitor gate pass. How does that work weekly?
faqs.answer: Register the tutor once with your society office as a recurring visitor rather than logging a fresh entry each week. Most Navi Mumbai and Thane complexes allow a standing weekly entry for tutors, music teachers and physiotherapists once a resident has sponsored them in writing, and some ask for an identity document copy to keep on file. Do it before the first session, not during it, because fifteen minutes lost at the gate out of a sixty-minute slot is a real cost. Also tell the tutor which gate and which tower, and whether service lifts are restricted during particular hours, which catches out newcomers in larger complexes.

faqs.question: Where should the sessions happen inside the flat, and should a parent sit in?
faqs.answer: Use the dining table or any room with a door, a hard surface and a plug, and sit in for the first ten minutes of the first session only. The dining table beats a bedroom because it discourages a child from half-lying on the bed, and a door matters more than space does in a Mumbai flat where the television and the kitchen share a wall with everything. Stay for the diagnostic opening so you hear what the tutor identifies, then leave, because a thirteen-year-old performs for an audience instead of working. Ask for a two-line message after each session instead of supervising it.

sections.heading: How IB Gram shortlists a certified IGCSE tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: An enquiry that says certified IGCSE tutor in Mumbai arrives with a great deal packed into one word. Before anything else happens, that word has to be turned into facts somebody can actually check: which board your school runs, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel, which subjects are in trouble, which year of IGCSE your child is in, which zone of the city you live in, and which evenings are genuinely free. None of that is visible in the search phrase, and all of it decides who can realistically sit at your dining table every week for a year.

The second step is availability, and with teacher-tutors it is the binding constraint, not an afterthought. A person who teaches a full school timetable is not free at four in the afternoon. They are free from roughly half past six on weekdays and for longer stretches on Saturday. They also carry their own marking weeks, their own report-writing deadlines and their own parent evenings, and those land in the same months your child's assessments land. A shortlist built without asking about this looks excellent on paper and quietly collapses around week five of the term.

The third step is checking, and it is worth being precise about what checking means here. IB Gram verifies what a tutor claims about themselves: identity, the degree they say they hold, the teaching qualification they say they hold, and the school where they say they currently teach. Verification is not certification. IB Gram does not certify anyone, no examination board certifies private tutors, and no tutor listed here is presented as approved or endorsed by Cambridge International Education, Pearson Edexcel or any school in the city. What you receive is a record of claims that somebody has actually tested.

You then get a small shortlist rather than a directory to wade through. Two or three profiles, each one carrying the subject, the board, the zone covered, the slot that can be held through a full term, and a plain description of where the teaching experience comes from. You meet one before you commit to anything. If the fit is wrong after two or three sessions you say so, and a replacement is arranged without an argument about notice periods.

sections.heading: What does certification actually mean for an IGCSE tutor?
paragraphs: Nothing issued by an examination board. Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel approve schools as examination centres and run training for teachers who work inside those schools. Neither body keeps a register of approved, licensed or certified private tutors, and neither endorses individuals who teach outside a school. Anybody who tells you otherwise is describing something that does not exist.

What does exist is a short list of things you can verify. A university degree in the subject being taught, which matters more at IGCSE than parents expect because the Extended tier moves quickly past school-level comfort. A teaching qualification issued by a university or a teacher-training institution, a Bachelor of Education or a postgraduate certificate in education or a Master of Education, which is evidence that somebody has been taught how to teach rather than simply knowing the content. And a current or recent post at a school that actually runs the syllabus your child sits. If a tutor mentions training they attended through their school, treat it as attendance at a course and nothing more. It is not a licence, it does not make anybody an approved tutor, and IB Gram will not describe it as one.

The structure a tutor has to understand is the tiering. Most IGCSE subjects split into Core and Extended, and the choice caps what is available. A student entered for Core sits an easier paper and cannot reach the top grades; a student entered for Extended sits the harder paper and risks more. That entry decision is usually made by the school on the evidence of internal results, not by the family, and a tutor who implies they can overturn it is overselling. What a good tutor can do is build the case: steady work on the Extended material so the school has a reason to move a borderline student up before entries close.

Both boards matter here because Mumbai schools split between them, and the forward link matters too. An Extended pass in Mathematics is what makes Higher Level (HL) Mathematics in the Diploma Programme (DP) survivable two years later, and a Core entry quietly closes that door. The full span of all IB and IGCSE subjects across IGCSE Years 9-11 that a tutor in Mumbai may be asked to teach runs from Additional Mathematics through to Global Perspectives, so the honest question is not whether somebody is certified but whether they have taught your specific subject through to a real final series. Parents who type best IGCSE tutor in Mumbai into a search box are asking that same question in different words.

sections.heading: Subjects, papers and the coursework a serving teacher already marks
paragraphs: A teacher who has taught a subject through to a final series has marked the same paper for a whole class in one sitting, which is a different kind of knowledge from having read the specification carefully. In Extended Mathematics they know the marks leak in the working rather than the answer, and that a student who writes only a final line is throwing away method marks they had already earned. In Physics they know the alternative-to-practical paper punishes a candidate who has never written a method in the passive voice and never drawn a results table with the units in the column header rather than beside every reading.

The pattern repeats across the subject list. In English Language the summary task is where confident writers lose most, because they rewrite the passage in their own voice instead of lifting and compressing the points the mark scheme is counting. In Economics the data-response questions reward a candidate who quotes a figure from the extract before explaining it, and give very little to the one who explains beautifully without touching the data. In Business Studies the case study work turns on applying each answer to the named firm rather than to firms in general. In Biology the extended-response questions carry command words that a student can be trained to read properly in about three sessions.

Coursework is where a teacher-tutor's instinct can mislead, and it is worth naming. Several IGCSE subjects offer a coursework route alongside a written alternative, and the choice is made by the school, not the candidate. A teacher who runs the coursework route at their own school will reach for it by default and may assume your child's school does the same. Ask in the first session which route your school has entered for, and bring the school's own assessment calendar so the tutor plans against your deadlines rather than theirs.

Across all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai is asked to cover, the sensible arrangement is one tutor for the sciences or one for the languages rather than one person claiming everything. Families who want all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Mumbai to sit under a single tutor usually end up with somebody strong in two subjects and thin in the rest, and the thin subjects are the ones that cost the grade.

sections.heading: IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai: six zones and who actually travels where
paragraphs: Mumbai, Maharashtra is six working zones for tutoring purposes, and a teacher-tutor is constrained twice over: once by where they live and once by where they teach. In South Mumbai, families in Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Walkeshwar, Peddar Road, Tardeo and Fort are matched inside the island, because a tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers a short distance and still loses most of an hour to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals at seven in the evening. The Coastal Road has changed the northbound run more than the southbound one. Metro Line 3 between Cuffe Parade and the Bandra Kurla Complex has changed it again for anybody who teaches in BKC by day.

The Western Suburbs run north to south along the Western Line and the Western Express Highway, which makes matching along the line sensible and matching across it painful. Bandra to Khar West to Santacruz works. Malad to Kandivali to Borivali to Dahisar works. Juhu, Andheri and Goregaon East sit in the middle and are served by Metro Line 1 and by Metro Lines 2A and 7 along the highway. A teacher who finishes the school day in Juhu will take a Santacruz or Khar West slot at seven and will not take a Dahisar one.

The Central Suburbs sit on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off the Jogeshwari Vikhroli Link Road in between. Powai has no station of its own, so tutors arrive by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, and the Santacruz Chembur Link Road is what makes a Kurla or Ghatkopar tutor reachable from the western side at all. The Eastern Suburbs run from Chembur and Govandi through Wadala, Vikhroli and Bhandup up to Mulund, and the Eastern Freeway makes South Mumbai far closer to Chembur than the map suggests.

Navi Mumbai is planned in nodes, so Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are matched node to node along Palm Beach Road and the Sion Panvel Highway; the Atal Setu has shortened the island crossing but a weekday evening lesson pulled across the creek still rarely survives a full term. Thane spreads from the station east along Pokhran Road, Majiwada and Ghodbunder Road out to Kasarvadavali, and that Ghodbunder stretch sets the schedule more than any other road in the city. A search for IGCSE tutors near me in Mumbai is really a search for somebody inside one of these six pockets, because distance here is measured in minutes at 7pm, not kilometres.

sections.heading: The Mumbai school calendar a teacher-tutor is already living inside
paragraphs: The reason a serving teacher understands your child's year is that they are living the same calendar, and the reason they sometimes cannot help in the week you need them most is exactly the same. Mumbai international schools cluster their pressure points. Internal assessments and coursework drafts land from late August through September. The first full mock series runs across the turn of the year. Final coursework submission and the second mocks fall in February and early March. Then the May and June series arrives and everything stops. A teacher-tutor's own school is doing all of that at the same time, with their own marking piled on top.

Families here deal with a wide spread of calendars. Children at Dhirubhai Ambani International School and Ascend International School in the Bandra Kurla Complex, at Ecole Mondiale World School, Jamnabai Narsee International School and Utpal Shanghvi Global School in Juhu, at Oberoi International School off the Jogeshwari Vikhroli Link Road, at Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, at Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, at B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade, at Bombay International School near Babulnath, at Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo, at NES International School in Mulund West, at the JBCN International School campuses in Parel, Borivali, Oshiwara and Chembur, at Thakur International School in Kandivali East, at Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and at D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul all work to timetables that differ by weeks.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page. Schools are listed here because their calendars are the pressure points a Mumbai family actually plans around, not because any arrangement exists between them and IB Gram. No school has approved, endorsed or recommended any tutor listed here, and a tutor who happens to teach at one of these schools is engaged with you privately, in their own time, with no involvement from their employer whatsoever.

The practical consequence is scheduling. Book the hardest subject into the slot that survives the February crunch, not the slot that is convenient in July. Ask any teacher-tutor, in the first conversation, which weeks of the year their own school will take them out of circulation, and build the plan around those weeks rather than discovering them in the middle of mock season.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid with a working school teacher?
paragraphs: Home tuition first, because it is what nearly everybody searching certified IGCSE tutor in Mumbai actually wants, and because for a fifteen-year-old sitting at a shared dining table it is the format with the fewest escape routes. A tutor in the room sees the page, sees the handwriting, sees the moment the student stops following and does not say so. Those three signals are the whole value of the hour. Home tuition also fixes the time, which matters more than parents expect, because a standing Tuesday at seven becomes part of the week rather than a thing that gets negotiated every Sunday.

The honest cost of home tuition with a serving teacher is their travel, and it shows up as a narrower choice of slot rather than as a worse tutor. A teacher who finishes in Andheri East cannot be in Nerul by half past six, so the pool for a Navi Mumbai family is the pool of teachers who live or work in Navi Mumbai. That is not a defect; it is the reason node-to-node matching holds for a full term while a glamorous cross-city match does not.

Online is the right answer in three specific situations and the wrong answer elsewhere. It is right when the subject is scarce, because an IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai can be the only person within reach who has actually taught Additional Mathematics or Economics to a final series. It is right during the monsoon, when the alternative is a cancelled session. It is right for short, frequent check-ins in the fortnight before a paper, where twenty focused minutes on one past question beats a cancelled ninety. It is weaker for a student who needs somebody physically present to stay on the page, and weaker for anything involving long handwritten working, unless the family is willing to photograph and send the script beforehand.

Hybrid is what most teacher-tutor arrangements settle into by the second term. One longer session at home each week for teaching and marked work, plus a short online slot for a question set or a doubt-clearing call. It also absorbs the February crunch gracefully: when the tutor's own school swallows a week, the home session moves online rather than disappearing, and the thread of the term is not broken.

sections.heading: How do you politely verify a teaching post in Mumbai?
paragraphs: You ask the tutor directly, in the first conversation, and you ask for specifics rather than a yes. Which school, which board, which year groups, which subjects, and for how long. A teacher who genuinely holds the post answers all five in a sentence without hesitating, because it is simply their job. Somebody who has taught one year of Year 9 Science as a substitute will usually say so when the question is specific enough to make vagueness obvious. That one exchange does more than any badge, and a certified IGCSE tutor in Mumbai, in the only sense that word honestly carries, is a tutor who answers it cleanly.

Three further checks cost nothing. Many Mumbai school websites publish a faculty page, so a name is often confirmable in thirty seconds. A professional profile that lists the post with dates is a second source. And an email from a school address, if the tutor is willing to send one, settles it entirely. If a tutor declines any of these, accept the decline gracefully and weigh it; plenty of teachers are private about outside work and that is a reasonable position, not a red flag on its own.

There is one check you should not perform. Do not telephone the school's front desk to ask whether a named teacher tutors privately. Many schools restrict or regulate outside tutoring, and an unsolicited call from a parent can create a problem for somebody who has done nothing wrong. Verify with the tutor, not around them. IB Gram's own checks work the same way: we ask the tutor, we look at documents they provide, and we record what was and was not confirmed. We do not represent any tutor as certified, and we do not contact a teacher's employer.

What this verification does not give you is authority. Confirming that somebody teaches at a reputable school tells you they know the specification and have marked real scripts. It tells you nothing about whether they are patient with a frustrated fifteen-year-old, whether they can explain a thing a second way when the first way fails, or whether they will mark the work they set. Those only show up in the first two sessions, which is exactly why you meet before you commit. An IGCSE private tutor in Mumbai who is excellent with a confident student can be the wrong choice for an anxious one.

sections.heading: The conflict of interest: when a teacher must not tutor your child
paragraphs: A teacher should not privately tutor a student they also teach and assess at school. This is the one hard line in the whole subject, and it is worth stating plainly because families ask for exactly this arrangement more often than any other. The reasoning is not about effort or ethics in the abstract. It is that the same person would be setting the work, marking the internal assessments, authenticating the coursework as the candidate's own and contributing to the predicted grade, while being paid by the family whose child those judgements land on. No amount of personal integrity removes the structural problem, and the student's own classmates can reasonably ask why one of them has private access to the person holding the pen.

This is the school's rule to make and the school's rule to enforce. Most Mumbai international schools have a written policy on it, usually requiring teachers to declare outside tutoring and prohibiting it with their own students. A family's part is simply not to ask. If your child's own subject teacher is the person you want, the respectful move is to ask them to recommend somebody rather than to take the work themselves. Good teachers usually have two names ready, because colleagues at other schools ask them the same question.

What you want instead is a teacher from a different school who teaches the same board and the same subject. That arrangement keeps everything useful and removes everything compromised. They know the specification, they have marked real cohorts, they know how the paper behaves and where the examiner is strict. They have no authority over your child's grade, no access to your child's school's confidential material, and no reason to soften an assessment. The feedback you get is the feedback the work deserves, which is the entire point of paying for it.

Ask a teacher-tutor from another school four things. Which board does your school run, and is it the same as ours? Have you taught this subject to a final series, or only up to Year 10? Will you mark written work between sessions, and how will I see that marking? And will you tell me plainly when my child is not working, even if that is uncomfortable? Those four answers predict the next twelve months better than any credential. Note also what such a tutor cannot do: they do not know your school's internal exam, they cannot see your child's predicted grade, and their own school's deadlines are irrelevant to you.

sections.heading: What progress looks like, and what nobody can promise
paragraphs: At four weeks you should see process, not marks. The student is bringing the right past questions to the session rather than whichever worksheet was nearest. Working is being written down. The tutor is setting something between sessions and returning it marked against the actual criteria. If none of that has happened after four weeks, the problem is the arrangement, not the child, and it is the right moment to say so rather than to wait politely until the term ends.

At one term, expect the scores on topics that were specifically worked on to move, and expect the untouched topics to sit still. That asymmetry is the honest signature of real tutoring; a uniform lift across everything usually means an easier paper rather than a better student. At one full exam cycle, from the first mocks through to the final series, a student who has worked consistently with a competent tutor generally moves, sometimes substantially. Nobody can tell you by how much, and the reason is that the student's own effort between sessions accounts for more of the result than the tutor does.

So the limits should be said out loud. IB Gram does not guarantee grades. No tutor here, however experienced, can promise a particular IGCSE grade, and anybody in this city who offers that promise in writing is selling something they cannot deliver. A tutor controls the quality of the explanation, the quality of the practice and the quality of the marking. They do not control how much work happens in the other six days of the week, how the final paper is set, or how a student performs on a bad morning in May.

The replacement question deserves a straight answer too, because it is the thing families most dread raising. If a tutor is not working out, you say so and a different tutor is matched. There is no penalty, no required notice period beyond the courtesy of telling the tutor, and no implication that you have done something wrong. Three sessions is usually enough to know. What IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on is a separate question and sits on its own page; here the only relevant point is that no arrangement locks you in.
bullets: Four weeks: process changes, marked work comes back, past questions appear
One term: worked topics move while untouched topics stay where they were

sections.heading: Booking a first IGCSE home tutor session in Mumbai
paragraphs: Prepare four things before the first session and the hour will not be wasted on admin. The most recent marked school assessment, including the teacher's comments, because that is the fastest honest read on where the marks are leaking. The school's assessment calendar for the term, so the tutor plans against your deadlines. The subject's syllabus or the school's topic list, confirming the board and whether the entry is Core or Extended. And a short, blunt note from you about what is actually going wrong, which is often different from what the report says.

The first session itself is diagnostic, and a good teacher-tutor will spend most of it watching your child work rather than talking. Expect them to put a past question in front of the student within the first twenty minutes and to say very little while it is attempted. What they are looking for is where the process breaks: reading the command word, setting the work out, knowing the content, managing the time. By the end they should be able to tell you which of those four is the real problem, and that one sentence is what you are paying for in session one.

Set up the practical side at the same time. Agree the standing slot and name the fallback if a session is missed. Agree a study space that is not the family television room, with a table, a chair at the right height and a plug. Tell the society gate how the tutor should be cleared each week, because a tutor arguing with security for ten minutes loses ten minutes of a ninety-minute session, every week. And agree how you will hear from the tutor: a short message after each session beats a long one at the end of the month.

After that, review at four weeks and again at the end of the term. Ask to see the marked work rather than asking how it is going, because the marked work answers the question and the conversation does not. An IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai who is doing the job properly will welcome that; one who deflects it is telling you something useful.

Have the term's assessment calendar and the Core or Extended entry confirmed

faqs.question: Is there such a thing as a Cambridge-certified or Edexcel-certified IGCSE tutor?
faqs.answer: No. Neither Cambridge International Education nor Pearson Edexcel certifies, licenses, approves or registers private tutors, in Mumbai or anywhere else. Both bodies approve schools as examination centres and run professional development for teachers employed by those schools, which is a different thing entirely. If a tutor or an agency describes somebody as board-certified, they are using a word that has no issuing authority behind it. IB Gram does not describe any tutor as certified or endorsed by a board. What can genuinely be checked is a subject degree, a teaching qualification from a university, and a current or recent post teaching that syllabus at a school.

faqs.question: Is a serving school teacher always a better tutor than a full-time private tutor?
faqs.answer: No, and the trade-off is worth understanding before you choose. A serving teacher brings current specification knowledge, experience marking whole cohorts and a feel for how the paper behaves, which is genuinely hard to acquire any other way. A full-time private tutor brings availability, flexibility in the exam term and, often, more practice at teaching one student rather than a class. The teacher is usually the stronger choice for a student who needs the paper decoded. The full-time tutor is often better for a student who needs frequent short sessions or help at awkward hours, because a teacher's free window is narrow and fixed.

faqs.question: Can my child's own subject teacher tutor them privately at home?
faqs.answer: They should not, and you should not ask. A teacher who also teaches and assesses your child at school would be marking internal assessments, authenticating coursework and contributing to a predicted grade for a student whose family pays them privately. Most Mumbai international schools prohibit exactly this and require teachers to declare outside tutoring, so asking puts the teacher in a difficult position. The better move is to ask that teacher to recommend a colleague at another school. You keep the expertise and lose the conflict, and your child's school assessments stay clean of any question about whose judgement produced them.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor really teaches where they say, without being rude?
faqs.answer: Ask them directly and ask for detail: which school, which board, which year groups, which subjects and for how long. Genuine teachers answer in one unhurried sentence because it is simply their job. Beyond that, many Mumbai school websites publish faculty pages, and a dated professional profile is a second source. An email sent from a school address settles it. What you should not do is telephone the school to check up on them, because outside tutoring is regulated at many schools and an unsolicited parent call can create trouble for someone who has done nothing wrong. Verify with the tutor, not around them.

faqs.question: A teacher-tutor can only offer 7.30pm on a weekday in Andheri. Does that actually work?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided you protect it rather than treat it as the leftover slot. A 7.30pm start in Andheri or Goregaon East is normal for a teacher who finishes a school day and crosses the Western Express Highway in evening traffic, and a ninety-minute session ending at nine is manageable for most Year 10 and Year 11 students. What breaks it is dinner, a younger sibling's bedtime and a television in the same room. Fix the study space, eat before the tutor arrives, and keep the slot the same every week. A late fixed slot beats an early slot that moves.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home while the session runs?
faqs.answer: Not in the room, and usually not in the house for the whole session, but somebody should be present at least for the first few weeks. Being in the flat without hovering is the right posture: the student works without an audience, and you are available if something needs settling. For a first session with a new tutor, stay for the opening ten minutes and the closing five so you hear the diagnosis directly. After the arrangement has settled, many Mumbai families leave a grandparent or house help at home and take the tutor's written update after each session instead.

faqs.question: Our school runs one board and the tutor teaches at a school running the other. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It can be, and it is worth checking before the first session rather than discovering it in February. Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel cover similar content at IGCSE but differ in paper structure, command-word conventions, coursework options and tiering detail. A strong teacher crosses between them with a few weeks of reading; a teacher who has only ever taught one board and assumes they are interchangeable will teach your child the wrong exam technique. Ask directly whether they have taught your board to a final series. If the answer is no, ask what they will do about it.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after three sessions?
faqs.answer: You tell us and we match somebody else. There is no penalty and no notice period beyond the courtesy of telling the tutor, and no explanation is required beyond what you want to give. Three sessions is normally enough to know, because by then you can see whether work is being set, marked and returned, and whether your child is talking during the hour or nodding. Say it early rather than waiting for the term to end out of politeness. A wasted term is far more expensive than an awkward message, and tutors who do this work professionally expect that some matches will not fit.

faqs.question: We live in Worli and the right subject specialist lives in Thane. Should we go online?
faqs.answer: Yes, in that specific case online is the sensible answer rather than a compromise. A tutor travelling from Thane to Worli on a weekday evening crosses the Eastern Express Highway and the whole city, and even a willing teacher will not sustain it past a few weeks. An IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai is the better arrangement when the subject is scarce enough that the nearest genuine specialist sits in another zone. Consider a hybrid instead: one longer weekend session at home when the traffic is tolerable, and shorter online sessions midweek. That usually holds for a full term where a weekday cross-city drive does not.

faqs.question: Our child studies at an IGCSE school in Navi Mumbai. Can a tutor come across from the island?
faqs.answer: They can, but it rarely survives a full term, so it should be the second choice rather than the first. The Atal Setu and the Sion Panvel Highway have genuinely shortened the crossing, yet a weekday evening run from South Mumbai to Nerul, Kharghar or Belapur still consumes more of a teacher's evening than the lesson does. Navi Mumbai families are better served node to node along Palm Beach Road: a Vashi tutor for a Nerul family, a Kharghar tutor for a Panvel family. If the subject is scarce enough that nobody in the nodes teaches it, go online rather than importing a tutor across the creek.

faqs.question: Will a teacher-tutor know what is coming up in our school's internal exam?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be wary of any tutor who hints otherwise. A teacher at a different school has no access to your school's internal papers, question banks, moderation decisions or predicted grades, and a teacher at your own school should not be tutoring your child at all. What a good teacher-tutor does know is how the external IGCSE paper behaves, which topics carry the most marks and which command words trip students up, and that knowledge transfers to internal exams because most schools build internals from past external material. Expect preparation on the specification, never a preview of the paper.

faqs.question: Should we tell our child's school that we have engaged a private tutor?
faqs.answer: You are not obliged to, but it usually helps to mention it to the subject teacher. Most Mumbai schools react well, and the subject teacher can tell your tutor which topics are being covered next and where the class is weak, which saves the tutor a fortnight of working it out. It also prevents the awkward situation where a tutor teaches a method the school does not use. The one thing to avoid is presenting the tutor as a correction of the school. Frame it as extra support at home and the conversation stays useful for everyone involved.

sections.heading: How does IB Gram find an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Chandivali who can actually reach you?
paragraphs: We ask which end of Saki Vihar Road you live at before we ask anything else. A request for an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Chandivali almost always arrives with the subject, the board and a preferred time, and without the one detail that decides whether the arrangement survives past week five: where on the Chandivali–Saki Vihar Road stretch you are, and which direction a tutor would drive in from. Chandivali has no railway station of its own and one real approach road. A tutor based at the Andheri East end and a tutor based at the Powai end are not interchangeable, however similar their subject history reads on paper.

So the shortlist gets built in a fixed order. 1. You give us the board, the year group, the subjects and your nearest landmark on Saki Vihar Road. 2. We filter for tutors who already teach on your side of that road, because someone with an existing lesson in the same pocket has a route that works and a reason to protect it. 3. We test your preferred time against the 6.30pm crush and offer a 5pm start or an 8pm start rather than pretending a 7pm start is realistic. 4. You receive two or three profiles, each one carrying the approach side the tutor comes from, the papers and components they have taught, and the evenings they can genuinely hold. 5. You choose one and we fix a paid trial session at your home. 6. After the trial you either confirm the standing weekly slot or tell us exactly what did not work, and we re-shortlist from the same pool.

What we avoid is sending the first available name and letting the traffic sort it out. That is how a family in Chandivali ends up on their third tutor by December, and it happens here more than almost anywhere else in Mumbai. A tutor who has to fight the Saki Vihar queue twice a week starts arriving late in week three, starts rescheduling in week five, and is gone by the time the mock papers land. The filter on approach side is not a nicety; it is the difference between a weekly slot that holds for a full academic year and one that quietly dissolves.

Parents often ask for three subjects when the real problem is one teacher-facing component in one of them, and a single tutor working two evenings is both cheaper and more effective than three tutors competing for the same two usable hours in your week. We would rather start narrow and widen in January than fill your calendar in August and have your child burn out before the first mock.

sections.heading: PYP, MYP, DP and IGCSE: what Chandivali families are choosing between
paragraphs: Chandivali sits between two different school pathways, and that shapes what tuition here looks like more than it does in most of Mumbai. Families on this stretch mostly send children either to Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, which runs Cambridge IGCSE and then the International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (DP), or to Bombay Cambridge International School, which runs the Cambridge IGCSE route. So the typical Chandivali household is not inside one programme for twelve years. It is doing a Cambridge International Education curriculum to Year 11 and then making a decision about Years 12 and 13.

The four structures a tutor here has to hold in their head are the Primary Years Programme (PYP), the Middle Years Programme (MYP), the Diploma Programme (DP) and IGCSE. PYP is inquiry-led with no external papers, so tuition at that stage is about reading fluency, number sense and the habit of explaining a method out loud. MYP runs on published criteria rather than marks out of a hundred, and the work in Years 9 and 10 is teaching a child to read the criterion descriptor and write to it. IGCSE, whether Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel, is the first point where a timed external paper decides the grade. DP adds Higher Level and Standard Level choices, Internal Assessment in every subject, the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) on top of six subjects.

The expensive mistake we see in this pocket is treating the MYP-to-IGCSE or IGCSE-to-DP change as a continuation. A child who scored well on MYP criteria can walk into an IGCSE Extended paper and lose marks purely on exam technique, because nobody taught them that an examiner awards method marks for a line of working they had been leaving out. A child who sailed through IGCSE can reach DP1 and discover that a Higher Level subject is not harder IGCSE but a different kind of reasoning with a coursework component attached.

When you write to us, name the programme and the year, and name the transition if one is coming. A tutor who has taken students through the IGCSE-to-DP step in Mumbai schools will spend the first fortnight on the shape of the new assessment rather than on content the child already has, and that is usually where the time is best spent.

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL, and Core versus Extended across both boards
paragraphs: All IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Chandivali may be asked to cover come with their own internal assessment, and the decisions about level and tier are usually made before anyone has looked at what that assessment actually demands. At IGCSE, Cambridge splits several subjects into Core and Extended, and the two tiers do not reach the same grades: the Core tier is capped well below the top of the scale, so a Year 10 entry decision quietly sets a ceiling on a Year 11 result. At DP, the Higher Level and Standard Level split changes both the content and the coursework load, and HL in three subjects plus the Extended Essay is a different working week from HL in three subjects where one of them is a strength.

Here is a worked example of the kind of thing a tutor earns their fee on. Take the DP Group 4 scientific investigation, the single piece of coursework a Physics, Chemistry or Biology student submits. It is marked on Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation. Most students lose their marks in Research design, and they lose them in the first week, before any data exists, by choosing a question with one controllable variable and no realistic way to measure it in a school lab. A DP1 student in Chandivali who brings a draft research question to a 5pm Tuesday session in early September can have that fixed in one sitting. The same student bringing a finished write-up in February cannot, because the data is already collected against a weak design and there is no time to repeat it.

The IGCSE equivalent is the tier conversation. A Year 9 student who is comfortable with algebraic manipulation but slow with it is often moved to Core for safety, when what they needed was six weeks of speed work and a method-marks habit. A tutor who has marked Extended papers can look at two of your child's school tests and tell you which of those two situations you are in. That judgement is worth more than an extra session a week.

We also expect a tutor to be honest about what they do not teach. A Mathematics specialist who has never supervised a DP Economics Internal Assessment should say so, and we will put a second tutor on that one component for a short block rather than stretch the first one across a subject they will fake their way through.
