sections.heading: Which subjects can a Dadar family actually get in person?
paragraphs: Nearly all of them, which is not true everywhere on the island. Parents ask for all IB and IGCSE subjects, and a home tutor in Dadar can cover more of that list face to face than one working an address further south. The routine requests are Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Economics, Business Management and English, and those are available across South Mumbai. What makes Dadar different is the second tier: Mandarin B, Music, Philosophy, Psychology, Global Politics, Design Technology and French ab initio.

No single home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects exists in Mumbai, so subject choice carries assessment weight that parents rarely see on the school timetable. Every DP subject has an internal assessment marked by the school and moderated by the IB: a scientific investigation in Chemistry and Physics, an exploration in Mathematics, a commentary in Economics, an individual oral in every Language B. IGCSE sits fewer internal pieces and more written papers, and the Extended tier in Mathematics (0580) includes a paper answered without a calculator, which is where a surprising share of lost marks sit.

Take the Mandarin B individual oral, a component that starts from a visual stimulus linked to one of the prescribed themes. The child has to describe the image, connect it to the theme, then hold a conversation about it in Mandarin under time pressure. Nothing about that is revisable from a textbook. It needs a person in the room asking the follow-up question the child was not ready for, twice a month, with printed stimuli on the dining table. Over a screen, with lag and a shared document, the same practice loses most of its value and the student learns to recite instead.
bullets: Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Economics and English across both boards
Mandarin B, Music, Philosophy and Global Politics available as home classes
Every DP subject carries an internal assessment the school marks first
IGCSE Extended Mathematics includes a paper answered without a calculator

sections.heading: Dadar Parsi Colony, Matunga and Prabhadevi: what one Dadar home tutor covers in a week
paragraphs: A tutor who takes a Dadar slot will usually take Dadar Parsi Colony, Matunga and Prabhadevi in the same week, because all three sit within a walk or one short auto ride of Dadar station. That is how a tutor builds a workable evening: two sittings close together rather than one lesson and an hour of travel. Dadar sits in the middle of the island city of Mumbai, Maharashtra, roughly equidistant from Churchgate and Bandra, and the areas around it share one tutor pool rather than three.

South Mumbai is dense and short-distance but slow. A tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers eight kilometres and can still lose forty minutes to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak, which is why tutors in this part of the city are normally matched within the island rather than brought down from the suburbs. Dadar is the exception the railway created: the tutor is not fighting the Coastal Road or the Western Express Highway, and is not waiting at a signal. They get off a train at your station.

Prabhadevi lies between Dadar and Worli and is reached from the same station, so a tutor with a six o'clock in Prabhadevi can hold a seven-thirty in Dadar without a dead hour between them. Going the other way is harder. A Dadar tutor asked to add Cuffe Parade or Nariman Point to the same evening will quietly stop taking the second slot after a month. A single tutor rarely covers all IB and IGCSE subjects though home classes in Dadar reach further down the subject list than anywhere else on the island, and keeping a tutor's evening geographically tight is most of the craft of home tuition in Mumbai.
bullets: Dadar Parsi Colony: a short auto ride, the same tutor pool
Matunga sits one stop away and shares the Dadar evening
Prabhadevi pairs with a later Dadar slot in one evening
Metro Line 3 brings BKC and Worli tutors within reach

sections.heading: The Dadar school calendar: Don Bosco International School and JBCN International School, Parel
paragraphs: Families here commonly send children to Don Bosco International School in Matunga and JBCN International School, Parel, and both run on the same Mumbai academic year: a June start, a first reporting round before the Diwali break, mocks around the turn of the year, and final assessment in the April to May window. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Don Bosco International School, JBCN International School, Parel, or any other school named on this page. The schools appear here as local context, because their calendars decide when a tutor is actually needed.

The pressure points are predictable enough to plan around. August and September are quiet and are the cheapest weeks to start, because a good tutor is still free at your preferred hour. October brings the first MYP criterion-marked tasks and the IGCSE class tests that make parents search in the first place. January and February are the hardest stretch of the Mumbai school year: DP2 internal assessment deadlines, the extended essay final version and TOK essay drafts collide inside a fortnight, and every family in the building wants the same seven o'clock. By March the pool is thin.

The other calendar that matters is the IGCSE series. Most children here sit the May to June series, some take the October to November one, and a resit decision made in August is a very different conversation from the same decision made in December. A Dadar family whose child finishes IGCSE in May and begins DP1 in June has roughly five free weeks between the two, and that is the single best window for the bridging work almost nobody books: mathematical notation, lab write-ups at DP standard, and essay structure that no longer rewards a five-paragraph answer.

August and September: the easiest weeks to secure an evening slot
January and February: DP2 IA, EE and TOK deadlines overlap
IGCSE May to June series, with an October to November option

sections.heading: Home tuition in Dadar, online classes, or a mix of both?
paragraphs: Home tutoring is the default here and it should be. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Dadar arrives at a fixed hour, works at the table your child already studies at, and sees the things a screen hides: the unopened textbook, the phone face up, the notes that stop in September. Because the station makes the address reachable, a home slot in Dadar survives a full term far more often than one in the far south of Mumbai, where the tutor quietly gives up the travel by November and the family starts again.

Online is not a lesser option, it is a different one. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Dadar is the right answer for a scarce HL subject where the only real specialist lives in Pune or Bengaluru, for a child who revises at ten at night, and for the fortnight your family is travelling. The trade-offs are honest ones: a younger child drifts without an adult beside them, diagram-heavy Physics and Chemistry work is slower over a shared screen, and no software fixes a weak internet evening in an older building with tired wiring.

Most families here end up with a mix without planning it. One in-person session a week for the teaching, a short online check closer to a deadline, and an online-only arrangement for the one subject nobody can supply in person. A DP2 student with a Chemistry investigation due can get the practical reasoning at home on Tuesday and a twenty-minute screen share on Saturday morning to fix the data analysis. Ask any tutor which mode they prefer and why: a tutor who says home classes suit a Year 9 and online suits a DP2 is telling you they have taught both.
bullets: Home tuition first: a fixed hour, your table, no travel for the child
Online suits scarce HL subjects and late-night DP revision
Hybrid: in-person teaching weekly, a short online check before deadlines
Younger children almost always need a person in the room

sections.heading: How is an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Dadar checked before you meet them?
paragraphs: Before a tutor reaches a Dadar shortlist we check identity, qualification and teaching history, and we ask for the thing that actually predicts the work: which board, which syllabus version and which components they have taught or marked. A graduate degree in Physics is not evidence that someone can supervise a DP internal assessment. Having supervised one, or marked one, is. We also ask for references from families who used them for a full term rather than a trial, because a tutor who is excellent for three sessions and unreliable by week eight is a known pattern.

Then there is the part only you can do. In the first session, ask the tutor to name the assessment objectives for the paper your child is sitting, and ask what they would do differently for Core and for Extended. Ask who writes the practice questions. Ask what happens if your child is ill on a Thursday. A good IB and IGCSE private tutor in Dadar answers all of that flatly and without a pitch. Then check the ordinary things: that they arrive on time twice running, and that your child can tell you what they did last week.

Verification is a filter, not a prediction. It removes the people who cannot do the job, and it cannot tell you whether one particular tutor and one particular fourteen-year-old will get along. That is why the shortlist stays at two or three names and why a replacement is a short conversation. If a parent types IB and IGCSE tutor near me in Dadar into Google, the only question worth asking of whatever comes back is what the platform checks and what it leaves to you. Anyone unwilling to answer that in plain words is answering it already.
bullets: Identity, degree and teaching history checked before any shortlist
Syllabus-version specific: which components they have taught or marked
References from families who used the tutor a full term
Ask the tutor to name the assessment objectives for the paper
A replacement is a conversation, not a renegotiation

sections.heading: Why the Dadar interchange gets you subjects a Colaba family cannot get in person
paragraphs: Dadar is where the Western and Central lines cross, and that one fact changes which tutors say yes. A tutor living in Borivali, Vile Parle or Virar is on the Western Line. A tutor in Mulund, Ghatkopar, Kurla or Thane is on the Central Line. Both reach the Dadar interchange without changing trains, and the walk at the far end is short. Ask either of them to teach in Colaba or on Malabar Hill and the journey gains a change plus a taxi through evening traffic, and the answer comes back as a polite no.

The consequence shows up in subject coverage, not in price. Common subjects are available everywhere in Mumbai. Scarce ones are not. There are few Mandarin B teachers in Mumbai, fewer Music specialists who know the DP course well, and the Philosophy and Global Politics tutors can be counted on your fingers. Those people will not spend ninety minutes each way for one lesson, and they will travel twenty minutes on a train that stops where they are going. So a Dadar shortlist for a scarce subject is drawn from the whole of Mumbai, while a Cuffe Parade shortlist for the same subject is drawn from the island and often comes back empty.

A worked case. A DP1 student in Dadar takes Mandarin B and needs the individual oral practised with someone fluent. The tutor who fits lives near Mulund on the Central Line. For a Dadar address that is one train and a short walk, so a Thursday seven o'clock holds week after week for a year. The same family living in Colaba would be offered that tutor online only, and the oral, which turns on an unscripted follow-up question about a visual stimulus, is precisely the component that online practice serves worst. That is the whole argument for this address in one paragraph.

The same logic applies to Higher Level coverage inside ordinary subjects. Economics HL Paper 3, the policy paper, needs someone who has taught HL rather than SL and has marked the quantitative answers. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL needs a tutor comfortable with the proof and calculus questions, not a general Maths teacher. Those tutors exist in smaller numbers than their SL equivalents, and they cluster where travel costs them the least time. In Dadar you compete for them with fewer constraints than at any other address on the island.

sections.heading: What should four weeks of Dadar home tuition actually have changed?
paragraphs: At four weeks you should see process, not marks. The child knows what the tutor will ask at the start of the hour, brings the right folder without being told, and can say what they got wrong last time. Homework is attempted before it is explained. That is the honest four-week deliverable, and a tutor promising a grade jump in a month is selling something. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and no tutor can, because the paper, the moderation and the day itself sit outside anyone's control.

At one term you should see marks move on school assessments and a visible change in whatever was weakest: the six-mark answers, the lab conclusions, the unseen comprehension. At one full exam cycle the gains compound, mostly because the child has stopped losing marks on things that were never about understanding at all. Command terms read carelessly. Method not shown. A graph without units. A conclusion that repeats the results. Those are the quiet grade thieves that any IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai should be hunting from the first session onward.

What should worry you is the absence of a diagnosis. If after a month the tutor cannot name two specific weaknesses and say what is being done about each, change the tutor rather than the subject. If the sessions have drifted into homework supervision, say so directly and early. Families in Dadar sometimes keep a tutor out of politeness because the person travels a long way to reach them, which is exactly the wrong reason to stay, and the interchange means the replacement will travel just as easily on the same evening.
bullets: Four weeks: preparation and process, not a grade jump
One term: school marks move on the weakest component
One exam cycle: fewer marks lost to method and command terms
No named diagnosis after a month means change the tutor
Progress is not guaranteed and no honest tutor promises it

sections.heading: What to have ready before the first session in Dadar
paragraphs: Getting started takes one message and about ten minutes of preparation. Have four things to hand: the board and year group, the subject and level, the last two marked assessments, and the two evening windows that genuinely work at home. If you know the paper codes, send them. If you do not, the school report usually carries them. That is enough for us to build a shortlist of an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Dadar who already teaches the syllabus version your child is sitting this year.

Set the room up once and it stops being a weekly argument. A table rather than a bed, a chair with a back, the phone in another room, and a plug point the tutor can reach for a laptop. Tell the society office that the same person comes every Tuesday at seven and ask whether a standing visitor entry can be recorded, because five minutes lost at the gate each week is five minutes taken out of the lesson. In the older buildings around Dadar, check the lift before agreeing a time with a tutor carrying files.

The first session is diagnostic. Expect the tutor to spend most of it reading your child's work rather than teaching, and expect a short summary afterwards of what they found. Ask for that summary in writing. After three sessions you will know whether to continue, and if the answer is no, tell us and we re-match from the same shortlist. Starting one subject properly beats starting three badly, and starting three badly is the most common mistake families make in this part of Mumbai in October.
bullets: Board, year group, subject and level in the first message
Two marked assessments the tutor can read before teaching
Two evening windows that genuinely work for your household
A standing gate entry saves five minutes of every lesson
Start one subject properly rather than three at once

faqs.question: How much does an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Dadar cost?
faqs.answer: It depends on five things, and any platform quoting one number before knowing them is guessing. IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Dadar move with the board and level, since DP Higher Level costs more than MYP work; with subject scarcity, because a Mandarin B or Music specialist prices differently from a Mathematics tutor; with session length; with how far the tutor travels to reach you; and with how close you are to an exam window. Dadar's position on the interchange tends to keep the travel component low, which is one of the few places a family here genuinely saves money. We give you a range for your exact request before you speak to anyone.

faqs.question: Can a tutor really reach our flat in Dadar on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and more reliably than almost anywhere else in Mumbai. A tutor coming off the Western or Central Line walks or takes a short auto from the station, so the seven o'clock does not depend on road traffic the way a Peddar Road or Haji Ali crossing does. The honest caveat is the monsoon. In heavy July rain the trains are the last thing to stop but they do slow down, so agree with the tutor in advance what happens to a delayed session: whether it moves online that evening or shifts to the weekend. Settle that in week one, not in the middle of a downpour.

faqs.question: Does the building gate and visitor pass process cause problems for a weekly slot?
faqs.answer: Rarely, if you set it up once. Tell your society office or the watchman that the same tutor comes on the same day at the same time, and ask whether they can record a standing entry rather than issuing a fresh pass every week. In the older buildings around Dadar the bigger nuisance is the lift rather than the gate. Give the tutor your flat number, the wing and a landline or alternate number, because mobile signal inside some of the older stone buildings here is poor and a tutor standing in the lobby unable to call you loses ten minutes of the hour.

faqs.question: Can you find a tutor for a scarce subject like Mandarin B, Music or Philosophy?
faqs.answer: In Dadar, usually yes, and that is the honest reason this page exists. Because the Western and Central lines cross at the station, a specialist living in Mulund, Thane or Borivali can take a Dadar slot on a single train, which the same person will not do for an address further south. Mandarin B, Music, Philosophy, Global Politics and Design Technology come up here as home classes rather than online-only arrangements. Allow a little longer for the match, usually a week rather than two days, because the pool for these subjects across Mumbai is small and the good ones are already teaching somewhere on a Tuesday.

faqs.question: Does online tuition really work for IB and IGCSE subjects?
faqs.answer: For some subjects and some ages, yes. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Dadar works well for DP essay subjects, for exam technique, for a late revision slot and for a specialist who lives in another city altogether. It works less well for a Year 7 who needs an adult sitting beside them, for diagram-heavy Physics and Chemistry, and for Language B orals, where the entire value is the unscripted follow-up question. Most families here run in-person teaching weekly and keep online for deadline weeks and travel. Decide per subject rather than as a policy for the whole household.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after three sessions?
faqs.answer: You tell us and we re-match, usually from the shortlist you already saw. There is no argument about it and you owe no explanation beyond what went wrong, though the detail helps us: a tutor can be genuinely strong and still be wrong for one child. Replacement in Dadar is easier than in most of Mumbai because the pool reachable by train is larger, so a second name is often free on the same weekday at the same hour. Do not sit out a full term out of politeness. The sunk cost is three sessions, and the cost of staying is a term.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Ask the tutor for two named weaknesses and the plan for each, in writing. If they cannot produce that, the problem is the tutor. If they can, compare it against what you are seeing at home: a child who has started attempting homework before the session has already changed, even if the marks have not moved yet. A month is enough time to change process and rarely enough to change a grade. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and we would rather tell you that in September than have the conversation in March when nothing can be done about it.

faqs.question: Do we need a parent at home during the session?
faqs.answer: For a younger child, someone should be in the flat, though not in the room. For PYP and early MYP, an adult at home keeps the session from drifting and gives the tutor a person to hand a two-minute summary to at the end. For IGCSE and DP students, a parent sitting in the room usually makes things worse, because the child performs instead of admitting what they do not understand. Either way, ask for a short written note after each session. That is more useful than hovering and it gives you something to compare across a term.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover an IGCSE Year 10 and a DP1 sibling in the same evening?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, within the same subject, and it is always worth asking. A Mathematics tutor can often take a Year 10 at six and a DP1 at seven-thirty in the same Dadar flat, which cuts the travel cost for everyone and makes the slot more attractive to the tutor. It stops working across programmes in different subjects, since an IGCSE English teacher is not automatically a DP English teacher. Tell us at the enquiry stage that there are two children, because it changes which tutors we approach rather than being something we patch in later.

faqs.question: Is a tutor travelling from the Western Suburbs or Thane reliable for a full term in Dadar?
faqs.answer: In Dadar, yes, which is unusual for Mumbai. A long-distance match normally fails by November because the travel wears the tutor down, and for most addresses we therefore match within the zone. Dadar is the exception: the tutor stays on one train and steps off at your station, so a Thane, Ghatkopar or Borivali tutor can hold a Dadar slot for a full academic year. Ask the tutor directly how they travel and at what time they leave home. A precise answer is a good sign; a vague one usually means they have not thought it through.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor also cover Dadar Parsi Colony, Matunga or Prabhadevi?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and most tutors prefer it that way. Dadar Parsi Colony, Matunga and Prabhadevi all sit within a short ride of the station, so a tutor can take two sittings in one evening without losing an hour in between. If a cousin or a classmate in one of those areas wants the same subject, say so at the enquiry stage, because a tutor will often agree to a better time for two bookings close together than for one on its own. Each of those areas also has its own page with its own specifics.

faqs.question: Who is the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Dadar?
faqs.answer: There is no single answer, and anyone who gives you one is selling. The best IB and IGCSE tutor in Dadar for a DP2 Chemistry student who needs internal assessment help is not the right person for a Year 9 who has stopped attempting homework. What you actually want is a tutor who has taught your child's syllabus version, can name its components without looking them up, and is free at an hour that works every single week. That is a matching question rather than a ranking question, which is why we send two or three names instead of one.

You will get two or three tutors who already teach that syllabus, with a fee range for your exact request, and you speak to each of them before anything is booked. The first session is a diagnosis, you get a written summary of what it found, and if the fit is wrong we re-match.

sections.heading: How a request for an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Dahisar becomes a shortlist
paragraphs: A parent in Dahisar writes to us with three things, usually in this order: the school, the year group, and the subject that has gone quiet. Those three answers already narrow the pool more than most parents expect. A Grade 4 student at Singapore International School working through a unit of inquiry needs a different person from a Year 10 candidate sitting Cambridge International Education papers in May, and both need someone who can reach a flat near the Western Express Highway by half past four on a weekday without three changes. We match IB and IGCSE home tutors across Mumbai, but the ones who last in Dahisar live near the Western Line.

What happens next is deliberately slow at one point and fast everywhere else. We confirm the programme and the exact assessment in front of the student before we look at a single profile, because an MYP Year 3 Sciences brief and an IGCSE Coordinated Sciences brief look similar in a WhatsApp message and are nothing alike on paper. Once that is settled, shortlisting takes a day or two. Introductions are arranged around your timetable rather than the tutor's convenience, and the first paid session happens in your home with a parent somewhere in the flat.

We also ask the question parents find odd: who else lives in the house, and when do they need the dining table. Home tuition in Dahisar is usually delivered in a two bedroom or three bedroom flat where a younger sibling is doing homework in the same room. Knowing that in advance decides whether the slot is five o'clock or eight, whether the tutor brings printed past papers instead of relying on a screen, and whether a sixty minute session is more honest than ninety for a Primary Years Programme student who has already done a full day at Dahisar East. A family running all IB and IGCSE subjects through home classes in Dahisar for two children needs that answered before the first booking, not after.

sections.heading: Which programme is your Dahisar child actually in: PYP, MYP, DP or IGCSE?
paragraphs: In Dahisar the honest answer is usually Primary Years Programme (PYP) or Middle Years Programme (MYP), not Diploma Programme (DP). Singapore International School at Dahisar East runs the International Baccalaureate (IB) from the early years upward, so this locality has a genuine population of PYP and MYP families, which almost no other address at Mumbai's northern municipal edge can say. That one fact changes what a tutor here is asked to do, and it is why this page is not a copy of a suburb page further south.

The practical difference matters. PYP has no external examinations and no papers to drill. Work is organised into units of inquiry with a central idea and lines of inquiry, and it ends in PYP 5 with the Exhibition, a long collaborative inquiry the student plans, researches, acts on and reflects on in a journal. A tutor who treats that like a worksheet exercise is useless. The right person teaches a ten year old how to take notes from two sources that disagree, how to ask an interview question that is not answerable with yes, and how to keep the reflection journal current instead of writing the whole thing the night before it is due.

MYP, Years 1 to 5, is where assessment gets teeth without becoming an examination. Every subject group is marked against four criteria on eight point scales, and the grade descriptors reward process as much as answers. By MYP 5 there is the Personal Project, assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, which lands in the same year many families are also deciding whether to continue into DP or move to a Cambridge International Education pathway. IGCSE sits alongside all of this for families at JBCN International School, Borivali and other Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel schools in the Western Suburbs, where Core and Extended tier choices start biting in Year 9.
bullets: PYP: units of inquiry, no external papers, the PYP 5 Exhibition as the milestone
MYP: four criteria per subject group, each marked on an eight point scale
MYP 5: the Personal Project, assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting

sections.heading: Subject choice across both boards, and the internal assessment each one carries
paragraphs: Across both boards the subject conversation is really two conversations: what the student takes, and what each of those subjects makes them produce internally before any examination arrives. We match across all IB and IGCSE subjects with tutors in Dahisar and the roads around it, which means Mathematics in both its DP routes, the four sciences, Economics, Business Management, English Language and Literature, Hindi and Marathi for the language acquisition requirement, and the IGCSE equivalents including Additional Mathematics and Coordinated Sciences.

Here is what the work actually looks like. An MYP Year 4 student at Singapore International School is given a Sciences investigation and assessed on Criterion B, inquiring and designing. The marks sit in a research question that is genuinely testable, a hypothesis with scientific reasoning behind it rather than a guess, named independent, dependent and controlled variables, and a method another student could follow without asking a question. Most of the lost marks are in the last two. A tutor working at your dining table in Dahisar makes the student rewrite the method as numbered steps, hands it to a parent cold, and watches where the parent stops reading. That is the whole lesson, and it moves a four to a six in a way no amount of content revision does.

The choices themselves need the same honesty. Higher Level (HL) is not Standard Level (SL) with extra homework: it is additional content plus a longer, differently weighted paper, and taking three sciences at HL because a university page once mentioned it is how a DP1 student ends up with two Internal Assessments and a Theory of Knowledge essay due in the same fortnight. At IGCSE, the Core and Extended decision is made in Year 9 and quietly caps the grade available, so it deserves a conversation with the school rather than a default. A home tutor who has taught both tiers will tell you which one the student is actually sitting rather than which one the family hoped for.

sections.heading: How far will a Dahisar home tutor travel: Borivali East, Borivali West or Mira Road?
paragraphs: Realistically, a Dahisar home tutor also covers Borivali East, Borivali West and Mira Road, and very little beyond that on a weekday evening. Dahisar sits at the northern edge of Mumbai, Maharashtra, where the municipal corporation's limit ends. The Western Suburbs run north to south along the Western Express Highway and the Western Line, so matching along the line works and matching across it does not. A tutor who lives in Borivali West and teaches in Dahisar is doing one stop. A tutor pulled up from Andheri is doing an hour each way at six in the evening, and that arrangement collapses by the third week of term.

Two pieces of road geography decide the timetable here. The Dahisar check naka on the Western Express Highway is where northbound traffic bunches, so a tutor driving in from Kandivali or Malad after five arrives late often enough to matter, while the same person on the Western Line to Dahisar station walks in on time. Metro Lines 2A and 7 end at Dahisar East rather than passing through, which is the same fact as the school being here: this is where the city's rail infrastructure stops and the suburbs beyond the boundary begin.

The direction of travel is the thing people get wrong. Families in Mira Road and Bhayandar drive south into Dahisar East for school, which makes this locality a destination for the morning and afternoon school run rather than only a place people live. Their children get home late, so the early evening slot a Dahisar resident can take at half past four is not available to them, and north of the municipal boundary the sensible answer often becomes an online backbone with occasional visits. Here it is the opposite: the school is inside the locality, the child is home by four, and IB and IGCSE home tuition in Dahisar is the straightforward option rather than the compromise.

sections.heading: The Dahisar and Borivali school calendar, and what it does to a Mumbai evening
paragraphs: Two schools shape most of the requests we take in Dahisar. Singapore International School at Dahisar East runs IB programmes, which is why PYP and MYP work dominates here, and JBCN International School, Borivali serves the families who went the Cambridge and IB route a few kilometres south. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Singapore International School, JBCN International School, Borivali, or any school named anywhere on this page. We name them because their calendars set the pressure points, and for no other reason.

The Mumbai school year opens in June, and the first real squeeze is late August into September, when MYP units close their first assessed tasks and IGCSE Year 10 students meet coursework deadlines they were warned about in July. October brings the first proper reporting round, then Diwali empties the city for a fortnight and parents discover that two weeks without a tutor undoes six weeks of habit. January and February are the hardest months in the Western Suburbs: DP2 mock examinations, an IGCSE January series for some candidates, Internal Assessment final drafts, and the PYP 5 Exhibition moving from planning into its research phase all at once.

March to May is examination season and the wrong time to start from zero, which is exactly when most enquiries arrive. A family that begins in June or July gets a tutor who has seen a full cycle before the stakes are high. There is a quieter calendar point too, specific to a locality with a school inside it: because the Dahisar East school run happens here rather than somewhere else, after school clubs and sport finish on a campus a short drive from home, so the half past four to six thirty window genuinely exists for Dahisar families. In most of Mumbai that window is spent in a car.

sections.heading: Is home tuition in Dahisar better than online for a PYP or MYP student?
paragraphs: For a PYP or MYP student in Dahisar, home tuition is better, and it is not a close call. A nine or thirteen year old on a video call drifts in under fifteen minutes, and the material at this stage is physical: a unit of inquiry folder, a science method written by hand, a mathematics page where the tutor needs to see which line the student stopped trusting. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Dahisar sitting at the table catches that in seconds.

Online earns its place in two situations. The first is a scarce subject: if the student needs Higher Level Economics, Computer Science, Psychology or French, the person who has taught that syllabus for years may be in Thane, Pune or Bengaluru, and IB and IGCSE online tuition in Dahisar with the right specialist beats home tuition with a generalist every time. The second is the week before a paper, when a thirty minute call to check one Internal Assessment paragraph is worth more than a cancelled ninety minute visit. What online loses is the small stuff: the tutor noticing the phone face up, the parent catching three minutes of the lesson on the way past.

Hybrid is what most Dahisar families end up with, usually without planning it. One visit a week at home for the work that needs a desk and a pen, one shorter online session for revision checking, and the balance tipping towards screens in February and back towards visits in June. The trade-off to be honest about is this: hybrid needs more organisation from the parent, not less, because two slots in two formats fail twice as easily as one. If nobody in the house will keep that timetable, pick home tuition alone and keep it simple.

sections.heading: How tutors are checked, and what a Dahisar parent should check themselves
paragraphs: Verification on our side is unglamorous and specific. We confirm identity with a government photograph document, we confirm the degree or teaching qualification claimed, and we confirm board experience by asking about the thing only an experienced person knows: how MYP criteria map to a report grade, what a moderator actually flags on an IGCSE coursework sample, which Internal Assessment sections students lose marks in. A tutor who has taught DP Physics can tell you in one sentence what goes wrong in the uncertainty analysis. A tutor who has not, cannot, and the gap shows inside a minute.

Then there is the part we cannot do for you, and it matters more for an IB and IGCSE private tutor in Dahisar who will be inside your flat weekly than it does for an online appointment. Ask to see the identity document yourself at the first session. Keep the first few lessons in a room where the door stays open and someone else is at home. Ask the tutor which board and which year group they have taught most recently, and listen for a specific answer. Tell your society office the name and leave it on the visitor register rather than waving the person through, because a standing weekly entry is easier for everyone from the second week onward.

Two more checks are worth the small awkwardness. First, ask what the tutor does when the student has no homework, because the answer separates someone with a plan from someone filling an hour. Second, ask for a one paragraph written note after every fourth session, not a verbal report at the door. Parents in Mumbai pay for sessions and receive impressions, and then cannot tell in November whether anything has changed since August. A short written record fixes that, and a tutor who resists writing it is telling you something useful.

Board experience tested with questions only an experienced teacher can answer
See the identity document yourself at the first home session
Keep early sessions in an open room with an adult in the flat

sections.heading: What does an hour of home tuition in Dahisar actually depend on?
paragraphs: IB and IGCSE home tuition fees in Dahisar depend on five things, and no honest page can give you a number without knowing them: the board and level, the subject's scarcity, how far the tutor travels, how long the session runs, and whether you are booking one subject or three. IB Gram does not publish a price list, because the same hour is priced differently for MYP Year 2 Mathematics and for Higher Level Chemistry, and pretending otherwise wastes everybody's first phone call.

Level does most of the work. PYP and early MYP support sits at the lower end because the pool of capable people is wide. Higher Level sciences, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at HL, Economics and the smaller language options sit at the top, because very few people in Mumbai have taught them to examination standard and they are all booked by August. Subject scarcity is a supply fact, not a quality judgement. Travel is the factor Dahisar families can actually influence: a tutor from Borivali East or Borivali West absorbs a short hop, while somebody crossing from Andheri or the Central Suburbs is pricing in two hours of their evening and will say so.

Here is where being the last stop with a school inside it helps you. In most of Mumbai the specialist lives somewhere else, so distance is built into every quote. In Dahisar, the fact that Singapore International School is in the locality means a number of experienced IB teachers already work within a few kilometres for their other students, and a slot next to an existing one costs them almost nothing in travel. Session length is the other lever: ninety minutes twice a week is the standard DP and IGCSE shape, while sixty minutes three times a week suits a PYP student far better and often costs the same in total.

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle in Mumbai
paragraphs: Four weeks buys you habits, not marks. By the end of the first month you should see the student bring work to the session unasked, a homework diary that is actually filled in, and a tutor who can name the two specific weaknesses rather than saying the student needs more practice. If after four weekly sessions nobody can tell you what is wrong in precise language, that is the signal to change tutor, not to wait another month and hope.

One term is where a grade moves, and usually by one band rather than three. An MYP criterion score going from four to six, an IGCSE predicted grade moving from a C to a B, a DP student who stops losing the method marks: those are realistic single term outcomes. One full examination cycle is the honest horizon for a two band jump. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and anybody in Mumbai who does is either lying or taking credit for a student who was going to improve anyway. What a good tutor controls is preparation, feedback speed and the number of unforced errors. What they cannot control is a bad night, a paper that falls awkwardly, or a student who stops working in April.

When it is not working, say so early and say so plainly. Tell us in the fourth week rather than the fourth month. We ask three questions: is the subject knowledge missing, is the explanation not landing, or is the relationship wrong, because the fix is different in each case. A replacement is arranged without an argument and without a fee for the swap, and we hand the new tutor the written notes from the old one so the student does not restart from the beginning. Changing tutor once in a year is normal. Changing three times in a term means the diagnosis was wrong at the start, and that is ours to redo.
bullets: Four weeks: habits, a filled homework diary, two named weaknesses
One term: typically a single band, on a criterion or a predicted grade
One examination cycle: the honest horizon for a larger move

sections.heading: Starting with an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Dahisar: what to have ready
paragraphs: Have four things to hand and the first session stops being a diagnostic hour you paid for. The most recent report card or MYP criterion sheet. The last two pieces of marked work, including the bad one, because the bad one is where the information is. The school's assessment calendar for the term. And a clear answer on when the student is actually free, which in Dahisar usually means after the school run settles and before dinner.

The first session itself should look like this. The tutor spends the opening stretch on the marked work rather than teaching, finds the point where the understanding stopped, and says it out loud so the student hears it. Then one worked problem taken all the way through, start to finish, at the student's pace. Then a short plan for the next three weeks that names the paper, criterion or unit being targeted. You should be able to read that plan in under a minute. If the first session was pure introduction and no work got done, ask why before you book the second.

A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai is easy to find and hard to find well, and the difference shows up in month three, not week one. Parents searching for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Dahisar are usually really asking for somebody who will still be turning up in February with the energy they had in July. That is a scheduling question as much as a teaching one, which is why we start with your week before we start with profiles.

Two pieces of marked work, including the one that went badly

faqs.question: Will an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Dahisar actually come to my flat on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the slot that works best here is between half past four and half past six. Dahisar families have an advantage most of Mumbai does not: because Singapore International School is inside the locality at Dahisar East, children are home before the evening traffic builds. A tutor arriving by the Western Line to Dahisar station, or living in Borivali East, can take that slot reliably week after week. Anything after seven is harder, because the tutor is then travelling back north through the Dahisar check naka at the worst hour of the day.

faqs.question: How does society gate access and the visitor register work for a weekly tutor?
faqs.answer: Put the tutor on the visitor register as a standing weekly entry in the first week and the problem disappears. Most Dahisar buildings on the Western Express Highway side ask for a photograph identity document at the gate, log the flat number, and issue a pass. Doing that once, with a note from you at the society office, saves ten minutes of argument every single week. If your building uses a visitor app, add the tutor as a recurring guest. We also tell tutors to carry identity to every session, not only the first, because watchmen change shifts.

faqs.question: What does searching IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Dahisar actually turn up?
faqs.answer: Mostly three things: directories of names with no board detail, coaching classes that teach a state syllabus and add IB to the signboard, and a handful of genuine specialists who are already full. The useful filter is board experience at the exact level. Ask any name you find which programme and year group they taught last term, and what the assessment was called. Someone who answers with MYP Year 4 Sciences and a Criterion B investigation is worth meeting. Someone who answers international board, all subjects, is not.

faqs.question: My child is in PYP. Is a tutor even appropriate at that age?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the reason is almost never content. PYP has no external papers, so a tutor here works on how a child reads a source, organises an inquiry and keeps a reflection journal, usually in the run up to the PYP 5 Exhibition. Dahisar sees more of these requests than most Mumbai localities because Singapore International School runs the programme inside the locality. Sixty minutes, twice a week, with a parent in the flat is the shape that works. If the request is really to make an eight year old do more worksheets, we will say no and explain why.

faqs.question: We live in Mira Road and drive to Dahisar East for school. Should the tutor come to us?
faqs.answer: Stay flexible, and expect online to carry more of the week than it would for a Dahisar resident. Crossing the boundary at Mira Road in the evening peak is the single biggest cause of cancelled sessions we see on this stretch, and your child is also getting home later because of the school run itself. A workable pattern is one weekend visit at home for the work that needs a desk, plus two shorter weekday online sessions. Families inside Dahisar do not need that compromise, which is the main practical difference between the two addresses.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is good but my child has made no progress after a month?
faqs.answer: Tell us in that fourth week, and expect a diagnosis before a replacement. No visible progress after four sessions usually means one of three things: the gap is further back than anyone assumed, the sessions are revising instead of teaching, or the student is not doing anything between visits. Each has a different fix and only the third belongs to the student. We will ask for the marked work from those four weeks and read it. If the tutor is simply wrong for this student, the swap costs nothing and the written notes go across with it.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover all IB and IGCSE subjects, or do we need several?
faqs.answer: One tutor can reasonably cover a PYP child's whole week, and should not try to cover a DP student's. Up to around MYP Year 3, a strong generalist with real IB experience handles Mathematics, Sciences and Individuals and Societies together, and the continuity helps more than the specialism would. From MYP Year 4 and across IGCSE and DP, subject specialists are the only honest answer, because Higher Level Chemistry and Language and Literature are different jobs. Most Dahisar families we work with end up with one person for the younger child and two specialists for the older one.

faqs.question: How do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Dahisar compare with Borivali West or Andheri?
faqs.answer: Broadly similar, with travel as the only real variable, and we will not quote a figure on a web page. The rate is set by level and subject scarcity first: Higher Level sciences cost more than MYP support anywhere in Mumbai. Where Dahisar differs is distance. A tutor from Borivali East or Borivali West is a short hop and prices accordingly, while pulling a specialist up from Andheri or Bandra adds two hours of travel to their evening, and that shows up in the number. Ask what each quote assumes about travel before you compare them.

faqs.question: Does the parent need to be at home during a home tuition session?
faqs.answer: For PYP and younger MYP students, yes, at least for the first several weeks. You do not need to sit in the room, but somebody should be in the flat with the door open. For an IGCSE or DP student, a parent at home is good practice rather than a requirement, and many sixteen year olds work better without an audience. Either way, walk past once. Thirty seconds of overheard lesson tells you more about whether the match is right than a month of politeness at the door does. That holds for an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Dahisar whether the session runs sixty minutes or ninety.

faqs.question: Which schools do your Dahisar students usually attend?
faqs.answer: Mostly Singapore International School at Dahisar East and JBCN International School, Borivali, with some families at Cambridge schools further south in Kandivali and Malad. IB Gram is an independent platform with no affiliation to any of them; we track their calendars because that is what decides when a student needs help. The practical value of knowing the school is timing. A September coursework deadline at one school and a first assessed MYP task at another land in different weeks, and the tutor should know which one is coming next.

faqs.question: Can we start with a trial session before committing to a term?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we recommend it, but treat it as a working session rather than a meeting. Bring the marked work, let the tutor teach something, and judge whether your child talked. A trial where the tutor explains their methodology to the parent for forty minutes tells you nothing about the teaching. Afterwards you should have a three week plan naming the paper, criterion or unit being targeted. If you want a different person after the trial, say so the same evening and we will send another profile rather than ask you to persist.

We come back with two or three matched profiles, each with the board and level they have actually taught, usually within a day or two. You pick who you meet. The first session happens in your Dahisar flat, with the marked work on the table, and you get a written plan after it.

sections.heading: How does IB Gram find an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Dombivli?
paragraphs: You send five things: the board, the year group, the subjects, your address in Dombivli, and the two or three time slots that genuinely work. IB Gram returns a shortlist drawn from Dombivli, Palava City, Kalyan and Thane West, and says plainly which of those tutors can hold a weekday evening slot and which can realistically only teach online. The process runs in five steps. 1. We search the pool in order of distance: tutors living in Dombivli first, Palava City and Kalyan next, Thane West after that, and the online pool across Mumbai alongside all three. 3. sections.heading: PYP, MYP, DP and IGCSE: what a Dombivli family is actually choosing between
paragraphs: Dombivli families are choosing between two systems run by different organisations and assessed in completely different ways. The International Baccalaureate (IB) runs the Primary Years Programme (PYP), the Middle Years Programme (MYP) and the Diploma Programme (DP). IGCSE is a qualification, usually from Cambridge International Education and sometimes from Pearson Edexcel, sat at the end of Year 11. Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane follows the Cambridge pathway; NES International School in Mulund West offers both IB and IGCSE. A child's programme here is therefore set by a school forty to sixty minutes from the front door.

The decision point most families hit is Year 8 into Year 9. MYP Years 4 and 5 are assessed against criteria set by the school and moderated by the IB; IGCSE is assessed externally on papers with published grade thresholds. Parents often read the second as the safer option because the marks look familiar. Both feed into the DP or into A Levels perfectly well. What changes is the kind of work your child does at home for two years: MYP demands sustained project and reflection work, IGCSE demands past-paper fluency, and a home tutor should be chosen for whichever of those two your child is weaker at rather than for the subject label.

At DP, your child takes six subjects, three at Higher Level (HL) and three at Standard Level (SL), plus Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and Creativity, Activity, Service. The HL and SL split is the most consequential choice of the two years, because HL adds teaching hours and, in several subjects, a further examination paper. A Dombivli student who takes three sciences at HL because a university page suggested it will spend the second year buried in internal assessment work while her TOK essay sits untouched, and the travel to school will already have taken two hours of that day.

IB Gram matches at programme level first and subject level second, because a tutor who is excellent at IGCSE Chemistry is not automatically useful to a DP student writing an HL Chemistry internal assessment. The two sit in different documents, carry different criteria and reward different habits. Say which programme and which year on the request form and the shortlist narrows usefully before anyone has discussed a fee.

sections.heading: Subject choice, Core versus Extended, and the assessments each one carries
paragraphs: Subject choice across both boards is where most of the damage is done, and it is done quietly on a form submitted in February. At IGCSE, Mathematics (0580), the sciences and several languages are tiered into Core and Extended. Core caps the grade available, which closes Higher Level in that subject two years later. A Year 9 student placed on Core Maths because her Year 8 marks were weak can usually be moved up, but only if somebody notices in time and works the Extended-only topics with her through the autumn.

Every DP subject carries an internal assessment, and they do not arrive politely spaced out. The sciences require an individual investigation built on a research question the student designs herself. Mathematics requires an exploration. Economics requires commentaries written on news articles. Business Management, Psychology, History and Geography each carry their own written task with its own criteria. Language A students sit an individual oral and, at Higher Level, write an essay on a studied text. Above all of that sit TOK and the Extended Essay. A tutor who only knows the final papers is of limited use between October and February, which is exactly when the pressure lands.

IGCSE carries less internal work but more components. English Language (0500) splits reading and directed writing across two papers. The sciences add an alternative-to-practical paper that asks about apparatus some students have barely handled. Mathematics splits into papers with different calculator rules. Knowing which component your child is losing marks on matters more than knowing the subject, and establishing that is the first job of a first session, not something discovered in January.

Families searching for all IB and IGCSE subjects support from one tutor in Dombivli usually end up better served by two specialists than by one generalist. IB Gram covers all IB and IGCSE subjects, and a two-subject request is shortlisted twice, once per subject. A strong Physics tutor and a strong English tutor are rarely the same person, and pretending otherwise costs a term that nobody gets back.

sections.heading: Dombivli, Kalyan, Thane West and Palava City: who can actually reach your door
paragraphs: Dombivli sits on the Kalyan–Dombivli belt in the far north-east of Mumbai, Maharashtra, two stops short of Kalyan on the Central Line, and Dombivli station divides the town into East and West. That split matters more than it looks, because a tutor in Dombivli East and a family in Dombivli West are separated by the station bridge at exactly the hour both want to use it. A search for an IB and IGCSE tutor near me in Dombivli returns names from across the Thane district, and a good many of them are in no position to reach you on a Wednesday.

The Kalyan–Shil Road is the road that makes this page workable. It runs from Kalyan down past Palava City towards Shil Phata and on into Navi Mumbai, which means a Palava-based tutor can reach a Dombivli address by car in a way a Thane West tutor cannot do on a train. Thane itself spreads west to east from the station across Pokhran Road, Ghodbunder Road and Majiwada, and the Ghodbunder stretch sets the schedule for everyone living there: a tutor near Thane station reaches Kasarvadavali in twenty minutes off-peak and nearly an hour in the evening. Ask that same tutor to continue out to Dombivli afterwards and the arrangement is finished before it has started.

So the matching rule here is simple and we apply it openly. Tutors living in Dombivli, Kalyan or Palava City are offered for home tuition. Thane West tutors are offered for weekend slots, and only where they have already taught in this direction and know what the journey costs them. Everyone else is offered online. An IB and IGCSE private tutor in Dombivli who lives in the town is worth more to you over a full year than a more decorated one in Thane West who will tire of the commute by the second month. Mumbai is a city where a tutor's address predicts attendance better than any promise made in week one.

One local detail worth planning around: the Central Line between Thane and Kalyan is the stretch that suffers most in a heavy monsoon. From the middle of June into September a Saturday session is safer than a weekday one, and a tutor who agrees in advance to switch a lost session to a screen rather than cancel it is worth more than a slightly cheaper tutor who will not.

sections.heading: Which schools do Dombivli families travel to, and how does that set the term?
paragraphs: Most international-board families in Dombivli travel out for school. Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and NES International School in Mulund West are the two names that come up most often, with the Palava City schools taking families who have moved south along the Kalyan–Shil Road. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page. We name them because their calendars, not ours, set your child's deadlines.

That travel decides the tutoring day before anyone has picked a tutor. A bus to Thane or Mulund West leaves Dombivli early and returns late, and a Year 10 child is frequently not home, fed and settled much before half past six. A home tutor arriving at seven and leaving at half past eight is asking a tired child for the worst ninety minutes of the day, and asking a travelling tutor to make the return journey at nine at night. An online session at eight, with the child at her own desk and no travel at either end, is simply a better use of the same hour. Accepting that early saves a term of frustration.

The Mumbai school year starts in June and the pressure points are predictable. August and September bring the first MYP criterion-assessed tasks and the first IGCSE class tests that feed a predicted grade. Late October and November bring internal assessment drafts and second-year mocks, often in the same fortnight as the TOK essay. January and February are mock season and the coursework deadline window. April and May are the DP examinations, with the Cambridge May and June series following for IGCSE and an October and November series for retakes. Book a tutor in June and you have room. Book one in January and you are bidding against every other family in Mumbai for the same evening hour.

Schools in this belt set homework through portals that parents can read. Bring that portal to the first session. A tutor who can see the actual task list, rather than a child's recollection of it, plans a term in ten minutes instead of three weeks, and will spot immediately that the science investigation and the language oral fall in the same month.

sections.heading: Is home tuition in Dombivli realistic on a weeknight, or is online the honest answer?
paragraphs: IB and IGCSE home tuition in Dombivli is realistic at weekends and in the weeks before examinations, and mostly unrealistic as a standing weeknight arrangement unless the tutor lives in Dombivli, Kalyan or Palava City. That is the honest answer. It is the one we lead with rather than the one that would sell more sessions, because an arrangement that breaks in week five costs a family more than a slower start would have.

Home tutoring is still the lead service here and it earns its place where it fits. A tutor in the room reads a child's face, picks up the page she is hiding, sees the handwriting slow on a particular kind of question and catches the moment attention goes. For a PYP or MYP child, for a student with weak exam-hall discipline, and for the fortnight before mocks, nothing on a screen matches it. The arrangement that holds out here is a long Saturday or Sunday morning session, ninety minutes or two hours rather than sixty, with a tutor who has not had to cross the city to arrive.

Online carries the weeknights. A good online session is not a thinner version of a home session; it is a different format that is better at several things, which the next section sets out properly. Hybrid is what most families here actually buy: online twice a week and one home visit at the weekend, with home visits stepping up in the month before papers. On cost, IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Dombivli depend on the board, the level, how scarce the subject specialist is, how far the tutor travels and how long the session runs. Travel is a real line item out here in a way it is not in Powai or Chembur.

Decide the shape before you decide the person. Some families want all IB and IGCSE subjects covered by home classes in Dombivli from day one, and we will try, but the shortlist will be short and two of those names will quietly give up the weekday slot. A family that asks instead for two online weeknights and one weekend home session gets a longer shortlist, stronger tutors on it, and an arrangement that is still running in March.

Weekend sessions run ninety minutes or two hours, not sixty

sections.heading: How is a tutor checked before teaching in a Mumbai home?
paragraphs: Checks happen before a tutor reaches any shortlist, and they are documentary rather than impressionistic. Government photo identity, the degree certificate for the subject being offered, and evidence of board experience: which syllabus codes, which examination sessions, at which school or centre. A claim to have examined or moderated for a board is checked separately from ordinary teaching experience, because it is the claim most often stretched and the one parents most reasonably care about.

After the documents comes a subject conversation, and it is specific. A prospective DP Chemistry tutor is asked how he would move a student from a vague research question to one that can actually be measured in a school laboratory within the time allowed. An IGCSE English tutor is asked to mark a short passage response and justify the band. Tutors offering screen sessions run part of that conversation on the setup they will use with your child, because somebody who cannot share a document, annotate it cleanly and keep a camera steady will not be a useful IB and IGCSE online tutor in Dombivli however well he knows the syllabus.

Then there is the half we cannot do for you. Sit in on the first session, or leave the door open. Ask which syllabus version your child is sitting and for which first examination year; hesitation there means the tutor has not taught it recently. Ask what your child is currently losing marks on and expect an answer about a component, not about effort or attitude. For home tuition, check that the person who arrives is the person on the profile, every single week, and tell us the same day if a substitute appears. For online work, check the same face is on camera and the shared folder is where it was promised.

References from previous families are taken where they exist, and where a tutor is new to the platform the profile says so rather than padding the gap. A teacher with three years in a Mumbai classroom and current syllabus knowledge is often a better match than a longer-listed name who last taught the subject two revisions ago.

Syllabus codes and examination sessions taught are verified, not assumed

sections.heading: What online tutoring genuinely does well for a Dombivli student
paragraphs: Online tutoring does four things better than a tutor in your living room, and none of them are small. It puts the same document in front of both people at the same moment. It removes travel from both ends, so a session can be fifty focused minutes on a Wednesday instead of ninety tired minutes on a Saturday. It makes a short emergency session possible the night before a deadline. And it widens the pool from the handful of qualified specialists inside the Kalyan–Dombivli belt to every subject specialist in Mumbai, which matters most at Higher Level where the local pool runs thin.

Here is the component it suits best. Take a Diploma Programme first-year student in Dombivli writing the first of her Economics internal assessment commentaries. The task is a tightly capped piece on a recent news article, applying one syllabus concept, carrying a diagram and a real evaluation. Almost all of the work is editing: choosing an article that contains a measurable intervention rather than a general news story, drawing a diagram that matches that article rather than the textbook, and cutting the paragraphs of summary that earn nothing against the criteria. In a shared document the tutor highlights the summary, writes the criterion descriptor beside it and watches her rewrite the passage live. The diagram is drawn over the same page on a tablet layer and redrawn twice inside four minutes. A tutor sitting next to her would do exactly this, upside down, on paper, after an hour of travel. Internal assessments in Economics, Business Management, History, Psychology and Language A, and Extended Essay chapters, all behave this way.

What online does badly is equally clear. A nine-year-old in PYP will not hold a screen session; book that one at home at the weekend or not at all. Timed handwritten practice under examination conditions needs a person in the room who is not the parent. A student who has learned to look busy will look busy on camera too. Setup fixes most of the rest: a second phone on a stand pointing down at the page so the tutor watches the working rather than the finished answer, wired earphones instead of a speaker, a desk rather than a bed, homework photographed and sent the night before, and one shared folder holding every past paper and marked script so nobody hunts for a file mid-session.

Online also fails quietly, which is the real risk out here. Nobody announces that the sessions have become a pleasant conversation. Two habits guard against it. Ask for a two-line note after each session saying what was covered and what was set. Once a month, ask for a timed question done cold and marked against the published mark scheme rather than discussed. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Dombivli who also teaches you online should be held to the same evidence as one sitting at your dining table, and across Mumbai that evidence is what separates an arrangement that works from one that merely continues.

A second phone as an overhead camera shows working, not just answers

sections.heading: What progress looks like, and what no tutor in Mumbai can promise
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not be looking at marks. Look for three other things: your child can say what she is weak at in the language of the syllabus rather than saying she is bad at Maths, homework is being started earlier in the week, and the tutor can name a specific component where marks are leaking. If none of that is true after four sessions, the match is wrong and it will not correct itself by waiting.

At one term, expect movement on the thing you agreed to attack first and little movement anywhere else, because that is what honest tutoring looks like. A student who was losing marks on Paper 2 structure should be writing better Paper 2 answers while Paper 1 stays roughly where it was. At one full examination cycle, with mocks behind you, you should see a trend across several marked papers rather than one encouraging score. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and any IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai who does is telling you something nobody can know in advance.

When a tutor is not working out, say so early and say precisely what is wrong, because the two common problems have different fixes. If the subject knowledge is thin, the tutor has to be replaced. If the knowledge is fine but your child has disengaged, the format is often the culprit: a weekend home session instead of a weeknight screen, or two shorter sessions instead of one long one. We ask for that distinction, send replacement profiles within a few days, and give the new tutor the previous session notes along with your original request so your child is not diagnosed again from zero. Nobody is locked into a term.

The limits deserve stating plainly. A tutor cannot rebuild two years of missing foundations in the term before IGCSE papers. A tutor cannot write an internal assessment and should not want to, because authenticity declarations exist and schools in Mumbai do read drafts. A tutor cannot replace attendance in class. What a good one does is make the hours your child already spends at the desk count for considerably more than they currently do.
bullets: Four weeks: better vocabulary and an earlier start, not higher marks
One term: movement on the agreed weakness, little elsewhere
One exam cycle: a trend across marked papers, not one good score

sections.heading: Booking your first IB and IGCSE home tuition session in Dombivli
paragraphs: Before the first session, put four things in one place: the last two marked scripts or reports, the subject list with levels and tiers written out, the school homework portal login or a printout of the current task list, and the two or three slots that genuinely work once the bus has arrived. Families who bring these get a useful first hour. Families who do not spend that hour assembling them while the tutor waits.

The first session is diagnostic and it should feel like it. The tutor works through a recent marked script with your child and finds where the marks actually went, which is almost never where the parent assumed. She asks what is due over the next three weeks and writes it down. She sets one piece of work small enough to be finished and specific enough to be marked. By the end she should be able to tell you, in two sentences, which component to attack first and roughly how long that will take. If the hour was mostly introductions and a syllabus overview, say so straight away.

For a Dombivli booking we also settle the shape in that first week: which nights are online, which weekend morning is at home, and what happens in a monsoon week when the Central Line stops running. Agree the substitution rule up front. A session lost to trains should convert to a screen slot within forty-eight hours rather than vanish from the count. Agree as well that home visits step up before mocks, so nobody is renegotiating in January when every decent tutor in Mumbai is already committed.

Start in June or July if the choice is yours. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai is easiest to find in the first weeks of the school year, when the strong ones still have slots open and your child still has room to change something that matters. By the time the first reports arrive in October, the same tutors are full and the same weeks are gone.

The first session ends with a named component and a rough timeline
