sections.heading: Do home classes work better than online for practical science?
paragraphs: Home tutoring leads for 4SD0 and the strongest reason is diagram work. Science explanation happens on paper: a circuit redrawn, a force arrow added, an ionic equation balanced beside the wrong attempt so the student sees the difference. A tutor at the table does this continuously and almost unconsciously, and your child's notebook fills with the record of it. Most families booking an Edexcel IGCSE Science Double Award 4SD0 home tutor in Mumbai are buying that, plus the fact that an hour in the flat gets used as an hour rather than drifting into a conversation.

Online is better than people expect for two of the three strands and weaker for one. Chemistry calculation work and Biology recall and terminology transfer to a screen well, because they are question-and-answer disciplines and a shared document works fine. Physics suffers more, because the teaching is spatial and a tutor needs to point at the student's own diagram and redraw it. If you are going to run one strand online, run Chemistry or Biology there. An IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai is also the sensible answer when the strand you need is scarce in your node, which happens with Physics in the outer suburbs more than anywhere else.

Hybrid is the arrangement that fits this subject naturally, because it solves the two-tutor problem. One strand taught at home weekly, the second strand run online at a shorter and cheaper slot, with past-paper questions set between both. That keeps one in-person relationship, adds a specialist you could not otherwise reach, and avoids two people climbing into your building every week. In the monsoon, when the Eastern Express Highway floods and the Central Line slows, the online slot is the one that still happens, and in a subject with this much content a missed fortnight is expensive.

sections.heading: Does Double Award close the door on IB HL sciences?
paragraphs: No, and this is the question behind most 4SD0 searches even when the parent does not ask it directly. Students move from Science (Double Award) into Higher Level (HL) sciences in the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) and into demanding A Level science courses every year, in Mumbai and everywhere else. Entry requirements are set by schools, not by the code, and they are usually expressed as a grade: a school may ask for a particular grade in science before admitting a student to HL Chemistry. Ask your target school or your current DP coordinator for the actual requirement in writing. They have the answer and we do not.

What is true is that the first term of a post-16 science course is harder from Double Award than from triple, in a specific and manageable way. The content gap is not vast; the fluency gap is real. A triple-science student has handled more Chemistry questions and met more Physics contexts simply because they sat more papers. A Double Award student arriving in HL Chemistry knows the ideas and has practised them less. The fix is boring and effective: work through the separate-science content for the one or two subjects your child intends to continue, during Year 11 or over the holiday before the course starts. A few weeks of that removes most of the disadvantage.

The second thing worth understanding is how the two grades behave, because parents assume they are an average and they are not quite. 4SD0 reports two grades from performance across the three disciplines, and the aggregation rules are the specification's business rather than something to be guessed at. What follows practically is that the weakest strand pulls both grades down, which is why strand diagnosis is worth more here than in any single-subject page on this site. A student who is strong in two sciences and poor in one does not get a strong grade and a weak grade. They get two grades that both reflect the drag. Ask your examinations officer to explain the current rules for your child's series.

On cost, be precise about what you are comparing. IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on board and level, how scarce the strand specialist is, travel distance and belt, and session length, and for Double Award on how many strands an engagement covers. One tutor covering all three at one rate and two specialists at two rates are different products, and the cheaper total is not automatically the weaker choice. We quote no figures because a number offered without seeing the papers is invented. Ask for rate, session length, strands covered and travel assumption as four separate items. Parents ask who the best IGCSE tutor in Mumbai is for science; the honest answer is whoever is strongest in the strand that is actually dragging your child's two grades down.

One timing note that costs families real marks. A Science (Double Award) (4SD0) IGCSE Years 9-11 tutor Mumbai households bring in during Year 9 or early Year 10 can fix a conceptual gap at the particle level, where it lives. The same tutor brought in during February of Year 11 can teach command words, calculation technique and paper timing, which are worth marks and are not the same as understanding. Both engagements are legitimate. They are not interchangeable.

sections.heading: What four weeks, one term and one exam cycle should show
paragraphs: At four weeks the evidence is in the notebook, not the marks. Look for diagrams drawn by your child rather than copied, calculations laid out in steps with units carried through, and a few questions where the command word has been underlined. Those three things say the tutor is teaching how science is written down. If the notebook holds only pages of notes the tutor dictated, the engagement is a lecture series. Say something in week five. Marks on three strands move slowly because content volume is the constraint, and a term of real work can produce a small numerical change.

At one term, expect the weak strand to have moved and the other two to be roughly where they were. That is the correct outcome of a triage decision and you should be able to see the decision written down from the first session. Ask what got attacked, what the evidence is, and which strand comes next. A tutor who worked all three strands evenly across a term has usually made no measurable difference to any of them, which is the most common way a well-intentioned science engagement wastes a term.

Across a full cycle, compare the October mock with the January mock strand by strand, and read the marked scripts rather than the totals. A student who went from no working to laid-out working in Chemistry has banked marks that will appear in the real session even if the mock total was flat, because the mock was marked by a teacher who already knew the student. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, cannot promise a specific outcome, and would rather tell you in January that a target is unlikely than let you find out in May.

The limits are worth stating plainly. No amount of home tutoring closes a two-year content gap in three months across three sciences; if your child is genuinely behind in all three, the realistic goal is two decent grades rather than two strong ones, and we will say that at the start. A student who does not do the set questions between sessions will not improve, because science rewards volume of practice more than any other subject on this list. And a student in the wrong route, one who needed triple science and was placed in Double Award or the reverse, has a timetable problem that no tutor can solve. That conversation belongs with the school.

sections.heading: Starting Science Double Award home tuition in Mumbai
paragraphs: To get a shortlist for an Edexcel IGCSE Science Double Award 4SD0 home tutor in Mumbai, send four things. The entry code confirmed by the school, the last two science assessments with question papers, any strand-level breakdown the school can give you, and the hours in the week when your child still has concentration left. Add your area and society name, and flag any gate-pass or visitor-register process so the tutor plans arrival time around it instead of losing ten minutes of the first session at the entrance.

The first session is a diagnostic and we tell tutors to run it as one. A short set of questions across all three strands, enough to confirm which one is dragging, followed by teaching one real question from that strand properly. Your child should leave the session having understood something specific that was confusing in the morning. You should leave it knowing which strand the term will target and why.

Within a day or two of that session you get a written plan: the strand sequence, the topics in the first four weeks, how many questions will be set between sessions, and what you should expect to see by the next school assessment. Read it and push back if it does not match what you want. The plan is also the handover document if you ever change tutors, which saves the replacement a fortnight of rediscovery.

Nothing about the trial commits you. If you want a different tutor after three or four sessions, tell us what specifically went wrong and we shortlist again from a sharper brief. An IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai is a term-long working arrangement in a subject with a lot of content, and the families who do best are the ones who fix a wrong match in September instead of tolerating it until January.

faqs.question: Is Science Double Award the same as triple science with less content?
faqs.answer: No. 4SD0 is its own specification with its own content boundaries, not the separate sciences with topics removed at random. Some material in the separate Physics, Chemistry and Biology qualifications is outside the Double Award, and the Double Award organises what it keeps in its own way. This matters when hiring: a tutor working from the separate-science syllabus will teach topics your child will never be assessed on and may skip ones they will. Ask any candidate to name two topics in the single sciences that a Double Award student does not need, and check the current Pearson specification yourself.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Kandivali East for an evening slot twice a week?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the tutor is based along the same stretch of the Western corridor. Malad, Borivali, Kandivali and Goregaon sit close together on the Western Line and Metro Lines 2A and 7, so a 6pm or 7pm start from within that group is routine. What fails is a tutor coming across from the Central or Eastern Suburbs twice a week, because the east to west crossing at that hour is unpredictable. If you want two strand specialists, tell us, and we will try to source both from the same side of the Western Express Highway.

faqs.question: Which of the three sciences should we get help with first?
faqs.answer: Whichever one your child's papers show is weakest, which is often not the one they complain about most. Students name the subject they dislike; the papers name the subject costing marks. Chemistry is the most common answer in our experience because the calculation chain compounds, where a shaky start on moles makes concentration, reacting masses and titration all unreliable. Physics is next, usually because of relationship selection rather than concepts. Biology trails, because the content feels familiar even when the terminology is imprecise. Send the papers and let the marking decide rather than the preference.

faqs.question: Do we need one tutor for all three strands or separate specialists?
faqs.answer: One tutor if your child is broadly behind, specialists if the problem is specific. A single strong generalist gives continuity, one relationship and a coherent plan across three disciplines, which suits a student who needs the whole subject rebuilt. A strand specialist fixes a precise gap faster, and a real Chemistry teacher will do more for mole arithmetic in six weeks than a generalist will in a term. If you go with two, try to source both from the same belt so you are not coordinating two commutes into your building every week.

faqs.question: How are practical skills assessed if there is no coursework?
faqs.answer: Through the written papers. Questions ask students to describe a method, identify the variable that should have been controlled, interpret a results table, explain an anomalous reading or suggest an improvement to an experiment. So practical ability is examined as a writing skill, and students who performed the experiment in the school lab but were never asked to write about it lose these marks consistently. Ask your tutor to teach method questions explicitly rather than treating them as common sense, and check the current Pearson Edexcel specification for how practical skills are examined in your child's series.

faqs.question: What do IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on for Double Award?
faqs.answer: Board and level, how scarce the strand specialist is, travel distance and which belt, session length, and how many strands the engagement covers. We quote no figures because any number offered before seeing your child's papers is invented. The specific thing to compare here is scope: one tutor covering three strands at one rate is a different product from two specialists at two rates, and the cheaper total is not automatically the weaker option. Ask for the rate, the session length, the strands covered and the travel assumption as four separate items, then compare tutors on those four.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for science?
faqs.answer: It works well for Chemistry calculation and Biology terminology, and less well for Physics. The first two are question-and-answer disciplines that transfer to a shared screen cleanly. Physics teaching is spatial: a tutor needs to point at your child's own diagram, redraw the force arrows and watch the rearrangement happen. If you run one strand remotely, make it Chemistry or Biology. Online is also the right answer when the strand specialist you need does not exist within reach of your node, which happens with Physics in the outer suburbs more often than families expect.

faqs.question: Our science grade has not moved after a month. Should we change tutors?
faqs.answer: Not yet, but check two things. Open the notebook and look for stepped calculations with units, diagrams drawn by your child rather than copied, and underlined command words. Then ask the tutor which strand they are working on and what the evidence of movement is. Three strands hold a lot of content and a month of real work can produce a small mark change, which is normal. What is not normal is a tutor covering all three strands evenly with no stated priority. That produces a wasted term, and it is worth raising in week five.

faqs.question: How does a tutor replacement work?
faqs.answer: Tell us what specifically is not working and we handle the handover. For science the common reasons are a tutor teaching from the separate-science syllabus, a tutor who lectures rather than setting questions, or a strand mismatch that only became obvious once the harder topics arrived. Pass on the written plan from the first tutor so the replacement knows what was covered and does not spend a fortnight rediscovering it. Give us the real reason rather than a polite one, because the detail is what makes the second shortlist better than the first.

faqs.question: When in the Mumbai school year should we start?
faqs.answer: June or July if you have a choice, and September at the latest. The quiet window before unit tests is when a tutor can rebuild a concept at the level it is actually broken. Unit tests from August give you strand-level signal, and the first full mock in late October or November is where the three strands get examined together. Most families contact us in November, which is three months after the information was available. Ask the school for strand-level marks in September and you get to make a targeted decision instead of a rushed one.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home for science sessions?
faqs.answer: For the first session yes, after that it is optional. Being there at the start means you hear the strand diagnosis directly rather than through your child, and you can ask about the four-week plan while the tutor still has the papers in front of them. After that, most Year 10 and Year 11 students work better without a parent in the room, and a two-minute conversation at the end of the session is enough. What matters weekly is a table with room for a notebook and a calculator, decent light, and no television in earshot.

faqs.question: We live in Thane and the school is in Mulund. Where should sessions happen?
faqs.answer: At home in Thane, and the Ghodbunder Road position within Thane decides the timing. Thane has its own tutor pool, and Mulund tutors do sometimes cross the Eastern Express Highway for a good slot, so your options are wider than in most belts. If you are near the station or Majiwada, a weekday evening works. Out towards Kasarvadavali, that same trip takes most of an hour in the evening peak, and a Saturday or Sunday morning session will be both more reliable and more productive than a tired 8pm one on a weekday.

The join is where students lose ground, and it is rarely the content that causes it. This page covers what actually breaks at a transfer and what home tuition should do about it.

sections.heading: How does IB Gram match an Edexcel IGCSE tutor in Mumbai after a mid-course move?
paragraphs: A transfer request is handled differently from an ordinary one. For an Edexcel IGCSE tutor in Mumbai joining a student partway through the course, the first thing we collect is not the weak subject but the two course positions: where the old school had reached in each subject, and where the new school currently is. Those two points rarely coincide, and the distance between them is the actual job. Sending a tutor to work on the subject the parent is worried about, before that mapping exists, is how the first term gets wasted.

So the request we build asks for the previous school's term reports and topic lists, the new school's current scheme or term plan if the office will share it, and the entry details the receiving school is working from. A student arriving in Thane from Dubai, in Kharghar from Pune or in Goregaon East from another Mumbai school all present the same shape of problem in different accents, and all three are answered by the same documents before a home tutor is approached at all.

The shortlist is then built around people who have handled a join before. That is a specific skill and it is not the same as subject strength. A tutor who is excellent with a student who has been on one course throughout may teach beautifully forward from the wrong starting point. What we look for in a profile is somebody who will spend the first sessions finding out what the student actually holds, and who says so without being prompted during the matching call.

sections.heading: Tier and paper route: what the receiving school decides at a transfer
paragraphs: At IGCSE many subjects run on two entry routes, commonly described as Core and Extended or as Foundation and Higher, and which papers a candidate sits follows from the route they are entered for. How many papers a subject has, what each contains and how the components combine are set out in the specification for that subject and examination year, and those arrangements differ between subjects and can change between specification versions. A transferring family should read the specification the receiving school is using rather than carrying assumptions across from the previous one.

The decision itself belongs to the new school. A receiving school looks at the evidence it has, which on day one is a report from an institution it does not know, and makes a provisional judgement. That judgement is often sensible and it is always made on thin information. Families have standing to ask what it was based on, what evidence would cause it to be reviewed and when the entry deadline falls, because a route set provisionally in the first month has a habit of becoming permanent by default.

Timing decides how much room there is. A student joining at the start of Year 10 can generate a term of evidence before anything is fixed. A student joining in the second term of Year 11 is arriving after most of the decisions, and the realistic goal shifts from changing the route to performing well within it. Neither situation is a crisis, but they call for different plans, and a tutor who treats them identically has not understood what the family is dealing with.

sections.heading: Which coursework and practical marks travel with a transferring student?
paragraphs: This is the question families ask last and should ask first. Where a subject carries coursework, a practical component or any internally assessed element, work begun at a previous institution is subject to the arrangements the receiving school and the board operate, and those arrangements vary by subject, by specification and by the circumstances of the transfer. The only authority here is the receiving school's examinations officer. Ask them in writing, early, and get the answer in writing, because a verbal reassurance in September is worth very little in February.

The possibilities that families should be prepared for are straightforward enough to plan around. Some work may carry across with the appropriate paperwork. Some may need to be redone under the new school's supervision. Some practical arrangements may differ, and a student may find they are completing an element their previous class had already finished, or discovering one their previous class had not started. Each of those outcomes is manageable in October and difficult in March, which is why the chase belongs in the first fortnight.

Subject choice itself sometimes has to be revisited at a transfer. The new school may not offer a subject the student was taking, may offer separate sciences where the previous school ran a combined award, or may run a different combination at the Diploma Programme level that the student is aiming towards, with Higher Level and Standard Level choices and their internal assessments waiting at the far end. A tutor working across all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai is commonly asked for should flag those consequences while the timetable is still being set.

sections.heading: Edexcel IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai for families who have just moved
paragraphs: Relocations inside this city follow predictable routes, and an Edexcel IGCSE tutor in Mumbai gets matched against the new address rather than the old one. A great many moves end in Thane, where families spread west to east from the station across Pokhran Road and Majiwada and out along Ghodbunder Road to Kasarvadavali. The Ghodbunder stretch sets every schedule there: twenty minutes off-peak from the station, close to an hour in the evening, which is why Thane students are matched with Thane home tutors and only occasionally with somebody crossing from Mulund.

Navi Mumbai takes the next largest share. Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are planned as nodes linked by Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, and tutoring holds together when it is arranged node to node. The Trans-Harbour Line and the Atal Setu have widened what a Panvel or Kharghar family can consider, but a weekday evening crossing from the island city is still the arrangement most likely to quietly collapse in week four.

Elsewhere the pattern repeats with different roads. In the Eastern Suburbs, Mulund, Bhandup, Vikhroli and Chembur sit on the Central and Harbour lines with the Eastern Express Highway and the Eastern Freeway doing the long-distance work. In the Central Suburbs, Ghatkopar and Powai connect by Metro Line 1 and JVLR rather than by any single train route. In the Western Suburbs, Borivali, Kandivali East, Goregaon East and Dahisar East are served by the Western Line and Metro Lines 2A and 7. In South Mumbai, families around Parel, Worli and Colaba use the Coastal Road and the Bandra-Worli Sea Link, and are matched within the island.

paragraphs: Receiving schools across the city, among them Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane, D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul, NES International School in Mulund West, Thakur International School in Kandivali East, JBCN International School, Parel and Ryan Global School in Worli, each run their own admission and placement process. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Pearson Edexcel, with Cambridge International Education, or with any school named here, and it is not an approved or registered examination centre for either board.

A school will normally confirm the year group, the subject timetable, the specification it teaches and a provisional entry route, and it will say when reports and references from the previous institution have been received. What schools are much less likely to volunteer, because nobody asks, is the mapping detail: which topics this cohort has already covered in each subject, which coursework deadlines have passed, and what the examinations officer's position is on internally assessed work begun elsewhere. Those three things are the family's to chase.

The calendar then applies its own pressure regardless of when you arrived. Internal exams land before the holidays, department coursework deadlines are fixed in advance, and the Year 11 mock arrives in winter whether or not a transferring student has caught up. A family joining a Mumbai school in the second half of the year should assume the first mock will understate the student, and should treat it as diagnostic rather than as a verdict, while still reading carefully which question types it exposed.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid in the first Mumbai term after a move?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the right default in a transfer term and the reason is the paperwork. The first month's work is partly archaeology: old exercise books, the previous school's reports, half-finished coursework, a folder of handouts from an institution three time zones away. Spreading that across a table with a tutor is a different exercise from describing it over a call, and the family in the next room can answer the questions that arise. We arrange all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Mumbai with that first month in mind.

Online earns its place in two specific situations here. The first is the period between flats, when the family has moved schools but not yet moved homes, or is living out of boxes in a serviced flat in Powai or Vashi. The second is subject scarcity: an IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai who has taught the specification beats a nearby generalist who has not, and after a transfer the student has already absorbed enough disruption without adding a mismatched tutor to it.

Hybrid suits the shape of a transfer term better than most. A weekly home session to work through physical materials and marked scripts, plus a shorter online session for timed questions, gives the frequency the catch-up needs without asking a tutor to cross Ghodbunder Road twice a week. One condition applies as always: the same tutor runs both. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai who shares a transferring student with a second online tutor produces two incomplete maps of the same gap.

sections.heading: What should you ask a tutor before the first session after a transfer?
paragraphs: Three questions, asked before the first session rather than after it. What will you do in the first month. Which specification is the new school working from. And what will you ask me to collect from the old school. A tutor who answers the first question with a teaching plan has misread the job. The answer you want describes mapping: working through the student's previous material, finding what is held and what is missing, and producing something written at the end of it.

IB Gram checks identity, qualifications and teaching history, and asks which boards and specifications a tutor has prepared students for. For a transfer we also ask directly whether they have handled a mid-course join, and what they did in that first month. Anyone offering an edexcel IGCSE tutor in Mumbai arrangement that begins with next week's chapter is describing a standard engagement, not a transfer one. Families who ask for an IGCSE private tutor in Mumbai in these circumstances should make the distinction explicit at the outset.

Then verify the output rather than the person. At the end of the mapping month you should receive a document that says, subject by subject, which topics the student has covered securely, which were taught in a different order and may need resequencing, which were never covered, and which were covered but in a form the new school's assessments do not recognise. That document is checkable. A tutor's confidence is not, and the gap between the two is where transfer terms are lost.

sections.heading: Why your child's old notes are the most useful diagnostic document in the house
paragraphs: Everything else a transferring family holds is a summary written by somebody else. The report says the student was working at a certain standard. The topic list says what the old school intended to teach. The reference says she is conscientious. Only the student's own exercise books record what she actually did: which topics have ten pages and which have two, where the handwriting tightens up because she was copying rather than following, which worked examples were left half-finished, and which pages carry a teacher's correction that was never acted on.

That is diagnostic information no test produces as quickly. A placement test shows what a student can do today under pressure, with no indication of whether a weakness is a gap in teaching, a gap in attention or a topic that was covered thinly in a week when she was ill. The notebooks show the history. A tutor who spends ninety minutes with the previous two years of books, in order, can usually name the three topics to attack before the student has sat a single diagnostic question, and an edexcel IGCSE tutor in Mumbai handling a join should ask for them unprompted.

The notes also expose sequence differences, which are the quiet problem at any transfer. Two schools teaching the same specification may order the content quite differently, so a student can arrive having covered material the new class will not reach until next term, while missing a unit the new class finished in September. Nobody notices, because the student is quietly fine in lessons on the topics she already did and quietly lost on the one she missed, and the average looks acceptable until the mock separates them.

So the instruction to families is simple and slightly counterintuitive: do not throw anything away during the move. The old exercise books, the marked tests, the half-finished coursework draft and even the loose handouts in the back of the bag are the most valuable academic documents in the house for the next two months. Students almost always want to discard them, because they belong to the school they have just left. Box them, bring them, and put them on the table in session one.

sections.heading: The first month of a transfer: what a tutor should do instead of teaching forward
paragraphs: Week one is reading: the notes, the reports, the specification the new school uses and whatever the school has shared about where the cohort has reached. Week two tests the suspected gaps with short, targeted questions rather than a long paper, because a transferring student who is handed a full assessment in a new country in their second week learns mainly that they are behind. Weeks three and four begin closing the two or three gaps that matter most while the student keeps up with current class work on everything else.

What progress looks like is therefore different in a transfer term. At four weeks the deliverable is the coverage map, not a mark. At one term you should see the named gaps closed and the student's school marks beginning to reflect what they actually know rather than what they missed. At one examination cycle you have mocks, the final series and the entry decisions in between. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and in a transfer year it is particularly dishonest to suggest otherwise, because so much of the outcome depends on decisions the receiving school makes.

If the match is wrong, say so in week two. In a transfer the cost of waiting is higher than usual: a term spent teaching forward from an unverified starting point leaves the family with no map and less time than they started with. We take the report as information, re-match against the same written request with the new evidence added, and ask the outgoing tutor for whatever mapping they did complete so the next person does not start again from nothing.

And the boxes of old exercise books, which matter more than any of the paperwork and are the thing most likely to have been left behind in the move.

Then make the slot durable. Register the tutor at the gate as a recurring visitor, confirm the tower and wing in writing, and agree a study space with a table in it rather than a bed. Weekday home tuition works across most of the Eastern Suburbs and Thane if the tutor lives on the right side of Ghodbunder Road; weekend mornings hold better in Kharghar and Panvel. faqs.question: My son is joining a new school in Year 11. Where do we actually start?
faqs.answer: Start with coverage, not content. Get the new school to tell you what this cohort has already covered in each subject and which coursework deadlines have passed, and get the old school's topic lists if they exist. Then put your son's old exercise books in front of a tutor. In a Year 11 join the time available is short enough that guessing wrong about the starting point costs more than the gap itself. The mapping takes a few weeks and everything useful afterwards depends on it being done properly.

faqs.question: The new school has put my daughter on a different entry route. Can we question it?
faqs.answer: You can ask, and you should ask early. A receiving school sets a provisional route on whatever evidence it has, which on arrival is a report from an institution it does not know well. Ask what the judgement was based on, what evidence would cause it to be reviewed, and when the entry deadline falls. If there is a term available before that deadline, a focused block of work plus an internal assessment that reflects it is the kind of evidence schools respond to. After entries close the conversation changes shape entirely.

faqs.question: Coursework was started at the old school. Does it carry over?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject, the specification and the circumstances of the transfer, and the only person who can answer it for your child is the receiving school's examinations officer. Ask in writing in the first fortnight and keep the reply. Some work carries with the right paperwork, some has to be redone under the new school's supervision, and some components sit at a different point in the new school's sequence. All of those are manageable in October and painful in March, which is why the question belongs at the top of the list.

faqs.question: Does the old school's mark book transfer with the student?
faqs.answer: Generally not in any usable form. You will typically receive reports and a reference, which are summaries, rather than the running record of class tests, homework marks and teacher notes that the previous subject teachers were actually working from. This is why the student's own books matter so much: they are the closest thing to that record which the family still has. Collect any marked tests and assessments the student kept, including the ones that went badly, because those are the most informative pages in the pile.

faqs.question: We moved from another board mid-course. What changes in practice?
faqs.answer: In practice four things change and none of them is about which qualification is harder. The order topics are taught in differs, so coverage will be uneven rather than simply behind. The entry route and paper arrangements are set by the specification the new school uses, so read that one. Internally assessed and practical work may be at a different stage. And the running record of your child's performance does not come across. Work through those four with the new school and the picture becomes manageable fairly quickly.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor reach Kasarvadavali or Kharghar once we have moved?
faqs.answer: Yes, when the tutor is matched to the new address rather than inherited from the old one. In Thane, a tutor living on the Ghodbunder Road side reaches Kasarvadavali reliably while one near the station will struggle at 6pm. In Navi Mumbai, Kharghar is served well from Belapur, Nerul and Vashi along Palm Beach Road. Tell us the new address and the evening you want before we shortlist, because a home tuition slot that works on paper and not in traffic fails in week three.

faqs.question: We are between flats and the study space is chaotic. Does home tuition still work?
faqs.answer: It works if you are honest about the interim. For a few weeks in a serviced flat or with half the furniture in storage, run the sessions online and keep the physical materials in one labelled box, then switch to home sessions once there is a table and a door. What does not work is pretending the chaos is temporary for three months. Tell us the realistic date and we will plan the format around it rather than booking a home tutor into a room that will not exist until February.

faqs.question: Is online better for the first few weeks after a move?
faqs.answer: Only if the physical materials can still be seen. The first month of a transfer depends on old exercise books and marked work, so if sessions are online the student needs to be able to show pages on camera or scan them in advance, and somebody has to make sure the box is unpacked. Where the family is settled and the table exists, home tuition makes that month considerably easier. Where they are not yet settled, online keeps the work moving and the format can change later.

faqs.question: What do IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on in a transfer year?
faqs.answer: The same variables as any other year: board, level, how scarce the subject is, how far the tutor travels and how long each session runs. The difference in a transfer is that the first month often needs longer sessions or an extra one, because mapping takes time that teaching does not. IB Gram quotes against the written request rather than from a list. Ask what is included, how the mapping month is handled, and whether marking between sessions is part of the arrangement.

faqs.question: It has been a month since the move and nothing has improved. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: At one month after a transfer, improvement is the wrong measure. Ask for the coverage map instead: which topics are secure, which were taught in a different order, which were never covered. If that document exists and is specific, the work is on track even if no mark has moved. If it does not exist, or reads as general reassurance, tell us in week four and we will re-match. Marks usually begin to move in the term after the mapping, not during it.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram affiliated with Pearson Edexcel?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform, is not affiliated with Pearson Edexcel or Cambridge International Education, and is not an approved or registered examination centre for either board. Schools named on this page appear as local context, because their calendars and admission processes shape what transferring families have to plan around. We match and check tutors, we ask what they have actually prepared students for, and we do not guarantee grades in any year, transfer or otherwise.

faqs.question: My daughter says her old notes are useless now. Should we throw them out?
faqs.answer: No. Box them and keep them for at least the first two months. Students want to discard material from a school they have left, and it is the single most useful diagnostic resource the household owns. Ninety minutes with the previous two years of exercise books tells a tutor which topics were covered thinly, where corrections were never acted on and where the sequence differed from the new school's. Once the coverage map is written and the gaps are closed, keep the marked assessments and let the rest go.

edexcel-igcse-tutor.closingCta: Send us the new school, the year group, the subjects and the previous school's last two reports, and tell us when the move happened. We shortlist tutors who have handled a mid-course join and send two or three profiles. The first sessions map coverage instead of teaching forward, and a written map of secure topics, resequencing and real gaps follows within the month.

evening-ib-tutor.heroIntro: Most families looking for an evening IB tutor in Mumbai are not choosing a time slot. They are choosing what the household gives up. Home tuition after work means dinner moves, a younger child is told to keep it down, and a student awake since six sits back down anyway. This page helps you decide whether that session is worth it.

sections.heading: How IB Gram matches an evening IB tutor in Mumbai to your household
paragraphs: The message we usually get does not start with a subject. It starts with a time. A parent writes that they need an evening IB tutor in Mumbai, eight o'clock if possible, because eight is when the house is finally still. Before we send a single profile we ask a different question: who else is in that room at eight, and what has to move so the session can happen. A Diploma Programme (DP) student in Khar West whose father reaches home from Bandra Kurla Complex at twenty past eight is not sitting down to a quiet hour. She is sitting down while the front door opens, while a bag lands on a chair, while someone asks whether anyone has eaten.

So our intake has two halves. The first half is academic and obvious: board, year group, subjects, Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) choices, the last report, the paper that is losing marks. The second half is domestic, and it is the half families are surprised we ask about. What time does the family eat. How old is the younger sibling and where does that child do homework. Is there a door that closes, or is the dining table the only flat surface in the flat. Does a parent want to be within earshot of the lesson or deliberately out of it. Those answers decide whether a booking is still alive in February.

From there we shortlist inside your own corridor rather than across the city. A tutor who has fought the Western Express Highway from Goregaon East to Santacruz West arrives in no state to teach and leaves resenting the slot, and that resentment shows up four weeks later as a cancelled Tuesday. You then meet one or two tutors for a first paid session, with the actual worry on the table rather than a general introduction. You decide afterwards. If nobody fits, we go back and look again instead of talking you into the nearest available person.

Sometimes what we send back is not a shortlist at all. If the picture you describe is a child who leaves Thane at half past six in the morning and is not home until five, we will say so, and propose something that is not two late weekday sessions. Families rarely expect a tutoring platform to argue them out of a booking. We would rather have that conversation in July than lose the family in November when everyone has stopped enjoying it.
bullets: 1. Send the subject, year group, school and the last report comment
2. Tell us the household: dinner time, siblings, which room, who is home
3. We shortlist tutors inside your corridor, not across the city
4. You meet one or two for a first paid session, then decide
5. We review the slot at four weeks and move it if it is not holding

sections.heading: Which year groups an evening slot actually suits
paragraphs: Age changes the answer more than subject does. A Primary Years Programme (PYP) child at eight in the evening is being asked to do something developmentally unreasonable, and no amount of good teaching fixes it. Middle Years Programme (MYP) students in Years 7 and 8 sit in the middle: a short late session is survivable once a week, twice is usually too much. From MYP Year 9 upward, and across Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE, students are genuinely capable of useful work after dinner, provided the work is the right kind. DP1 and DP2 students often prefer it, because that is when their own day finally belongs to them.

The International Baccalaureate (IB) structure matters here too. A DP student is carrying six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and Creativity, Activity, Service, and the evening is already the only unallocated time they have. Adding a tutor to it is not adding a free hour, it is competing with the hour they were going to use for the Internal Assessment (IA) draft. That is a real trade and worth naming out loud before you book, rather than discovering it when the IA is late.

For IGCSE families the calculation is different again. Years 9 and 10 have room; Year 11 does not. A Year 11 student at an IGCSE school in Juhu or Chembur is already carrying coursework deadlines, and an evening booking that sits on top of them without replacing anything becomes the thing that gets dropped first. If you are adding an evening session in Year 11, something else in the week should come off. We will ask you what.
None of this is an argument against evenings. It is an argument for matching the hour to the year group honestly, which is a conversation most families have never been offered.
bullets: PYP and early MYP: evenings rarely work, mornings or weekends are better
MYP Years 9 and 10: one late session a week is usually sustainable
IGCSE Years 9 and 10 have room in the week; Year 11 generally does not
DP1 and DP2 students often work better late than early, if rested
Adding an evening slot should replace something, not simply sit on top

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL, and which work survives a late hour
paragraphs: Some academic work is genuinely fine at eight in the evening and some is not, and the difference is not difficulty. It is how much original thinking the task demands from a brain that has been running since six in the morning. Drilling Mathematics Analysis and Approaches questions from a past paper, consolidating a vocabulary list for Spanish ab initio, tidying the data table and uncertainty column of a Physics IA, checking that a Business Management case response has actually used the command term asked for: all of this holds up late. A tutor can carry the structure while the student supplies the effort.

What does not hold up late is first exposure. Meeting HL Chemistry organic mechanisms for the first time at that hour wastes the session and, worse, teaches the student that the topic is incomprehensible. Nor does genuinely generative work. Building the argument of a TOK essay, deciding what an EE research question is really asking, choosing between Core and Extended entry for IGCSE Mathematics: these need a rested student and a morning. If the only hour you have is late, spend it on consolidation and move the thinking work elsewhere.

Subject choice across both boards is its own conversation and it is one we are happy to have in an evening session, because it is discussion rather than production. A Year 11 student weighing whether to take Economics HL or Geography HL in DP1, a family deciding whether Extended Mathematics is the right risk at IGCSE, a DP1 student wondering whether to drop from HL to SL before the deadline: those talks go well late, and they often matter more to the final result than another hour of practice questions.

When we brief a tutor for an evening booking we tell them which category the work falls into. A tutor who plans a late session as if it were a Saturday morning session is planning a session the student will fail to deliver, and then both of them feel bad about it.
bullets: Good late: past-paper drilling, command-term checking, IA data and tables
Good late: vocabulary, definitions, recall, worked examples with the method visible
Poor late: first teaching of a new HL topic the student has never seen
Poor late: TOK essay argument, EE research question, anything genuinely generative
Good late: subject choice and HL, SL, Core and Extended decisions, because they are discussion

sections.heading: Evening home tuition across all six Mumbai zones
paragraphs: Evening home tuition works zone by zone in Mumbai, Maharashtra, because the evening is precisely when crossing a zone stops being realistic. In South Mumbai we match inside the island. A tutor living near Walkeshwar or Tardeo takes a Cuffe Parade, Colaba, Fort or Parel booking, and the Coastal Road has changed the Worli run more than anything else in the last few years, while the Peddar Road signals remain what they always were. Metro Line 3 helps a tutor coming down from Bandra Kurla Complex on the Aqua line, though the walk at either end still costs real minutes.

In the Western Suburbs we match along the Western Line rather than across it. Khar West to Santacruz West is a short hop; Juhu to Kandivali at seven in the evening is not a plan, it is a hope. Metro Lines 2A and 7 have made the Dahisar to Andheri run predictable in a way the Western Express Highway never was, which matters enormously when a family in Borivali or Malad wants a fixed weekday evening rather than a floating one. The Bandra-Worli Sea Link only helps the tutor travelling south, and only before the peak.

In the Central Suburbs, Powai and Chandivali have no station of their own, so a tutor reaches Hiranandani Gardens by road from Andheri East over JVLR, or from Ghatkopar and Kanjurmarg on the Central Line and Metro Line 1. That single road is the entire scheduling problem for Powai home classes, and it is why we match Powai from Powai wherever we can. The Santacruz-Chembur Link Road makes Kurla and Chembur reachable from the western side, but not reliably at half past seven.

The Eastern Suburbs run from Chembur and Govandi through Vikhroli and Bhandup to Mulund West on the Central and Harbour lines, and the Eastern Freeway puts Wadala and Chembur closer to South Mumbai than the map suggests. Navi Mumbai is node to node: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar, Panvel and Airoli, along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway. The Atal Setu has shortened the crossing from the island, but we still do not build a weekday evening around it. Thane follows its own logic, with Pokhran Road, Majiwada and the long Ghodbunder Road stretch out to Kasarvadavali, where a tutor leaving at six and a tutor leaving at seven are nearly forty minutes apart.

sections.heading: Does your child have anything left after a Mumbai school day?
paragraphs: Often, no. A student at an international school in Mumbai is typically out of the house between seven and half past seven, in class until mid-afternoon, and then in a bus or a car for another forty to seventy minutes depending on where the school sits relative to home. By the time a Dhirubhai Ambani International School or American School of Bombay student living in the Western Suburbs is back, the useful part of the day is behind them. That is the fact an evening booking has to work around, not the one it should pretend does not exist.

Layer the school calendar on top of it. The IB Diploma year has its own pressure points, and they are not spread evenly. The October to November window in DP2 stacks EE deadlines against early IA drafts. January and February bring mock examinations at most Mumbai schools, which is also when the TOK essay is being finalised. March and April are the final internal deadlines before May session examinations. For IGCSE cohorts at schools such as Bombay International School, Cathedral and John Connon School, Hiranandani Foundation School or Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane, coursework and mock windows land in a similar rhythm.

Schools also fill the evening themselves. A Model United Nations weekend, a production rehearsal at Ecole Mondiale World School, a sports fixture, a Creativity Activity Service commitment: these are not optional extras the family can simply cancel, and they routinely collide with a fixed weekday evening. When a family tells us their child has three fixed commitments after school already, we take that seriously rather than treating it as a scheduling detail.

The honest conclusion is that a Mumbai school day plus travel plus activities is already a full working day for an adult. An evening tutor is being added to the end of it. That can be worth doing. It is not free.
bullets: School bus or car adds forty to seventy minutes at each end for many families
DP2 pressure stacks in October and November, then again in January mocks
IGCSE coursework and mock windows follow a similar January to March rhythm
Rehearsals, fixtures and service commitments collide with fixed weekday evenings

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid when the clock has already reached eight
paragraphs: Home tuition is what most families want from an evening IB tutor in Mumbai, and for good reason. The student does not travel, the materials are already on the desk, a parent can see what is happening without sitting in the room, and the tutor can tell in thirty seconds whether tonight is a working night. The cost is to the household. Someone has to be awake and dressed, the living room is occupied, and the tutor's arrival time is hostage to the same traffic everyone else is sitting in. An IB home tutor in Mumbai who is regularly fifteen minutes late is not unreliable, they are commuting at the worst hour of the day.

Online is the honest alternative and it is better at night than people expect. There is no arrival, so the session starts when it says it will, and a tutor in a different suburb or a different city is suddenly available to you. A student can take an IB online tutor in Mumbai from their own room with the door shut, which solves the sibling problem outright. The trade is attention. A tired student on a screen can look present while doing very little, and a tutor who cannot see the page in front of them is working blind unless the student shares it deliberately.

Hybrid is what we most often end up recommending for late slots. Home tuition once a week, usually on the less loaded evening, with the second contact online and shorter. The in-person session sets the direction and checks the written work properly; the online one holds the student to it. This also stops the household from absorbing two full evening disruptions a week, which is the thing that quietly ends most bookings.

Whatever the mode, IB home tuition in Mumbai should be chosen around the week you actually have. Parents ask us who the best IB tutor in Mumbai is, and the honest answer is that there is no such person, only the tutor whose subject, method and schedule fit this student in this flat at this hour.
bullets: Home: no travel for the student, visible work, but the household absorbs the evening
Online: punctual, wider choice of tutor, solves the shared-room problem
Online risk: a tired student can look engaged while producing nothing
Hybrid: one home session plus one shorter online session is the usual late-slot answer

sections.heading: How we check an IB home tutor in Mumbai before they ring your bell
paragraphs: Every tutor on the platform is identity-checked against government photo identification, and their degree and teaching claims are verified against documents rather than taken from a profile. Beyond that, we check the thing that actually matters: whether they have taught this specific syllabus recently. An IB private tutor Mumbai parents are happy with in DP Economics is not automatically the right person for MYP Mathematics, and a tutor who last taught the IGCSE Biology syllabus several specification cycles ago will be teaching content that has moved. We ask for the syllabus, the recent cohort and the papers they have marked or prepared students for.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Cathedral and John Connon School, Hiranandani Foundation School, Ecole Mondiale World School, the International Baccalaureate organisation, Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Schools are named on this page as local context, because their calendars shape when Mumbai families feel pressure, and for no other reason. No tutor on the platform represents a school, and none should imply otherwise.

There is a second layer of checking that only you can do, and for an evening booking it matters more than usual. Watch the first session. Does the tutor arrive settled or flustered. Do they ask your child what they did in school today before opening a book, which tells you whether they are reading the student's state. Do they finish on time, or do they drift past the end because the work is unfinished, which is how a reasonable hour becomes an unreasonable one. Ask them directly what they will do on a night when your child has nothing left.

Check the practical things too. Confirm how the tutor will be cleared at your society gate for a standing weekly slot, because a tutor arguing with security at five past eight has already lost part of the session. Agree what happens when traffic makes them late, and whether a shortened session is made up or simply shortened.
bullets: Government photo identification and document-checked qualifications before any match
Recent experience of the exact syllabus, not the subject in general
Ask the tutor what they do when the student arrives with nothing left
Agree society gate clearance for a standing slot before week one
Agree in advance how a late arrival is handled and whether time is made up

sections.heading: Should this evening session happen at all?
paragraphs: Here is the test we give families, and it takes one week to run. Sit near enough to hear the first ten minutes of three consecutive sessions. In a productive late session the student talks. They ask something, they object to something, they say they do not understand a step. There is a pen moving. In a session everybody is enduring, the tutor talks and the student agrees. Nothing is written except what is copied. The student's answers get shorter as the hour goes on, and at the end they say it was fine. A student who says the session was fine three weeks running and cannot name one thing they learned is not learning; they are being polite in their own home.

There are other tells. Watch what happens on the one evening the tutor cancels. If the reaction in the house is relief rather than inconvenience, that is information. Watch whether your child starts negotiating the start time later and later, or discovers urgent homework at ten to eight. Watch yourself as well: if you have started dreading the doorbell, or if dinner has quietly become something eaten in shifts, the booking is costing the household more than it is returning. None of this means the tutor is bad. An evening IB tutor in Mumbai cannot rescue an hour that was already spent before they arrived. It usually means the hour is wrong, not the person.

Most families have never been shown the alternatives, so here they are. Some students, particularly early risers who are hopeless after six, do far better with a session before school; it is unusual and it requires a tutor who lives genuinely close, but when it fits it fits completely. A second option is to replace two tired weekday sessions with one longer one when the student is rested, which also halves the disruption to the household. A third is the opposite move: shorter, more frequent contact. Three short sessions hold a weak topic better than one long one, and a short session is far easier for an exhausted student to agree to and to finish well.

A tutor should also know what to do when the student has nothing left, and the right answer is not to push through. It is to switch the session to something low-demand and still useful: sorting the next fortnight's deadlines into an order, marking a paper the student already wrote, reading a mark scheme together, listing the three questions to ask the subject teacher tomorrow. If a tutor cannot do that, or treats a short session as a failure, they are the wrong tutor for an evening slot. And if that is happening most weeks rather than occasionally, the slot itself is wrong. A session nobody in the house wants does not survive the year. It survives until roughly November, and then it ends badly, with the student convinced that tutoring does not work for them. It is far better to move it in August than to abandon it in November.
bullets: Productive late: the student asks questions, objects, writes unprompted
Enduring: the tutor talks, the student agrees, nothing is written
Relief when a session is cancelled is the clearest signal there is
Alternatives: before school, one longer rested session, or shorter and more often
A good tutor downshifts to planning or marking when the student is spent
Move a failing slot in August rather than abandoning tutoring in November

sections.heading: What does progress look like when the lessons are late ones?
paragraphs: Slower than in a morning slot, and you should plan for that rather than be disappointed by it. At four weeks, expect process rather than marks: the student knows what the tutor is going to ask, homework between sessions is actually being attempted, and one specific weakness has been named. If at four weeks nobody can tell you what is being worked on, that is a problem with the match and we will change it. At one term you should see a measurable shift in a defined area, usually the paper or the criterion you flagged at the start. At one full examination cycle you can judge properly, because the student has sat something under conditions and you can compare like with like.

We do not guarantee grades, and anyone in this market who does is making a promise they cannot keep. Grades depend on the student's work between sessions, on what school teaching has or has not covered, on the particular paper that comes up, and on the student's state on the day. What a good tutor controls is preparation, honest feedback and the removal of specific recurring errors. That is a lot, and it is not the same as a guaranteed outcome.

On what you will pay: IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on board and level, with DP HL and the harder IGCSE Extended papers sitting above MYP work. They depend on subject scarcity, because a tutor who genuinely teaches HL Further Mathematics or a less common Group 2 language is rarer than a Mathematics or Business Management tutor. They depend on travel distance and the hour, since a tutor crossing a zone in the evening peak is giving up two hours of their day for one hour of teaching. They depend on session length and frequency. We will not quote a figure here that pretends those variables do not exist.

The household cost is real too and worth counting honestly before you commit. Two evening sessions a week is roughly a quarter of your family's weekday evenings given over to this. If the academic return does not justify that, the right decision is fewer sessions, not a cheaper tutor.
bullets: Four weeks: a named weakness, attempted homework, a tutor who can describe the plan
One term: measurable movement in the specific paper or criterion you flagged
One exam cycle: the first fair comparison, because conditions were the same
Fees track board, level, subject scarcity, travel distance, session length and frequency
Evening peak travel raises cost because the tutor loses two hours for one

sections.heading: Booking an evening IB tutor in Mumbai without wrecking your week
paragraphs: Before you write to us, spend ten minutes on three things. Write down the actual week: school finish, travel time home, fixed commitments, dinner, and the hour your child currently goes to bed. Write down what the last report or mock said, in the teacher's words rather than your summary of them. And decide where the session will physically happen, because the dining table with a sibling nearby and a bedroom with a door are different bookings. Families searching for IB tutors near me in Mumbai often skip this and then wonder why the third tutor has not worked either.

The first session should do four things. It should establish what the student can already do, not what the report says they cannot. It should identify one specific recurring error, which in practice is usually a command term being misread, a method step being skipped, or working not being shown. It should set a piece of work for before the next session that takes under thirty minutes. And it should end on time, so the household learns that this booking has edges.

After that first session we ask you one question and the tutor another. We ask you whether your child talked. We ask the tutor what state the student was in and whether the hour is right. If those two answers disagree, we would rather change the slot in week one than discover the mismatch in the middle of mock season. We can arrange all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Mumbai families need across both boards, but the arranging is the easy part. Getting the hour right is the part that decides whether this is still running at the end of the year.
bullets: Write out the real week before you ask for a slot, including bedtime
Bring the report or mock in the teacher's words, not your paraphrase
Decide the room: a door that closes changes what is possible
Expect the first session to end on time, deliberately
Tell us after week one whether your child actually talked

faqs.question: Is eight in the evening too late for a useful session?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, but it depends entirely on the student and the work. A rested DP2 student doing past-paper practice at eight is often sharper than the same student at four, because the school day is behind them and nothing else is competing. A Year 9 student who left home at half past six that morning is a different case, and asking them to meet new Higher Level content at that hour wastes everybody's time. The test is not the clock, it is whether the student is talking, writing and asking questions in the first ten minutes. If they are, the hour is fine. If they are nodding, it is not.

faqs.question: My husband walks in at half past eight while the session is running. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: It matters more than most families expect, and it is fixable. An arriving parent changes the room: the front door, the bag, the conversation about dinner, the younger child running out to say hello. A student who was concentrating is pulled out of it, and a tutor who is mid-explanation has to restart. The usual fixes are simple. Shift the session to a room with a door, start it earlier so the last twenty minutes are the lighter ones, or move it to the evening your spouse is home earlier. We would rather you tell us the arrival time up front than have the tutor work around it silently for a month.

faqs.question: Could the tutor come before school instead?
faqs.answer: For some students, yes, and it is the most under-used option in Mumbai. An early-rising student who is useless after dinner can do genuinely good work between half past six and half past seven, particularly recall, past-paper questions and anything that benefits from a fresh brain. The constraints are real: the tutor has to live very close, because nobody is crossing the Western Express Highway at that hour for one session, and the school bus time caps the length absolutely. It suits students in Powai, Thane and Navi Mumbai nodes where tutor and family are often in the same pocket. It rarely suits a family whose child already leaves at six.

faqs.question: What does an evening IB tutor in Mumbai cost?
faqs.answer: It depends on five things and we will not invent a number for you. Board and level come first, since DP Higher Level work and IGCSE Extended papers sit above Middle Years Programme work. Subject scarcity comes second: a tutor who genuinely teaches HL Further Mathematics or a less common language is harder to find than a Mathematics tutor. Travel distance and the hour come third, because an evening crossing costs the tutor two hours for one. Session length and frequency come fourth and fifth. An evening IB tutor in Mumbai making a long peak-hour journey will sit above the same tutor's daytime rate, which is one more reason to match inside your own corridor.

faqs.question: Our tutor has to come up Ghodbunder Road to reach Kasarvadavali. Will they be late every week?
faqs.answer: Probably once or twice a month, and the fix is in the booking rather than the tutor. The Ghodbunder stretch from Thane station out to Kasarvadavali runs roughly twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour at the worst of the evening, so a tutor leaving at six and a tutor leaving at seven are living in different cities. We match Thane families with tutors already living along Pokhran Road, Majiwada or the Ghodbunder corridor rather than sending someone from Mulund across the Eastern Express Highway. Agree before week one what happens to a late arrival: made up at the end, made up next session, or simply absorbed.

faqs.question: Our building in Powai requires a gate pass for every visitor after seven. How does that work?
faqs.answer: Set it up once as a standing entry and you never think about it again. Most Hiranandani Gardens and Chandivali societies will register a recurring visitor for a fixed weekly slot if the resident files it with the society office, which converts a nightly argument at the gate into a name on a list. Do this in the first week, not the third. We give you the tutor's full name and identification details for the form, and we ask the tutor to arrive a few minutes early for the first two visits while the process settles. A tutor still negotiating with security at ten past eight has already lost a quarter of the session.

faqs.question: My younger child cannot stay quiet for an hour and a half. What do other families do?
faqs.answer: Three things, in order of how well they work. First, give the session a door rather than the dining table, even if that means the tutor sits in a bedroom; the younger child does not then have to perform silence in a room they can see into. Second, pair the slot with something the younger child actively wants to be doing elsewhere, rather than a prohibition. Third, and most effective, shorten the session. A focused shorter session that the whole household can tolerate beats a long one that two people are resenting. Telling a six-year-old to be silent twice a week is a plan that fails by October.

faqs.question: Is online better than a home tutor for a late slot?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and for specific reasons. Online removes the arrival, which means the session starts on time and the household is not opening the door at eight. It also lets a student with a sibling in the room simply close their own door. The trade is that a tired student on a screen can appear attentive while doing nothing, and the tutor cannot see the page unless the student shares it. If you go online for a late slot, insist the student works on a shared document or holds their written work to the camera. Many Mumbai families settle on one home session a week plus one shorter online session.

faqs.question: It has been four weeks and I cannot see any change. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Ask three specific questions before you change anything. Ask the tutor to name the one error they are working on; if they cannot, that is your answer. Ask your child what they did in the last session; a blank is a different problem from a vague answer. Ask whether work set between sessions is being done, because a tutor cannot outrun a student who does nothing in between. Four weeks is too early for a grade shift and about right for process to be visible. If process is not visible either, tell us and we will change the tutor. You should not have to manage that conversation yourself.

faqs.question: The tutor seems good but my daughter dreads Tuesdays. Do we change the tutor or the day?
faqs.answer: Change the day first, almost always. Dread attached to a specific evening is usually about the shape of that day rather than the person teaching. Find out what else sits on Tuesday: a long school commitment, a fixture, a late bus, a subject she has back to back. Move the session to the emptiest evening in the week and watch for a fortnight. If the dread moves with the tutor rather than staying with the day, then it is the match, and we will replace the tutor without you starting the explanation from scratch. We keep the subject brief, the history and the named weakness, so the new tutor begins where the last one stopped.

faqs.question: Which parts of Mumbai do you actually cover in the evening?
faqs.answer: All six zones, but matched within them rather than across them. We place a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families ask for in South Mumbai from Colaba to Parel, across the Western Suburbs from Bandra to Dahisar, in the Central Suburbs including Powai, Chandivali, Ghatkopar and Mulund, through the Eastern Suburbs from Wadala and Chembur to Bhandup, across the Navi Mumbai nodes of Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel, and throughout Thane. What we will not do for a weekday evening is send a tutor across the creek on the Atal Setu or down the Sea Link, because that booking does not last a term.

evening-ib-tutor.closingCta: Send us the week rather than just the subject: what time school ends, how long the journey home takes, when the family eats, who else is in the flat and what is already fixed in the diary. We will come back with two or three tutors who live close enough to arrive settled, or with an honest suggestion that a different hour would serve your child better. You meet a tutor, decide after that session, and we review the slot at four weeks.
